Duskull itself is considerably less forgiving before level 37, and reaching Dusknoir may require both a Reaper Cloth and a trade, so some runs will realistically use Dusclops as the final obtainable stage. That is not necessarily a problem from Generation V onward: Eviolite Dusclops becomes extraordinarily difficult to break with neutral attacks and can often survive situations that would threaten Dusknoir. The family's low HP and poor Speed still matter, and Dark or Ghost attacks target its only ordinary type weaknesses; repeated status, critical hits, or Knock Off removing Eviolite can also undermine an apparently safe defensive plan. Dusknoir offers more immediate damage and item freedom, while Dusclops usually provides the greater raw defensive margin, making the choice unusually dependent on what kind of safety the run needs.

pokemon.name: Duskull
pokemon.biologyAndBehavior: Duskull is a nocturnal spectral predator capable of becoming invisible, passing directly through walls, and pursuing a chosen target relentlessly until dawn. Its single red eye floats freely between the sockets of its skull-like mask, reinforcing the impression that the visible body is more supernatural than anatomical. Folklore claims that Duskull spirits away children who misbehave, a story deliberately told by adults to frighten children into obedience, but the species is also explicitly described as feeding on children's vital energy. Victims drained by Duskull experience an intense chill afterward, suggesting that the Pokemon feeds by removing life force rather than ordinary physical food. It inhabits dark forests and mountainous areas and becomes active primarily at night, when invisibility and the ability to move through walls make escape from a pursuing Duskull extremely difficult.
pokemon.description: Duskull is a Ghost-type Pokémon introduced in Generation III and the first stage of its evolution line, with a base stat total of 295.

pokemon.name: Dusclops
pokemon.biologyAndBehavior: Dusclops is a hollow, bandage-wrapped Ghost whose empty body behaves like a black hole: anything drawn through the gaps in its wrappings disappears inside and has never been observed emerging again. The single red eye is sometimes said to be the Pokemon's true form, although no one has successfully confirmed what actually exists beneath the wrappings. Dusclops can wave its hands and move its eye in hypnotic patterns that place opponents under its control, forcing victims to act according to its wishes. Its natural prey includes drifting will-o'-the-wisps, which it pulls directly into the hollow body and consumes. The combination of a physically empty interior, unexplained absorption, and hypnotic control makes Dusclops less like an ordinary organism than a mobile supernatural void concealed inside a vaguely humanoid shell.
pokemon.description: Dusclops is a Ghost-type Pokémon introduced in Generation III and a middle stage of its evolution line, with a base stat total of 455.

pokemon.name: Dusknoir
pokemon.biologyAndBehavior: Dusknoir acts as a supernatural intermediary between the living world and the spirit world, using the antenna on its head to receive mysterious transmissions instructing it which spirits or beings to collect. It is widely feared because those transmissions can command it to take people away, and rare accounts suggest that living people may sometimes be carried off by mistake; whether Dusknoir has free will or is compelled to obey the signals remains unknown. The band across its abdomen opens into a large mouth capable of swallowing a target whole, but Dusknoir is specifically said to consume only spectral essence or souls and leave the physical body behind. Other accounts describe a more benevolent role in which it takes lost spirits into its pliant body and guides them to the place they belong, making the same behavior appear either terrifying or compassionate depending on the victim. Dusknoir therefore occupies an unusually ambiguous ecological role: it is not simply a predator of the living, but something closer to a psychopomp whose body transports souls between worlds according to signals no one fully understands.
pokemon.description: Dusknoir is a Ghost-type Pokémon introduced in Generation IV and a final stage of its evolution line, with a base stat total of 525.

playthrough: Tropius is a single-stage Grass/Flying Pokemon built more around bulk, recovery, and utility than immediate offensive power. Its base 99 HP, 83 Defense, and 87 Special Defense are respectable, while a Ground immunity and resistances to Water, Fighting, and Grass create useful switch opportunities; however, base 68 Attack, 72 Special Attack, and 51 Speed make straightforward sweeping difficult. In Generation III, Grass attacks are special and Flying attacks are physical, so its two STAB types naturally split across its similarly modest offensive stats, while Earthquake, Leech Seed, Synthesis, and status or coverage can give it several practical roles. Chlorophyll doubles Tropius's Speed in harsh sunlight, Solar Power can strengthen its special offense in sun at the cost of HP, and the later Hidden Ability Harvest can repeatedly restore consumed Berries and support unusually durable defensive strategies. The defining danger is a quadruple Ice weakness, joined by Fire, Flying, Poison, and Rock weaknesses, so Tropius is much safer when exploiting known resistances and recovery than when attempting to tank arbitrary coverage.
competitive: Tropius has spent most of its competitive history in the lowest tiers because its respectable bulk and useful movepool are undermined by low offensive stats, very poor Speed, and a difficult defensive typing. In ADV lower-tier play it can operate as a physically defensive wall using Leech Seed and Synthesis, while Hidden Power Flying and Earthquake prevent it from being completely passive and Chlorophyll offers a separate sun-based offensive route. Later generations gave Tropius Harvest, creating its most distinctive long-term defensive niche: under favorable conditions it can repeatedly recycle Berries for healing or status recovery while combining Substitute, Protect, Leech Seed, or other stalling tools. Solar Power and Chlorophyll also preserve specialized sun roles, but stronger Grass-types generally offer better offenses, speed, typing, or utility without carrying Tropius's severe quadruple Ice weakness. Its competitive identity is therefore that of an inventive lower-tier wall and weather specialist rather than a conventional high-level threat.
nuzlocke: Tropius can be a useful Nuzlocke Pokemon because it arrives fully evolved and combines good HP with recovery, a Ground immunity, and useful resistances to Water, Fighting, and Grass. Leech Seed and Synthesis can reduce item consumption and allow Tropius to win favorable battles gradually, while Harvest can become excellent long-term insurance when a suitable Berry and the relevant ability are available. Its low Speed means it frequently takes a hit before acting, however, so even respectable defenses do not make blind switching especially safe. Ice coverage is the major threat because it deals quadruple damage, and Rock, Fire, Flying, and Poison attacks can also punish what otherwise looks like a bulky matchup. Tropius is safest as a sustain-oriented specialist used against opponents whose coverage is known, rather than as a universal defensive answer.

pokemon.name: Tropius
pokemon.biologyAndBehavior: Tropius is a huge tropical herbivore whose broad leaf-like wings serve two purposes: they generate lift for surprisingly maneuverable flight and produce sugar through photosynthesis. Its long neck lets it browse fruit high in jungle canopies, and generations of continuously eating one especially favored fruit are said to have caused edible banana-like fruit to begin growing around Tropius's own neck. Those fruits can be eaten by both people and Pokemon and grow twice each year because the large leaves manufacture sugar so quickly; in Alola, the fruit is said to be especially sweet. Humans in warm regions raise Tropius on ranches specifically for this produce, making it one of the clearer examples of a Pokemon species integrated into agriculture as a renewable food source. During spring it also scatters pollen from its neck, tying its reproductive-season behavior to the same plantlike anatomy that supplies flight, food production, and photosynthetic energy.
pokemon.description: Tropius is a Grass/Flying-type Pokémon introduced in Generation III, with a base stat total of 460 and no standard evolutions.

playthrough: The Chimecho family is unusual historically because Chimecho debuted alone in Generation III and the baby stage Chingling was added in Generation IV; Chingling evolves into Chimecho when leveled with high friendship during the night. Standard Chimecho is a pure Psychic special attacker and support Pokemon with Levitate, giving it a valuable Ground immunity while Psychic STAB, Calm Mind, screens, Heal Bell, Yawn, Recover in later movepools, and broad support options allow it to contribute without overwhelming raw power. Its stats were improved beginning in Generation VII to 75 HP, 80 Defense, 95 Special Attack, 90 Special Defense, and 65 Speed, making modern Chimecho appreciably sturdier than the original Hoenn version while retaining the same general role. Mega Chimecho, introduced in the Mega Dimension DLC for Pokemon Legends: Z-A, becomes Psychic/Steel and jumps to 110 Defense, 135 Special Attack, and 120 Special Defense; in ability-enabled formats it retains Levitate, creating an especially strong defensive profile with a Ground immunity despite Steel's normal Ground weakness. The family's main practical drawbacks are Chingling's friendship-and-night evolution requirement, Chimecho's middling Speed, and weaknesses to Ghost and Dark attacks, with Mega Chimecho also needing to respect Fire.
competitive: Chimecho had a legitimate niche in ADV NU, where Levitate, Psychic typing, useful special bulk, and a deep support movepool made it one of the tier's more flexible Psychic-types rather than a simple novelty. Calm Mind sets could threaten to sweep or pressure defensive teams, while Heal Bell, Yawn, Toxic, Reflect, Light Screen, and other utility allowed Chimecho to support teammates and exploit its Ground immunity and Fighting resistance. Power creep gradually pushed standard Chimecho toward lower relevance despite later stat buffs, since its base 65 Speed and merely good base 95 Special Attack are difficult to distinguish from stronger modern Psychic-types. Mega Chimecho substantially changes that equation with Psychic/Steel typing and base 135 Special Attack backed by 110 Defense and 120 Special Defense, giving it much greater offensive and defensive presence; official current data also lists Levitate, preserving a Ground immunity in ability-based formats. Because Mega Chimecho is a 2025 addition rather than a form with decades of established singles history, its long-term tier legacy is still developing, but its raw profile clearly shifts the species from niche support toward a slow, powerful, unusually resilient special attacker.
nuzlocke: Chingling is a somewhat awkward Nuzlocke investment because it must reach high friendship and then level at night before gaining Chimecho's significantly better stats, making the timing of evolution dependent on both care and the game's clock. Once evolved, Levitate supplies a complete Ground immunity and Chimecho's respectable special bulk, Psychic offense, screens, status, and healing or cleric tools can create safe utility against predictable opponents. Bug, Ghost, and Dark attacks are the main dangers for ordinary Chimecho, and its modest physical Defense means strong neutral physical moves also deserve respect. Mega Chimecho is dramatically safer where available: Psychic/Steel provides numerous resistances, its defenses rise to 110/120, and Levitate removes the Ground weakness in formats that use abilities, leaving Fire, Ghost, and Dark as the most important conventional threats. The line therefore changes from a fragile friendship project into a useful support Pokemon, and in its newest Mega form into a much more forgiving defensive-special attacker.

pokemon.name: Chingling
pokemon.biologyAndBehavior: Chingling is a living bell whose mouth contains a red orb that strikes the surrounding cavity as the Pokemon moves, producing its characteristic ringing sound with every gentle bounce. It can deliberately vibrate that orb to produce cries at frequencies too high for humans to hear directly, yet the resulting sound can still cause severe headaches and disorient or deafen opponents. The high-frequency cry can continue for an unusually long time, making a tiny, physically unimposing Pokemon surprisingly effective at defending itself through sound alone. Its locomotion and vocalization are inseparable: even ordinary hopping sets the internal orb ringing, so Chingling's body functions continuously as a biological musical instrument.
pokemon.description: Chingling is a Psychic-type Pokémon introduced in Generation IV and the first stage of its evolution line, with a base stat total of 285.

pokemon.name: Chimecho
pokemon.biologyAndBehavior: Chimecho has a hollow wind-chime-like body that amplifies even faint air currents into powerful vibrations, allowing it to produce ultrasonic waves capable of startling opponents or knocking much larger prey unconscious. It possesses seven distinct echoing cries used to communicate with others of its species, making vocal variation an important part of its social behavior rather than merely a battle technique. A suction cup on top of the body allows Chimecho to hang from tree branches or building eaves, while its long tail can pluck Berries and other food; it is omnivorous and becomes especially active during warm weather and at night. Rather than powering conventional flight, Chimecho rides natural winds, allowing air currents to carry its light body between habitats. Mega Chimecho surrounds itself with seven resonating bell-like ornaments whose combined cries can soothe listeners and are said to purify malice and evil spirits, yet the same resonance can be weaponized in every direction so violently that victims become detached from reality, lose memories, and may even forget who they are.
pokemon.description: Chimecho is a Psychic-type Pokémon introduced in Generation III and a final stage of its evolution line, with a base stat total of 455.

playthrough: Absol is a single-stage Dark-type built around an enormous base 130 Attack but only base 75 Speed and 65/60/60 defensive bulk, making it a powerful but relatively fragile physical attacker. Generation III is awkward for Absol because Dark attacks are special by type and therefore ignore its best stat, forcing physical offense to rely on Normal, Ghost, Fighting, or other coverage; the Generation IV physical/special split is a major upgrade because moves such as Night Slash and later Knock Off or Sucker Punch can finally use base 130 Attack as Dark STAB. Super Luck can increase critical-hit frequency, Pressure can drain enemy PP, and the later Hidden Ability Justified raises Attack when hit by Dark moves, while Swords Dance can push Absol's damage to extreme levels when a safe setup turn is available. Standard Mega Absol raises Attack to 150, Special Attack and Speed to 115, and gains Magic Bounce in traditional ability-based formats, reflecting many status moves and hazards while supporting physical, special, or mixed offense. Mega Absol Z, introduced later through Mega Dimension, instead becomes Dark/Ghost with base 154 Attack and extraordinary base 151 Speed, gaining immunities to Normal, Fighting, and Psychic while leaving Fairy as its only conventional type weakness.
competitive: Absol's early competitive career was constrained by Generation III's special Dark typing, which prevented its defining base 130 Attack from powering Dark STAB even though Swords Dance, physical Shadow Ball, Double-Edge, and coverage could still make it threatening in lower tiers. The physical/special split gave standard Absol the offensive identity its stats implied, and later Sucker Punch, stronger Knock Off, Super Luck strategies, and Swords Dance helped it remain a dangerous lower-tier wallbreaker despite poor bulk and only moderate Speed. Mega Absol became a significant XY and ORAS offensive threat through base 150 Attack, base 115 Speed, useful base 115 Special Attack, and Magic Bounce, which discouraged hazards and status while letting it attack from either side of the spectrum. Mega Absol Z is a much newer form and should not be assigned the same historical résumé: its Dark/Ghost typing, base 154 Attack, and base 151 Speed instead define an extremely fast physical profile with three immunities and only a Fairy weakness, though the same 65/60/60 bulk remains. Across every form, Absol succeeds by forcing immediate offensive respect rather than absorbing attacks; prediction, priority, and safe entry are far more important than defensive longevity.
nuzlocke: Absol can be an excellent Nuzlocke attacker because base 130 Attack arrives without any evolution requirement and its Dark typing provides a complete Psychic immunity. The line's weakness is survivability: base 60 defenses leave very little room for incorrect damage estimates, and ordinary Absol's Fighting, Bug, and later Fairy weaknesses can be especially dangerous because base 75 Speed does not guarantee moving first. Sucker Punch can eliminate faster attacking opponents but depends on the target actually choosing an attacking move, making it much less reliable when enemy behavior is uncertain. Standard Mega Absol greatly improves Speed and Magic Bounce can reflect many status or hazard moves in ability-based formats, but its defenses remain unchanged, so Mega Evolution does not turn it into a tank. Mega Absol Z offers even greater offensive safety through base 151 Speed and Normal, Fighting, and Psychic immunities, yet the same frail defenses mean a strong neutral hit or Fairy attack can still end the matchup abruptly.

pokemon.name: Absol
pokemon.biologyAndBehavior: Absol lives in remote mountain environments and possesses an extraordinary sensitivity to subtle changes in the sky and land, allowing it to predict earthquakes, tidal waves, and other natural disasters before they occur. It descends from its isolated habitat specifically to warn humans of approaching danger, but because disaster repeatedly followed its appearances, people historically blamed Absol for causing the very catastrophes it was trying to prevent and named it the Disaster Pokemon. Later understanding reversed much of that superstition, and Absol is now also remembered as a protector that has helped safeguard fields and settlements by providing advance warning. Its sickle-shaped horn is central to this sensory ability and can continue detecting danger even while Absol sleeps; the species can live for roughly a century and is described as moving with wind-like speed when necessary. Standard Mega Absol intensifies its frightening aura so greatly that fainthearted observers can collapse from shock, despite Absol itself disliking unnecessary fighting, while Mega Absol Z manipulates its dark fur into sharp clawlike structures and is described as ending battles with a single merciful blow intended to prevent prolonged suffering.
pokemon.description: Absol is a Dark-type Pokémon introduced in Generation III, with a base stat total of 465 and no standard evolutions.

playthrough: Snorunt has two final evolutions: any Snorunt can evolve into pure Ice-type Glalie at level 42, while a female Snorunt can instead use a Dawn Stone to become the faster Ice/Ghost Froslass. Glalie is statistically balanced at base 80 in every stat, which makes it flexible but rarely exceptional; Ice Beam, Crunch, Earthquake, Spikes, Ice Shard, and other coverage or utility let it fill several roles without a dominant specialty. Froslass trades some of that neutrality for base 110 Speed and two immunities to Normal and Fighting, but its 70/70/70 bulk means it relies on moving first, status, Spikes, or offensive pressure rather than taking repeated hits. Mega Glalie raises both offenses to 120 and Speed to 100, with Refrigerate in traditional ability-based formats turning Normal attacks into stronger Ice-type moves, while the newer Mega Froslass reaches base 140 Special Attack and 120 Speed and uses Snow Warning in current ability-based formats to summon snow immediately. Every branch retains Ice's difficult weakness profile—Glalie fears Fire, Fighting, Rock, and Steel, while Froslass also adds Ghost and Dark weaknesses—so the family rewards offense and matchup knowledge far more than defensive switching.
competitive: Glalie and Froslass developed very different competitive identities despite sharing Snorunt as a pre-evolution. Glalie's most persistent niche has been entry-hazard support: in DPP lower tiers, base 80 Speed, Spikes, Taunt, Ice Shard, and Explosion allowed it to function as an aggressive lead, while Mega Glalie later became a potent wallbreaker and Spikes setter through base 120 mixed offenses, base 100 Speed, and Refrigerate-boosted Normal attacks. Froslass has the stronger historical support résumé: base 110 Speed, Spikes, Taunt, Destiny Bond, and Ghost typing let it set hazards while simultaneously blocking Rapid Spin, and it was effective enough to earn UUBL status in DPP while even receiving a documented Ubers lead niche. The newer Mega Froslass shifts dramatically toward special offense with base 140 Special Attack and 120 Speed; current official competitive coverage also highlights Snow Warning as a weather-setting tool, letting it establish snow immediately for Blizzard accuracy or team support in ability-based formats. All forms remain vulnerable to common super-effective attacks and entry-hazard pressure, but this family has produced several unusually effective lead, hazard, and offensive roles from otherwise modest base forms.
nuzlocke: Snorunt can be awkward in a Nuzlocke because it remains relatively weak until a late level-42 evolution into Glalie unless the player has a female individual and access to a Dawn Stone for Froslass. Glalie's perfectly balanced base-80 stats provide reasonable consistency, and Inner Focus prevents flinching while Ice Body can supply passive recovery in snow, but pure Ice typing offers very few defensive opportunities and several common weaknesses. Froslass is much faster and gains Normal and Fighting immunities, creating excellent planned switches, but its low bulk means Fire, Rock, Ghost, Dark, and Steel coverage can be lethal; Destiny Bond is generally undesirable when the goal is keeping every team member alive. Mega Glalie can shorten fights dramatically through stronger Refrigerate offense, while Mega Froslass's high Special Attack, base 120 Speed, and immediate snow can reduce the number of turns an opponent gets to act. Neither Mega form fixes the fundamental fragility of Ice-based defensive typing, so the safest choice depends on whether the run values Glalie's steadier all-around stats or Froslass's speed and immunities.

pokemon.name: Snorunt
pokemon.biologyAndBehavior: Snorunt is extraordinarily cold-adapted and can survive temperatures as low as roughly minus 150 degrees Fahrenheit while feeding primarily on snow and ice. It is social rather than solitary, commonly traveling in groups of five and living together peacefully beneath large leaves or inside caves when the surrounding landscape lacks sufficient snow. In snowy regions, folklore treats a visiting Snorunt as a sign of prosperity and claims that homes welcomed by the Pokemon will flourish for generations. Its heavy cloak helps retain warmth despite the brutal climate, and even populations living in warmer regions such as Alola seek out the coldest available mountain habitats. The line's later split evolution makes this humble communal snow-eater the starting point for either Glalie's armored ice predator or the far more supernatural Froslass.
pokemon.description: Snorunt is an Ice-type Pokémon introduced in Generation III and the first stage of its evolution line, with a base stat total of 300.

pokemon.name: Glalie
pokemon.biologyAndBehavior: Glalie consists of a dark rock core enclosed in ice armor formed by instantly freezing moisture from the surrounding air into whatever shape it requires. The underlying rock is not exceptionally hard, but once coated in this self-generated ice the body becomes harder than steel and can remain frozen without melting even under intense heat. Glalie hunts by freezing prey solid and swallowing it whole, showing a particular preference for creatures that are already frozen, such as Vanillite. A mountain legend claims the species began when a boulder absorbed the distress and regrets of lost mountaineers and came to life, giving its otherwise physical ice-control biology a supernatural origin tradition. Mega Evolution violently dislocates and breaks Glalie's jaw, causing endless blizzards to pour from its mouth; although this makes Mega Glalie much more dangerous, the damaged jaw prevents it from eating normally and leaves the Pokemon perpetually irritated.
pokemon.description: Glalie is an Ice-type Pokémon introduced in Generation III and a final stage of its evolution line, with a base stat total of 480.

pokemon.name: Froslass
pokemon.biologyAndBehavior: Froslass is a female-only Ice/Ghost Pokemon with a hollow, kimono-like torso and breath cold enough to freeze targets at roughly minus 58 degrees Fahrenheit. Its hunting behavior is among the darkest recorded for an ordinary species: it is said to prey on frozen souls, particularly those of men, and may freeze humans or Pokemon it finds attractive before carrying the bodies back to its den and arranging them neatly as decorations. Stories warn that Froslass descend to human settlements during severe blizzards and knock on doors, and traditional advice is explicit that anyone hearing such a knock should not open the door. One major origin legend claims the species formed when the spirit and lingering regrets of a woman who died on a snowy mountain possessed an icicle. Mega Froslass magnifies its supernatural cold so greatly that spectral energy allows it to freeze normally intangible things such as flames and wind, create enormous ice structures, and disappear into shadows before reappearing elsewhere.
pokemon.description: Froslass is an Ice/Ghost-type Pokémon introduced in Generation IV and a final stage of its evolution line, with a base stat total of 480.

playthrough: The Spheal line develops into a bulky Water/Ice family, with Spheal evolving into Sealeo at level 32 and Walrein at level 44. Walrein's 110 HP, 90 Defense, 90 Special Defense, and 95 Special Attack give it much better overall durability than many Ice-types, while Water and Ice attacks are both special in Generation III and therefore naturally use its stronger offensive stat from the family's debut. Surf, Ice Beam, Blizzard, Body Slam, Earthquake, Encore, Toxic, Rest, and other options allow Walrein to function as a bulky attacker or utility Pokemon, while Thick Fat halves Fire- and Ice-type damage and makes its defensive profile more comfortable than the typing alone suggests. Ice Body provides passive recovery during hail or snow in games where its healing effect applies, creating a much more defensive weather role, while Oblivious offers narrower protection from attraction, Taunt in later mechanics, and similar effects. Water/Ice still carries weaknesses to Electric, Grass, Fighting, and Rock, and the level-44 final evolution is relatively late, but Walrein rewards the wait with strong mixed bulk and useful dual STAB.
competitive: Walrein was a significant ADV UU Pokemon rather than merely a bulky Ice-type, using 110/90/90 defenses, Thick Fat, base 95 Special Attack, Surf, Ice Beam, and physical coverage to check or pressure a wide range of prominent threats. Its Water/Ice typing and Thick Fat gave it useful matchups against selected Fire- and Ice-based attackers, while the combination of strong STAB and respectable bulk meant opponents could not simply treat it as a passive wall. DPP created the family's most famous competitive strategy through Ice Body: under permanent hail, Leftovers plus Ice Body restored one-eighth of Walrein's maximum HP per turn, allowing Substitute and Protect to repeatedly consume opposing turns while hail and Toxic Spikes wore enemies down. This 'Stallrein' strategy became one of the defining pieces of dedicated hail stall because the passive recovery could replenish the HP spent on Substitute over a Protect cycle, creating long sequences that were extremely difficult for slower teams to break. Weather mechanics and later power creep reduced that niche in newer generations, but Walrein retains a meaningful competitive history as both an ADV bulky attacker and one of DPP hail's signature defensive abusers.
nuzlocke: The Spheal line is a strong Nuzlocke option because every stage has substantial HP and the final Walrein combines base 110 HP with 90 in both defenses, giving it a forgiving margin against neutral damage. Thick Fat is particularly useful because Fire damage is halved and Ice becomes extremely easy to absorb, while Ice Body can provide free recovery in compatible snow or hail conditions. The family does not reach Walrein until level 44, but Spheal and Sealeo are naturally bulky enough to contribute during the long development period rather than functioning only as dead weight until the final evolution. Electric, Grass, Fighting, and Rock attacks remain serious dangers, and Walrein's base 65 Speed means it often has to absorb a hit before responding, so super-effective coverage should still be checked carefully. Within favorable matchups, the combination of strong HP, dual STAB, and weather or ability-based sustain makes Walrein one of Hoenn's safer Ice-type choices for permadeath play.

pokemon.name: Spheal
pokemon.biologyAndBehavior: Spheal is so round and its flippers are so poorly suited to walking that rolling across ice is faster and more natural than trying to move on foot. A thick layer of blubber beneath plush fur traps body heat and allows it to remain comfortable on drift ice and in freezing seas. Spheal are strongly social and clap their fins noisily when eating together, while individuals drifting at sea actively search for prey and report successful feeding locations back to the Walrein leading their herd. Sealeo frequently balance and roll Spheal on their noses, not simply for play but to check the younger Pokemon's scent and confirm that it remains healthy. The family therefore shows coordinated herd behavior from its youngest stage, with Spheal participating in food scouting even before it develops the strength of its evolutions.
pokemon.description: Spheal is an Ice/Water-type Pokémon introduced in Generation III and the first stage of its evolution line, with a base stat total of 290.

pokemon.name: Sealeo
pokemon.biologyAndBehavior: Sealeo possesses extremely sensitive whiskers and investigates unfamiliar objects by balancing them on its nose, spinning them, and using both scent and touch to determine what they are and whether it likes them. This habit extends to younger members of its own species: Sealeo rolls Spheal on its nose specifically to verify their familiar scent and check their health. It lives on drift ice and in cold seas and dives underwater to hunt roughly five times each day, locating prey primarily through its keen sense of smell rather than vision. Its powerful front flippers are strong enough to crush ice, giving the middle evolution much greater ability to reshape its frozen environment than the rolling Spheal. Even while asleep, Sealeo's whiskers remain sensitive enough to register surrounding conditions, suggesting that environmental monitoring continues with little interruption.
pokemon.description: Sealeo is an Ice/Water-type Pokémon introduced in Generation III and a middle stage of its evolution line, with a base stat total of 410.

pokemon.name: Walrein
pokemon.biologyAndBehavior: Walrein lives in icy seas in herds of roughly twenty to thirty individuals, with a dominant leader that protects the entire group so fiercely it may sacrifice its own life during an attack. A deep layer of blubber insulates the body against extreme cold and also cushions physical blows, causing some enemy attacks to bounce away rather than penetrate effectively. Its enormous tusks can crush blocks of ice weighing up to ten tons with a single blow and continue growing throughout life; tusks broken during combat naturally regrow by the following year. Younger Spheal in the herd scout surrounding waters for prey and alert the Walrein leader when food is found, revealing a coordinated feeding system rather than a loose aggregation of individuals. The species combines enormous physical power with unusually strong social responsibility, making the largest member of the family not just a predator but the defender and organizer of an extended cold-ocean herd.
pokemon.description: Walrein is an Ice/Water-type Pokémon introduced in Generation III and a final stage of its evolution line, with a base stat total of 530.

playthrough: Clamperl has a branching trade evolution: trading it while it holds a Deep Sea Tooth produces Huntail, while trading it with a Deep Sea Scale produces Gorebyss. That requirement can make the line inconvenient in a normal playthrough, but Clamperl itself has an unusual item interaction—the Deep Sea Tooth doubles its Special Attack and the Deep Sea Scale doubles its Special Defense while held—so even the unevolved form can perform surprisingly specialized roles. Huntail is the more physically oriented evolution with base 104 Attack and 105 Defense, while Gorebyss favors special offense with base 114 Special Attack and the same 105 Defense; in Generation III, however, Water attacks are special, so Gorebyss's main STAB fits its stats much better than Huntail's. The Generation IV physical/special split improves Huntail through physical Water moves such as Waterfall, while Generation V gives both evolutions Shell Smash, sharply raising Attack, Special Attack, and Speed at the cost of both defenses and turning either one into a dangerous setup attacker. Both remain slow before setup and are weak to Grass and Electric, so their best story role is usually to find one safe turn, boost or exploit rain, and attack aggressively rather than attempt to function as conventional bulky Water-types.
competitive: Huntail and Gorebyss spent their early competitive lives as niche rain sweepers, but Generation V's addition of Shell Smash gave the entire family a much more distinctive identity. Gorebyss became the stronger special Shell Smash sweeper thanks to base 114 Special Attack, Swift Swim, Surf or Hydro Pump, Ice Beam, and coverage, while Huntail used base 104 Attack, physical Water STAB, and later Sucker Punch to approach the same strategy from the physical side. Both also gained notoriety from combining Shell Smash with Baton Pass, allowing a single setup turn to transfer enormous Attack, Special Attack, and Speed boosts to another teammate; that strategy became powerful enough to face restrictions or bans in several Smogon formats. Gorebyss generally received more competitive attention because its higher Special Attack made it better able to threaten opponents itself rather than functioning only as a passer, while Huntail has frequently been described as the more situational choice. Low base 52 Speed before boosting, merely average special bulk, common Electric and Grass weaknesses, and competition from stronger Shell Smash users keep both evolutions out of high tiers, but the family retains one of the series' clearest setup-and-pass identities.
nuzlocke: The Clamperl family can be difficult to plan around in a Nuzlocke because reaching either final form traditionally requires both the correct held item and a trade, which may be impossible under a solo-cartridge or no-trade ruleset. If the evolution is available, Huntail and Gorebyss both offer good physical Defense and simple pure Water typing, leaving only Grass and Electric as ordinary weaknesses. Gorebyss is generally the safer immediate special attacker, while Huntail becomes more attractive once physical Water STAB is available; Shell Smash can let either one sweep but also lowers both defenses, which is a serious permadeath risk if the opponent survives. Swift Swim can provide much safer speed control in rain without sacrificing defenses, while Huntail's Water Veil prevents burns and Gorebyss's Hydration can cure status during rain in generations where those abilities are available. The line is strongest when evolution access and opposing coverage are known in advance; otherwise, the trade requirement and setup-dependent Speed make it less dependable than more straightforward Water families.

pokemon.name: Clamperl
pokemon.biologyAndBehavior: Clamperl is a carnivorous deep-sea bivalve that remains protected inside an extremely hard shell and clamps down on captured prey until the victim stops moving. The central pearl-like structure is biologically valuable rather than decorative: Clamperl's pearls can amplify psychic power, are said to be roughly ten times more valuable than pearls produced by Shellder, and are the source of the pearls carried by Spoink. As Clamperl approaches evolution, the soft body inside grows too large to fit comfortably within the original shell, making physical growth itself a sign that the protected juvenile stage is ending. Older shells accumulate scratches and nicks from life on the seafloor, while the powerful valves continue serving both as armor and as a feeding weapon. Clamperl therefore combines the defensive biology of a shellfish with an unexpectedly active predatory lifestyle and produces one of the Pokemon world's most valuable naturally occurring gemstones.
pokemon.description: Clamperl is a Water-type Pokémon introduced in Generation III and the first stage of its evolution line, with a base stat total of 345.

pokemon.name: Huntail
pokemon.biologyAndBehavior: Huntail lives at extreme ocean depths where sunlight never reaches, and its large eyes are adapted to seeing through the darkness and murky deep-sea water. Its tail mimics a small fish and carries glowing eye-like markings; Huntail waves this false prey in the darkness to lure other animals close before opening its enormous toothed mouth and swallowing the victim whole. A thick, sturdy spine allows its long serpentine body to withstand crushing deep-sea pressure, although Huntail is not actually an especially powerful swimmer and moves by wriggling its body from side to side. Because people rarely encounter the species alive near the surface, a Huntail washing ashore has traditionally been interpreted as an omen that misfortune is approaching. Its anatomy is therefore built around life in a world of darkness and pressure: strong skeletal support, enlarged vision, bioluminescent deception, and ambush feeding compensate for relatively weak sustained swimming.
pokemon.description: Huntail is a Water-type Pokémon introduced in Generation III and a final stage of its evolution line, with a base stat total of 485.

pokemon.name: Gorebyss
pokemon.biologyAndBehavior: Gorebyss looks graceful while swimming through the deep southern seas, but its feeding behavior is remarkably predatory: the long needle-like mouth is driven into prey and used to drain the victim's body fluids. The discarded remains sink to the seafloor and become food for other Pokemon, giving Gorebyss's hunting a direct role in moving nutrients down into the deep-sea ecosystem. It is not exclusively carnivorous and also feeds on seaweed growing between rocks, making the species capable of switching between plant material and animal prey. Its pink coloration changes with water temperature and becomes noticeably more vivid after feeding and during spring, with Alolan individuals described as almost blindingly bright. Like Huntail, Gorebyss possesses a body capable of surviving enormous deep-water pressure, but evolution has produced a very different hunting strategy centered on precision feeding rather than swallowing prey whole.
pokemon.description: Gorebyss is a Water-type Pokémon introduced in Generation III and a final stage of its evolution line, with a base stat total of 485.

playthrough: Relicanth is a single-stage Water/Rock Pokemon with excellent physical durability: base 100 HP and 130 Defense allow it to absorb many Normal-, Flying-, Fire-, and other physical attacks comfortably, while base 90 Attack gives Rock and Ground moves respectable power. Its Special Defense is only base 65 and Special Attack only 45, so the huge physical bulk should not be mistaken for all-purpose tanking; Electric, Fighting, and Ground attacks are dangerous, and Grass deals quadruple damage. Rock Head is particularly useful because it eliminates recoil from moves such as Double-Edge and, in later generations, Head Smash, letting Relicanth use extremely powerful physical attacks without damaging itself, while Swift Swim can double its Speed in rain. Generation III suits its offense reasonably well because Rock attacks are physical and use its stronger Attack even though Water attacks are special and comparatively weak from Relicanth itself. In the Hoenn games Relicanth also has unique progression value beyond combat: it is one of the Pokemon required in the Sealed Chamber party puzzle that unlocks access to Regirock, Regice, and Registeel, making an otherwise optional deep-sea encounter essential for that legendary sidequest.
competitive: Relicanth was one of ADV NU's strongest Rock-types, with Smogon highlighting its enormous physical bulk, respectable Attack, and useful choice between Rock Head and Swift Swim. Defensive sets could check many Normal- and Flying-type attackers while using Rock Slide, Earthquake, Toxic, Rest, or Sleep Talk, whereas Choice Band sets turned Relicanth into a bulky physical attacker that did not immediately surrender defensive utility. Later access to Head Smash gave Rock Head an ideal partner: a 150-power Rock STAB attack could be used without recoil, making Relicanth far more threatening than base 90 Attack alone would imply. Swift Swim provides a separate rain-sweeper role by doubling its otherwise poor base 55 Speed, though the low Special Defense and severe Grass weakness make setup and positioning important. Relicanth has remained a lower-tier specialist as stronger Water/Rock Pokemon and faster attackers appeared, but its combination of physical bulk and recoil-free high-power Rock offense has given it a consistent competitive identity.
nuzlocke: Relicanth can be very safe in a Nuzlocke against known physical opponents because 100 HP and base 130 Defense create one of Hoenn's strongest physical cushions. Rock Head is also unusually Nuzlocke-friendly because recoil moves can be used without slowly damaging the user, while Head Smash in later games becomes a massive attack without its usual self-inflicted cost. The danger is special coverage: base 65 Special Defense is much weaker than the physical side, and Grass attacks deal quadruple damage while Electric, Fighting, and Ground are also super effective. Swift Swim can improve safety in rain by allowing Relicanth to move first, but rain simultaneously strengthens opposing Water attacks, so the weather should not be treated as universally beneficial. In Hoenn, catching and preserving a Relicanth also has strategic value even outside battle because the Regi sidequest requires it for the Sealed Chamber puzzle.

pokemon.name: Relicanth
pokemon.biologyAndBehavior: Relicanth is an ancient deep-sea fish whose body plan has remained essentially unchanged for roughly 100 million years, leading researchers to describe it as a living fossil and even an already 'perfect' life-form for its environment. Its rough stone-like scales, fatty body, and oil-filled swim bladders allow it to tolerate the crushing pressure of extreme ocean depths. Although its ancestors possessed teeth, those structures have atrophied completely; modern Relicanth are toothless filter feeders that suck microscopic organisms from the surrounding water rather than hunting larger prey. Two pairs of pectoral fins help it crawl or push itself along the seafloor, preserving a mode of movement that has apparently required almost no evolutionary modification over geological time. The species was believed extinct until discovered during a deep-sea expedition, making its survival one of the Pokemon world's clearest examples of a lineage persisting virtually unchanged while ecosystems around it transformed.
pokemon.description: Relicanth is a Water/Rock-type Pokémon introduced in Generation III, with a base stat total of 485 and no standard evolutions.

playthrough: Luvdisc is a single-stage pure Water Pokemon whose one clearly strong stat is base 97 Speed; its 43 HP, 30 Attack, 55 Defense, 40 Special Attack, and 65 Special Defense leave it dramatically weaker than most fully evolved Water-types. In Generation III Water attacks are special, but base 40 Special Attack means Surf, Water Pulse, or Hydro Pump still produce disappointing damage unless the target is weak to Water or Luvdisc is heavily overleveled. Swift Swim can double its already good Speed in rain and nearly guarantees moving first, while Hydration in later generations can cure status during rain, but neither ability fixes the lack of offensive power or physical durability. Charm, Sweet Kiss, Attract, Aqua Ring, status, or other support can create niche utility, yet many battles last longer than they would with almost any other Water-type and therefore expose Luvdisc to additional risk. Its most valuable Hoenn-era gameplay role may actually occur outside direct combat: wild Luvdisc have historically been an important renewable source of Heart Scales used by Move Reminder services.
competitive: Luvdisc has essentially no meaningful history in serious standard competitive singles because its base-stat total is simply too low for a fully evolved Pokemon. Base 97 Speed and Swift Swim can make it exceptionally fast in rain, but base 40 Special Attack means that even boosted Water attacks fail to threaten the bulky Pokemon that dedicated rain sweepers are expected to break. Support options such as Toxic, Charm, Sweet Kiss, Aqua Ring, or Endeavor can create novelty strategies, but 43/55/65 bulk provides almost no opportunity to use them repeatedly. Stronger Water-types outperform Luvdisc as attackers, walls, rain users, and support Pokemon, leaving it without the unique mechanic that allows some other statistically weak species to carve out a niche. Competitive analyses consequently treat Luvdisc as a challenge or novelty pick rather than a strategically efficient choice.
nuzlocke: Luvdisc is a difficult Nuzlocke Pokemon to justify for direct combat because low HP, poor physical Defense, and extremely weak offenses make even ordinary neutral exchanges unnecessarily dangerous. Its excellent Speed is the main safety advantage, allowing it to use status or support before many enemies can act and making accidental critical hits from slower foes less likely simply because Luvdisc may finish a weakened target first. Swift Swim makes that Speed extreme in rain, but the inability to secure knockouts reliably means moving first does not guarantee avoiding damage. Grass and Electric attacks are the obvious weaknesses, while strong neutral physical moves can also be threatening despite the simple pure Water typing. In games where Heart Scales are valuable, catching Luvdisc may still be worthwhile for resource acquisition even if the Pokemon itself never becomes a permanent battle-team member.

pokemon.name: Luvdisc
pokemon.biologyAndBehavior: Luvdisc is a warm-water reef fish covered in heart-shaped scales and closely associated with Corsola branches and tropical coral habitats, where it builds nests in protected reef structures. During breeding season enormous groups congregate around coral reefs in such numbers that the surface of the sea appears pink. The species forms strong social bonds and becomes visibly disheartened when isolated, leaving a lone Luvdisc more vulnerable to predators such as Pelipper. Its heart-shaped body became a human symbol of romance after people repeatedly observed Luvdisc swimming around loving couples; hotels release them into honeymoon pools, and several cultures traditionally give a Luvdisc as a declaration of love. That symbolism once became dangerous for the species when a rumor that its scales could help someone find a romantic partner caused heavy overfishing, showing how human folklore can directly affect Pokemon populations.
pokemon.description: Luvdisc is a Water-type Pokémon introduced in Generation III, with a base stat total of 330 and no standard evolutions.

playthrough: The Bagon line is Hoenn's Dragon-type pseudo-legendary family, evolving from Bagon to Shelgon at level 30 and finally into Salamence at the unusually late level 50. The payoff is enormous: Salamence has base 135 Attack, 110 Special Attack, and 100 Speed alongside Intimidate, making it both a powerful mixed attacker and a useful physical pivot whenever it enters battle. Generation III gives Salamence an unusual mixed profile because Dragon attacks are special while Flying attacks, Earthquake, and most Normal coverage are physical; Dragon Dance can strengthen physical Attack and Speed even though its Dragon STAB itself still uses Special Attack. The Generation IV physical/special split unlocks physical Dragon STAB such as Dragon Claw and Outrage, making Dragon Dance substantially more threatening, while the later Hidden Ability Moxie can raise Attack after each knockout and create snowballing sweeps. Mega Salamence raises Attack to 145, Defense to 130, Special Attack to 120, and Speed to 120 while Aerilate turns Normal moves into boosted Flying STAB, but every ordinary and Mega form retains a quadruple Ice weakness that must be respected.
competitive: Salamence was one of the defining threats of ADV OU from the moment it appeared, combining 135 Attack, 110 Special Attack, 100 Speed, Intimidate, a Ground immunity, and enough coverage to function as a mixed wallbreaker, Choice Band attacker, or Dragon Dance sweeper. The Generation IV physical/special split and access to powerful physical Dragon moves pushed it even further, and Salamence ultimately ended DPP classified in Ubers rather than OU. Later generations brought competition from other Dragons and Fairy-types, but Moxie preserved dangerous cleaning sets and the introduction of Mega Salamence in ORAS completely reset the family's competitive ceiling. Mega Salamence's 95/145/130/120/90/120 stats, pre-Mega Intimidate, Dragon Dance, Roost, and Aerilate-boosted Flying attacks proved overwhelming for ORAS OU and resulted in a rapid ban to Ubers, where it remained a genuine top-level threat rather than merely an exile from standard play. Its enduring counters are the quadruple Ice weakness, Rock damage and entry hazards, Fairy- and Dragon-type attacks, and faster revenge killers before setup, but few non-legendary Pokemon have matched Salamence's combination of offensive versatility and repeated high-tier relevance.
nuzlocke: The Bagon line is a major long-term Nuzlocke investment because Bagon is usually obtained relatively late and does not reach Salamence until level 50, leaving a long period in which the team must protect Bagon and then the slow, defensive Shelgon. Shelgon's base 100 Defense and strong shell make the middle stage much safer physically than Bagon, while Salamence finally adds base 100 Speed, enormous offense, a Ground immunity, and Intimidate for immediate physical damage reduction. Intimidate is one of the family's strongest permadeath tools because simply switching Salamence into a known physical move lowers the opponent's Attack before damage calculations begin. The quadruple Ice weakness is the critical danger and makes unexpected Ice Beam, Ice Punch, or Ice Shard potentially lethal even to a healthy Salamence; Rock, Dragon, and later Fairy coverage also require careful scouting. Mega Salamence's dramatically improved Defense and Speed increase its margin for error, but it does not remove the Ice weakness, so the family remains strongest when its offensive power is paired with disciplined coverage knowledge.

pokemon.name: Bagon
pokemon.biologyAndBehavior: Bagon is a solitary mountain Pokemon driven by an extraordinary instinctive desire to fly despite being born without wings. It repeatedly leaps from high cliffs in doomed attempts to take flight and, frustrated by failure, slams its head into surrounding rocks with enough force to smash boulders apart. Years of this behavior have made the skull as hard as steel, while powerful neck muscles absorb the repeated impacts and support its headbutting attacks. Researchers believe the dream of flight may be encoded genetically and that Bagon's constant attempts actually stimulate the cellular changes needed for future evolution. The obsession continues even in sleep, when Bagon may flap its short arms and appear to practice flying in its dreams.
pokemon.description: Bagon is a Dragon-type Pokémon introduced in Generation III and the first stage of its evolution line, with a base stat total of 300.

pokemon.name: Shelgon
pokemon.biologyAndBehavior: Shelgon represents an extended transformation stage in which Bagon's body becomes almost completely enclosed inside six hard white shell plates made from a substance similar to bone. The shell repels most attacks but is so heavy that Shelgon can barely move, causing it to hide deep inside caves while its internal cells rapidly reorganize into the body of Salamence. During this period Shelgon is never seen eating or drinking despite remaining alive for a long time, and researchers suspect that energy stored before evolution sustains the transformation. When the process is complete, the shell peels away almost immediately rather than gradually wearing down. Even while sleeping and conserving energy, Shelgon can be observed moving its legs as though running or flying in a dream, suggesting that Bagon's fixation on the sky survives intact throughout the otherwise almost motionless pupal stage.
pokemon.description: Shelgon is a Dragon-type Pokémon introduced in Generation III and a middle stage of its evolution line, with a base stat total of 420.

pokemon.name: Salamence
pokemon.biologyAndBehavior: Salamence is one of the clearest examples in Pokemon biology of behavior apparently reshaping evolution: the line's generations-long longing for flight is said to trigger a sudden cellular mutation that produces enormous red wings. After finally achieving that goal, Salamence spends long periods flying joyfully across the sky and releases blasts of fire in excitement, often refusing to land until exhaustion forces it to sleep. That exuberance has a violent opposite—when angered, Salamence loses control completely and continues shredding objects with its claws and burning the surrounding landscape until it has exhausted itself. It competes with Garchomp for food in the air, suggesting that its newly acquired aerial lifestyle places it directly against another powerful apex Dragon. Mega Evolution deforms its proud wings into one crescent-shaped blade and causes severe psychological stress; Mega Salamence can slice obstacles or opponents apart without slowing down, may even attack the Trainer who raised it, and has consequently earned the name 'the blood-soaked crescent.'
pokemon.description: Salamence is a Dragon/Flying-type Pokémon introduced in Generation III and a final stage of its evolution line, with a base stat total of 600.

playthrough: The Beldum line is Hoenn's Steel/Psychic pseudo-legendary family, with Beldum evolving into Metang at level 20 and Metang into Metagross at level 45. Metagross combines base 135 Attack and 130 Defense with 80 HP, 95 Special Attack, and 90 Special Defense, giving it exceptional physical power and bulk while Clear Body prevents opponents from lowering its stats. Generation III fits its mixed offense well because Steel attacks such as Meteor Mash are physical while Psychic is special, letting Metagross use both base 135 Attack and base 95 Special Attack; Earthquake, Shadow Ball in older mechanics, Explosion, and broad coverage further increase its flexibility. Its defensive typing was even stronger before Generation VI, when Steel still resisted Dark and Ghost and Metagross had only Fire and Ground weaknesses; from Generation VI onward Dark and Ghost also become super effective, although the newly introduced Fairy resistance adds another important defensive role. Mega Metagross raises Attack to 145, Defense to 150, Special Defense to 110, and Speed to 110 while Tough Claws strengthens contact moves, but in the original Hoenn games the family has little effect on the main story because Steven's Beldum is normally obtained only after becoming Champion.
competitive: Metagross was immediately one of ADV OU's defining Pokemon, combining tremendous physical bulk, base 135 Attack, an excellent defensive typing, Clear Body, Meteor Mash, Earthquake, Explosion, and enough special coverage to fit offensive, defensive, mixed, Choice Band, and Agility roles. It remained one of DPP OU's best glue Pokemon, where Stealth Rock, Bullet Punch, improved physical coverage, Explosion, and Agility let it support teams or threaten sweeps without giving up its natural defensive value. Standard Metagross declined in later generations as Steel lost its Dark and Ghost resistances and power creep exposed its base 70 Speed, but Mega Metagross restored it to the top level in ORAS with base 145 Attack, 150 Defense, 110 Special Defense, 110 Speed, Tough Claws, and an enormous coverage movepool. Mega Metagross remained a major threat into Sun and Moon and was ultimately treated as an Uber rather than a standard OU Pokemon in that generation, illustrating how its combination of speed, bulk, and coverage could become overwhelming. Its recurring limitations are weaknesses to Fire and Ground plus later Dark and Ghost, imperfect accuracy on moves such as Meteor Mash or Zen Headbutt, and severe four-moveslot pressure because no single set can carry every coverage option it wants.
nuzlocke: The Beldum line can become one of the safest and strongest Nuzlocke families available, but availability often determines whether that matters: in the original Hoenn games Beldum is primarily a post-Champion gift and therefore cannot help with the normal main-story run. In games where it can be obtained earlier, Beldum's extremely low catch rate when wild and historically tiny early movepool can make acquisition and training awkward, but it reaches the much more capable Metang at only level 20 and Metagross at level 45. Metagross's huge Defense, strong Special Defense, Poison immunity, long resistance list, and Clear Body make many physical matchups extremely forgiving, while base 135 Attack can end battles quickly enough to reduce exposure to critical hits and secondary effects. Fire and Ground are the major original weaknesses, with Dark and Ghost joining them from Generation VI onward; despite its excellent bulk, strong super-effective special attacks can still cause serious damage and should be checked rather than tanked blindly. Mega Metagross increases both defenses and Speed dramatically, making it even safer where available, though Tough Claws encourages contact attacks that may still trigger effects such as Rough Skin, Static, or damaging held items.

pokemon.name: Beldum
pokemon.biologyAndBehavior: Beldum appears mechanical, but it is a living organism with emotions, a need to eat, and a means of reproduction; instead of blood, its body is composed of cells that function like tiny magnets. Magnetism powers almost every aspect of its life, including movement, communication, and attacks, while groups of Beldum can synchronize telepathically and magnetically to move together like a coordinated swarm. When enraged, the magnetic field becomes strong enough to disrupt or break nearby machinery, making emotional state directly capable of interfering with human technology. Beldum can also pull an opponent rapidly toward itself with magnetic force and strike with the clawed end of its body. When sleeping in rugged terrain it anchors those rear hooks into a cliff face, preventing its heavy metallic body from drifting or falling while at rest.
pokemon.description: Beldum is a Steel/Psychic-type Pokémon introduced in Generation III and the first stage of its evolution line, with a base stat total of 300.

pokemon.name: Metang
pokemon.biologyAndBehavior: Metang forms when two Beldum fuse together and connect their brains through a magnetic nervous system, doubling their psychokinetic output without actually doubling their intelligence. The combined magnetic field allows Metang to levitate and fly through harsh mountain terrain at more than 60 miles per hour by rotating its arms backward. Its body is so durable that even colliding with a jet is said to leave it unscratched, while the claws can tear through thick iron sheets as though they were fabric. Metang actively hunts rather than simply scavenging: psychic power stops prey from escaping, after which the claws seize the victim and refuse to let go. It is especially attracted to magnetic minerals and has been documented pursuing Nosepass at high speed, turning the magnetism that powers its own body into a guide for locating food.
pokemon.description: Metang is a Steel/Psychic-type Pokémon introduced in Generation III and a middle stage of its evolution line, with a base stat total of 420.

pokemon.name: Metagross
pokemon.biologyAndBehavior: Metagross is created when two Metang fuse, producing a body with four linked brains connected through a complex neural network and capable of parallel calculations said to exceed a supercomputer. It uses that intelligence tactically, analyzing opponents with extraordinary speed and calmly calculating how to drive them into losing positions rather than relying on brute strength alone. When hunting, however, its method is brutally physical: Metagross pins prey beneath its massive body with four clawed legs and then consumes the trapped animal using a large mouth on its underside. It can tuck in its legs and float through the air, and populations living on snowy mountains become especially energetic because cold temperatures strengthen their magnetic power. Mega Metagross is formed through an even larger linkage—one Metagross, one Metang, and two Beldum—and the resulting increase in brainpower makes it ruthlessly pragmatic; it will use almost any method to win, and if calculation shows victory is impossible it may seize the opponent with its claws and prepare to explode rather than accept defeat.
pokemon.description: Metagross is a Steel/Psychic-type Pokémon introduced in Generation III and a final stage of its evolution line, with a base stat total of 600.

playthrough: Regirock is a single-stage pure Rock legendary built around one of the highest physical Defense stats in the series: base 200 Defense paired with base 80 HP and 100 Attack. That makes ordinary physical Normal-, Flying-, Poison-, and Fire-type attacks extremely easy to absorb, while Rock Slide or Stone Edge, Earthquake, Hammer Arm, Superpower, and other coverage let Regirock retaliate with respectable physical damage. Clear Body prevents opponents from lowering its stats, and the later Hidden Ability Sturdy can guarantee survival from a full-HP knockout attempt, which is particularly useful during difficult story battles. The problem is typing rather than raw durability: pure Rock is weak to Water, Grass, Fighting, Ground, and Steel, and Regirock's base 100 Special Defense—good in isolation—is much less spectacular than its physical side. Because it is usually encountered late and often behind puzzle or postgame requirements, Regirock rarely shapes an entire main story, but once caught it functions as an extremely dependable physical tank and Stealth Rock or status user.
competitive: Regirock debuted in ADV UUBL and has spent much of its competitive history in lower tiers, where base 200 Defense, base 100 Attack, and a broad utility movepool make it far more useful than a simple wall. It can set Stealth Rock in later generations, spread Thunder Wave or Toxic, use Rock STAB and Earthquake for respectable damage, and exploit its enormous physical bulk to check Normal-, Flying-, and Fire-type attackers. Clear Body protects against Intimidate and other stat drops, while Sturdy in later formats can guarantee an emergency support turn if entry hazards have not broken it. Its weaknesses to common Water-, Ground-, Grass-, Fighting-, and Steel-type attacks and lack of reliable instant recovery are the recurring reasons it does not become a dominant wall despite the extraordinary Defense stat. Regirock's competitive identity is therefore that of a sturdy lower-tier glue Pokemon: excellent at compressing physical tanking, hazard setting, and status support, but vulnerable to special pressure and repeated chip.
nuzlocke: Regirock can be exceptionally safe against known physical attackers in a Nuzlocke because base 200 Defense leaves an enormous margin for error against neutral contact and resisted physical moves. Sturdy is excellent insurance when available, while Clear Body prevents unexpected stat drops from turning a carefully planned matchup against it. The danger is assuming that the Defense stat makes every matchup safe; super-effective Water, Grass, Ground, Fighting, and Steel attacks can still deal enormous damage, especially from the special side. Its low base 50 Speed also means Regirock usually has to absorb an attack before responding, so coverage knowledge matters even when it has the favorable raw stat line. As with most legendaries, availability is often late enough that its Nuzlocke value is concentrated in endgame or postgame encounters rather than throughout the run.

pokemon.name: Regirock
pokemon.biologyAndBehavior: Regirock is a golem composed entirely of stone and boulders, with no detectable heart, brain, or conventional internal anatomy even when examined using advanced technology. When pieces of its body are broken off or eroded, it repairs itself by finding new rocks and attaching them directly to the damaged area. Because of this endless self-repair, stones making up a single Regirock may originate from geological layers and locations scattered around the world, giving the body a literal patchwork history. Legend says Regigigas created Regirock from stone, after which ancient humans worshipped it before eventually fearing its power and sealing it away. The mystery is not simply how Regirock lives, but what 'living' means for a creature with no organs at all whose body can be rebuilt indefinitely from ordinary rock.
pokemon.description: Regirock is a Rock-type Pokémon introduced in Generation III, with a base stat total of 580 and no standard evolutions.

playthrough: Regice is the special-defense counterpart of the original legendary giants, with base 200 Special Defense, base 100 Defense, and base 100 Special Attack. Ice Beam or Blizzard uses that respectable Special Attack well, while Thunderbolt or Thunder provides excellent coverage against Water-types and creates the famous Ice-plus-Electric combination that very few targets resist comfortably. Clear Body prevents hostile stat drops, while later Ice Body can restore HP during hail or snow in games and formats where its healing effect applies. The weakness is pure Ice typing: Fire, Fighting, Rock, and Steel all hit super effectively, and Ice supplies almost no defensive resistances beyond resisting itself. Regice therefore performs much better as a special sponge that threatens meaningful damage than as an all-purpose wall, especially because its base 50 Speed forces it to take a hit before attacking.
competitive: Regice was a genuine ADV OU Pokemon and occupied a rare niche as a special wall that also exerted real offensive pressure. Base 200 Special Defense let it pivot into many special attackers, while base 100 Special Attack and Ice Beam plus Electric coverage forced opponents such as Zapdos, Celebi, Skarmory, Starmie, and Water-types to respect its damage rather than treating it as passive. Explosion gave ADV Regice an especially valuable endgame option: after drawing in opposing special walls such as Blissey or Snorlax, it could sacrifice itself to remove or heavily damage them and open the field for a teammate. Later generations made pure Ice typing and hazard weakness more punishing, and stronger special walls with better recovery or typing pushed Regice toward lower tiers despite the same spectacular Special Defense. Its ADV history remains important because it demonstrates that Regice was not merely a novelty with one enormous number—it was an actual OU special pivot with an offensive edge.
nuzlocke: Regice can be exceptionally safe against known special attackers because base 200 Special Defense is so high that even many neutral special moves become manageable. Clear Body protects its stats, while Ice Beam provides strong and accurate offense against Dragons, Flying-types, Grass-types, and Ground-types. The danger is physical coverage and typing: Fighting, Rock, Fire, and Steel attacks can overwhelm Regice quickly, and pure Ice does little to provide safe resistance-based switching. Its base 50 Speed means it usually cannot escape a bad matchup by attacking first, so the player should use Regice as a targeted special sponge rather than simply sending it into anything special-looking. When the opponent's coverage is known, few Hoenn Pokemon can absorb special damage as reliably.

pokemon.name: Regice
pokemon.biologyAndBehavior: Regice is composed of solid ice formed during an ancient ice age, and the material is so deeply frozen that even immersion in molten magma cannot melt its body. It constantly surrounds itself with air at roughly minus 328 degrees Fahrenheit, or minus 200 degrees Celsius, cold enough to freeze nearby living creatures simply by proximity. Pokédex research identifies the body material with Antarctic or South Pole ice and suggests that Regice may have slept inside a glacier for thousands of years before being discovered. Legend says Regigigas created it from ice of the ice age, after which ancient people worshipped and later sealed it away out of fear. Regice is therefore less a creature wearing ice armor than an animate remnant of a prehistoric glacial environment whose body still maintains temperatures far beyond ordinary natural cold.
pokemon.description: Regice is an Ice-type Pokémon introduced in Generation III, with a base stat total of 580 and no standard evolutions.

playthrough: Registeel is the most evenly defensive of the original three legendary giants, combining base 150 Defense and 150 Special Defense with pure Steel typing and base 80 HP. Its offenses are only base 75 on both sides and Speed is just 50, so its main value comes from surviving attacks, spreading status, setting Stealth Rock in later generations, and using fixed-damage or utility moves rather than attempting to sweep. Clear Body prevents opposing stat reductions and preserves its defensive consistency, while the later Hidden Ability Light Metal halves its weight but is generally much less impactful in ordinary story play. Before Generation VI, Steel's resistance to Dark and Ghost made Registeel's defensive profile even more extreme; modern Steel remains excellent but leaves Fire, Fighting, and Ground as dangerous weaknesses while Dark and Ghost are now neutral. Registeel works best as a mixed wall that repeatedly pivots into resisted attacks and supports the rest of the team, though lack of reliable instant recovery can make long routes and repeated boss battles wear it down.
competitive: Registeel debuted in ADV UUBL but possessed a genuine OU niche as a mixed wall, using pure Steel typing and 150 defenses on both sides to pivot into a huge range of attacks. Thunder Wave, Toxic, Seismic Toss, Counter, Curse, and Explosion gave it ways to create progress even though its direct offensive stats were modest, while immunity to sandstorm and Clear Body made it difficult to wear down through several common ADV mechanics. Later generations strengthened the support identity through Stealth Rock, allowing Registeel to compress hazard setting, status, and mixed walling into one slot and become a recurring staple of several lower-tier metagames. Its main flaws are passivity, low Speed, common Fire-, Fighting-, and Ground-type weaknesses, and the lack of reliable instant recovery, which means repeated chip eventually defeats it even when individual attacks do not. Unlike Regirock and Regice, Registeel's defining strength is not one extreme defensive stat but the ability to remain very difficult to break from either attacking side.
nuzlocke: Registeel is one of the safest late-game defensive Pokemon a Nuzlocke can offer because 150 in both defenses and pure Steel typing create a huge number of predictable resistances. Clear Body prevents random stat drops from eroding those defenses, and status support can make dangerous opponents easier for the entire team to manage. The biggest threats are Fire, Fighting, and Ground moves, which are common enough that Registeel should never be treated as invulnerable simply because the health bar falls slowly against neutral attacks. Its low Speed means it usually absorbs damage before acting, and without dependable instant recovery every hit matters across a long sequence of battles. When used as a planned resistance-based pivot rather than a universal wall, Registeel offers an unusually high margin for error.

pokemon.name: Registeel
pokemon.biologyAndBehavior: Registeel's body is completely hollow yet made from a mysterious metallic substance harder than any known conventional metal, while somehow remaining flexible enough to stretch and shrink. The material is said to have been tempered by immense underground pressure for tens of thousands of years until the surface became effectively impossible to scratch. Some traditions claim Registeel formed deep inside the planet's mantle and emerged onto the surface about 10,000 years ago, while the legendary-giant myth instead says Regigigas created it from magma. No one knows what Registeel eats—or whether a hollow being made from unknown metal needs food in any recognizable biological sense. Ancient people once worshipped the Pokemon before fearing its power and sealing it away, leaving modern researchers with a living metallic object whose origin, nutrition, and internal functioning remain largely unexplained.
pokemon.description: Registeel is a Steel-type Pokémon introduced in Generation III, with a base stat total of 580 and no standard evolutions.

playthrough: Latias is the more defensively oriented member of the Eon duo, with base 110 Speed, 110 Special Attack, 130 Special Defense, good overall bulk, and Levitate for a complete Ground immunity. Dragon/Psychic provides useful resistances to Fire, Water, Grass, Electric, Fighting, and Psychic, while Recover, Calm Mind, Psychic or Mist Ball, Dragon attacks, healing support, and broad coverage make Latias both durable and flexible. Generation III's Dragon attacks are special, which naturally fits its Special Attack, while the original Soul Dew dramatically amplifies Special Attack and Special Defense in formats where the old effect is active and makes the Eon twins far stronger than their base stats imply. From Generation VI, Fairy joins Ice, Dragon, Bug, Ghost, and Dark as a weakness, but Latias remains extremely useful because Speed, recovery, resistances, and Levitate let it enter many battles safely. Mega Latias keeps Dragon/Psychic and Levitate while raising Defense to 120, Special Attack to 140, and Special Defense to 150, creating an exceptionally durable Calm Mind or support Pokemon that can still threaten meaningful damage.
competitive: Latias was an ADV Uber and one of the tier's premier answers to Kyogre and Groudon, using Levitate, Recover, Calm Mind, excellent special bulk, and the original Soul Dew's 1.5x Special Attack and Special Defense boosts. Compared with Latios, Latias trades some immediate offensive power for greater Defense and Special Defense, which made it particularly valuable as a long-term weather-legend check that could repeatedly recover and remain useful throughout a battle. In later generations where the Eon twins could participate in standard tiers under changed item rules, Latias repeatedly found high-level niches as a fast defensive pivot, Defog user, Healing Wish supporter, Calm Mind sweeper, or Choice user. Mega Latias became a notable OU threat in Generation VII, where 80/120/150 defenses, base 110 Speed, Calm Mind, Roost or Recover, and excellent coverage let it become exceptionally difficult to wear down. Its recurring limitations are Pursuit or Dark pressure in older formats, weaknesses to Ice, Dragon, Ghost, Bug, Dark, and later Fairy, and competition with Latios when raw damage matters more than longevity.
nuzlocke: Latias is an exceptionally forgiving Nuzlocke legendary because good mixed bulk, base 130 Special Defense, Recover, and Levitate give it far more safe switching opportunities than most fast attackers. A Ground immunity plus resistances to several common elemental types can create completely safe entry points when opposing movesets are known. The main dangers are strong Ice, Dragon, Ghost, Dark, Bug, and later Fairy attacks, especially physical ones that target Latias's lower Defense. Mega Latias improves the physical side substantially and can make Calm Mind or recovery-based strategies extremely reliable, but setup should still be reserved for opponents without dangerous critical-hit or super-effective coverage. Availability is often late or version-dependent, but whenever Latias is legitimately obtainable during a run it provides one of the best combinations of speed, recovery, and defensive safety in Hoenn.

pokemon.name: Latias
pokemon.biologyAndBehavior: Latias is an extremely intelligent, gentle aerial Pokemon capable of understanding human speech and communicating telepathically while normally avoiding direct contact with people. Its downy, glass-like feathers refract light around the body, allowing Latias to become invisible or alter its appearance; several canon depictions even show it disguising itself as a human girl. It reacts strongly to hostility, ruffling its feathers and crying loudly when threatened, but generally prefers to disappear rather than fight and may live in small herds near water. Latias can also share visual information with others in some depictions, allowing another being to see what Latios is seeing. Mega Latias greatly increases flight performance: it is described as capable of reaching around Mach 4 and is smaller and more agile than Mega Latios, allowing exceptionally sharp turns at extreme speed.
pokemon.description: Latias is a Dragon/Psychic-type Pokémon introduced in Generation III, with a base stat total of 600 and no standard evolutions.

playthrough: Latios is the more offensively oriented Eon Pokemon, combining base 130 Special Attack, 110 Special Defense, and 110 Speed with Dragon/Psychic typing and Levitate.
