Later Contrary sets can end fights rapidly with repeated Leaf Storm boosts, but Leaf Storm is only 90 percent accurate and therefore introduces a failure chance that matters under permadeath rules; a more reliable Grass move can be safer when no boost is needed. Glare is valuable in later games because it provides accurate paralysis even against many targets that resist Grass, but Serperior still has five common weaknesses and should not be treated as a universal tank. Timid Contrary Serperior is excellent for controlling tempo, while a defensive or Coil-oriented Serperior can be safer in generations where the Hidden Ability is unavailable.

pokemon.name: Snivy
pokemon.biologyAndBehavior: Snivy performs photosynthesis through the large leaf at the end of its tail, gaining energy that improves its speed and physical performance. The tail visibly droops when Snivy is low on energy, making it a clear external indicator of the Pokemon's condition. Because its arms are short, Snivy compensates by manipulating vines with exceptional dexterity. It is intelligent, calm, and generally solitary, preferring to avoid groups when possible.

pokemon.name: Servine
pokemon.biologyAndBehavior: Servine performs photosynthesis through the leaves growing along its body, but those leaves only work efficiently when kept clean, so it goes to considerable effort to avoid dirt. It uses speed and concealment rather than brute force, hiding in thick foliage or shadows to evade an attack before retaliating with its vines. Servine is extremely proud and can have difficulty cooperating with other Pokemon because of that temperament. Individual behavior therefore combines careful maintenance of its plant structures with a more aggressive and independent social attitude than Snivy.

pokemon.name: Serperior
pokemon.biologyAndBehavior: Serperior has lost the functional legs of its earlier stages and moves primarily by slithering, while the small leaf-like forelimbs near its neck are normally held folded behind its body. It can amplify solar energy internally and uses its imposing posture and piercing gaze to intimidate opponents, with Pokédex accounts claiming the stare alone can halt an enemy's movement. Serperior deliberately withholds its full strength from opponents that are already intimidated and only fights at maximum effort against foes that remain unfazed. This regal behavior and commanding presence have earned it the title 'Lord of the Forest.'

playthrough: Tepig evolves into Fire/Fighting Pignite at level 17 and then into Emboar at level 36, producing a slow but extremely strong mixed attacker with base 110 HP, 123 Attack, and 100 Special Attack. In the original Unova games the line uses Blaze, while its later Hidden Ability Reckless increases the power of recoil or crash moves by 20 percent and turns attacks such as Flare Blitz, Wild Charge, Head Smash, and other compatible options into even more extreme wallbreaking tools. Fighting STAB from Arm Thrust, Brick Break, Hammer Arm, Superpower, or other generation-specific moves combines well with Fire attacks, while Grass Knot, Scald in older movepools, Rock coverage, and Electric coverage can punish many conventional answers. The weaknesses are equally clear: base 65 Speed means Emboar is frequently hit before attacking, base 65 defenses are mediocre despite the huge HP stat, and many of its strongest attacks cause recoil or stat drops. Adamant maximizes physical damage, Jolly can salvage selected Speed matchups, and Brave or Quiet can support mixed or Trick Room strategies. Mega Emboar, introduced in Pokémon Legends: Z-A, remains Fire/Fighting but rises to base 148 Attack, 110 Special Attack, 110 Special Defense, and 75 Speed with a 628 total; in ability-enabled data it gains Mold Breaker, creating a much stronger and more specially durable version of the same aggressive concept.
competitive: Standard Emboar entered competitive play as a BW RU wallbreaker, where base 123 Attack, Fire/Fighting STAB, 110 HP, and coverage such as Wild Charge, Head Smash, and Grass Knot gave it ways to pressure the bulky Water-, Rock-, and Flying-types that attempted to stop its primary attacks. Smogon noted that it competed with established Fire-types such as Entei and Moltres, but Fighting STAB, neutrality to Stealth Rock, resistance to Sucker Punch, and the ability to attack from either side gave Emboar a distinct niche. The later release of Reckless sharpened that role by boosting several of the already powerful recoil moves in its arsenal, and SM placed Emboar in NUBL while it remained a dangerous RU wallbreaker despite competition from faster or more specialized Fighting- and Fire-types. Modern SV Smogon places standard Emboar in ZUBL, where it still succeeds by forcing progress with extremely strong attacks rather than through Speed or defensive consistency. Mega Emboar is too new to assign a mature historical tier résumé, but its confirmed 148 Attack, sharply improved Special Defense, and Mold Breaker in ability-enabled mechanics give it substantially better raw tools; any claim that it has already established the same kind of long competitive history as standard Emboar would be premature.
nuzlocke: Emboar's huge base 110 HP can absorb more punishment than its 65/65 defenses suggest, but its low base 65 Speed means it often takes that damage before getting to use its enormous Attack. The line's strongest moves are a major permadeath concern: Flare Blitz, Wild Charge, and Head Smash inflict recoil, Superpower lowers offensive and defensive stats, and Reckless makes recoil-based attacks even more powerful without making them any safer. Blaze can therefore be the more comfortable story ability even when Reckless is technically stronger, because ordinary reliable Fire and Fighting moves already benefit from Emboar's high Attack and do not require deliberately spending HP. Water, Ground, Psychic, and Flying attacks should be treated cautiously, especially from fast special attackers that target its mediocre Special Defense. Mega Emboar's much higher Special Defense and Attack improve the safety margin substantially where available, but it is still not fast and remains weak to the same four types; Adamant standard Emboar or a bulkier Mega can be excellent boss breakers when recoil is reserved for situations where it is genuinely necessary.

pokemon.name: Tepig
pokemon.biologyAndBehavior: Tepig is surprisingly nimble for its round build and uses quick movement to dodge and confuse opponents before counterattacking. It breathes fire through its snout, but when sick it produces thick black smoke instead of healthy flame. Tepig has an excellent sense of smell and an enormous appetite, often locating food and roasting Berries before eating them; it can become so excited that it accidentally burns the food. The condition of its fire therefore provides a visible indication of health in much the same way as several other Fire-type first partners.

pokemon.name: Pignite
pokemon.biologyAndBehavior: Pignite maintains a fire inside its stomach and feeds that flame with the food it eats. Adding fuel or becoming angry makes the internal fire burn hotter, raising its body temperature and increasing its speed; at extreme intensity the body can become surrounded by a scorching fireball. When its stomach is empty, however, Pignite loses much of its strength because the fire has little fuel. It is fiercely protective of its friends and will confront opponents far stronger than itself to defend them. If escape is necessary, Pignite can release thick clouds of smoke to conceal its retreat.

pokemon.name: Emboar
pokemon.biologyAndBehavior: Emboar's internal body flame erupts around its neck and shoulders as a permanent fiery beard, and it can spread that fire over its hands before using powerful fighting techniques. The more dangerous the situation becomes, the more excited Emboar appears to grow, with the neck flame intensifying alongside its power and speed. It is relentless in battle but deeply affectionate toward individuals it considers friends, so the aggressive fighting style does not translate into indiscriminate hostility. Emboar can also expel large blasts of fire directly from its nose and cloak its body in flames for attacks.

pokemon.name: Emboar
pokemon.biologyAndBehavior: Mega Evolution greatly increases both Emboar's muscular power and fire output, causing the flaming beard to spread across the upper body like protective armor. It shapes fire emitted from its palms into a long serpentine spear and fights with that weapon while its emotions remain constantly heightened. Mega Emboar becomes more independent and reckless, repeatedly challenging enemies and sometimes taking battles too far, but it retains such a strong sense of duty that it will risk its life to rescue a threatened friend. The tip of its flame spear can reach roughly 18,000 degrees Fahrenheit, and official descriptions state that one punch from its enhanced muscles can destroy about half of a reinforced concrete building.

playthrough: Oshawott evolves into Dewott at level 17 and Samurott at level 36, producing a pure Water final evolution with base 95 HP, 100 Attack, 108 Special Attack, and enough movepool breadth to function physically, specially, or as a mixed attacker. Surf or Hydro Pump, Razor Shell, Aqua Jet, Ice Beam, Grass Knot, Megahorn, Swords Dance, and other coverage make standard Samurott difficult to shut down with a single defensive answer, although base 70 Speed and 70 Special Defense keep it from being especially fast or bulky. Torrent is the ordinary ability, while the Hidden Ability Shell Armor completely prevents critical hits and is particularly valuable in story or Nuzlocke play; like the other Unova starter Hidden Abilities, Shell Armor Samurott was not officially distributed until Generation VI in 2015. In Hisui, Dewott evolves into Water/Dark Hisuian Samurott instead, gaining base 108 Attack and 85 Speed plus the signature Ceaseless Edge; in modern turn-based mechanics Ceaseless Edge both deals damage and sets Spikes, while the Hidden Ability Sharpness boosts slicing moves such as Ceaseless Edge, Razor Shell, Aqua Cutter, and Sacred Sword. Modest or Timid can suit special standard Samurott, Adamant or Jolly support physical sets, and Hisuian Samurott generally prefers physical investment because Sharpness and its signature Dark STAB reward that approach.
competitive: Standard Samurott established itself as a strong BW NU Water-type because its 100 Attack and 108 Special Attack allowed physical Swords Dance, special, and mixed sets to punish very different counters. Smogon emphasized that unpredictability as its main advantage: Hydro Pump, Ice Beam, and Grass Knot could break common physical answers, while Swords Dance plus Aqua Jet and physical Water STAB threatened offensive teams and faster revenge killers. Samurott remained one of SM NU's better offensive Water-types for the same reason, although mediocre base 70 Speed and competition from faster or bulkier Water-types kept it from climbing into sustained upper-tier play. Hisuian Samurott completely changed the family's competitive ceiling in Generation IX and is currently an OU Pokemon, largely because Ceaseless Edge can attack while simultaneously setting Spikes; this bypasses much of the normal tempo cost of laying hazards and makes every successful attack advance both immediate and long-term pressure. Sharpness further boosts Ceaseless Edge and other slicing moves, while Knock Off, Aqua Jet, Sucker Punch, Flip Turn, and Sacred Sword give it additional utility, making Hisuian Samurott one of the most influential hazard setters introduced in modern OU.
nuzlocke: The Oshawott line is a dependable Nuzlocke starter because Water typing leaves only Grass and Electric weaknesses and the family evolves at the reasonable levels 17 and 36. Standard Samurott's mixed offenses allow the player to use whatever reliable Water and coverage moves the run provides, and Aqua Jet can safely finish weakened opponents before they retaliate. Shell Armor is one of the best possible Nuzlocke abilities when legitimately available because it removes critical hits entirely, eliminating a major source of unexpected deaths; in the original Black and White games, however, an ordinary starter will have Torrent instead. Hisuian Samurott gains several additional weaknesses from its Water/Dark typing but also receives a Psychic immunity, increased Speed, and a much more aggressive physical toolkit; Ceaseless Edge is useful because setting hazards no longer requires spending a completely passive turn. Razor Shell's imperfect accuracy and defense-drop variability should still be considered, and Sharpness boosts damage without creating recoil, making physical Hisuian Samurott safer than many other high-output attackers when the matchup is known.

pokemon.name: Oshawott
pokemon.biologyAndBehavior: Oshawott carries a detachable shell called a scalchop on its belly, made from the same material as its claws. It uses the scalchop as both a knife and a shield, blocking an incoming attack before immediately retaliating with a slash, and also uses it to break open hard Berries. Oshawott maintains the blade by rubbing it against riverbed stones after observing humans sharpen tools on whetstones. If the scalchop is badly damaged or lost, a replacement can grow from the navel.

pokemon.name: Dewott
pokemon.biologyAndBehavior: Dewott carries two detachable scalchops and follows a strict daily training routine to master fighting with both at once. Individual Dewott develop different scalchop techniques rather than all using an identical style, and they carefully maintain each blade as part of that discipline. Their flowing two-blade movements can defeat skilled swordsmen, and Pokédex accounts say humans actually modeled swordplay on the motions of Dewott. The species is stern, studious, and defined more by repeated practice than by instinctive aggression.

pokemon.name: Samurott
pokemon.biologyAndBehavior: Samurott fights with large shell blades called seamitars attached to its forelegs and can rise onto its hind limbs when drawing them. Its sword-drawing technique is based on iaijutsu: Samurott can draw, strike, and sheathe a seamitar in the time it takes an opponent to blink, and a single swing is said to be capable of felling a foe. It leads groups through strict discipline and can silence opponents with a glare or howl. Unlike its Hisuian counterpart, standard Samurott is generally characterized as a straightforward fighter that prefers honorable combat.

pokemon.name: Samurott
pokemon.biologyAndBehavior: Hisuian Samurott developed in the harsher environment of ancient Hisui, gaining darker shell armor, curved seamitars, longer wavy whiskers, and a much colder temperament than the Unovan form. It remains perfectly still until an opening appears, then draws its blades almost instantaneously and relies on tricks, surprise attacks, and other underhanded tactics rather than fair combat. Its repeated slashing attacks are compared to ceaseless waves that confuse and overwhelm the target, and wounds inflicted by its blades are said to take many years to heal. The environmental change therefore alters both anatomy and behavior: Hisuian Samurott is not merely darker in color but a more deceptive and opportunistic predator-fighter.

playthrough: Patrat evolves into Watchog at level 20, giving the player a fully evolved Normal-type very early but only modest final statistics: Watchog has base 85 Attack, 77 Speed, and 60/69/69 bulk. Its main story value comes from utility rather than raw power, with moves such as Super Fang, Hypnosis, Crunch, Low Kick, Seed Bomb, and reliable Normal STAB allowing it to weaken or disable targets that stronger teammates can finish. Keen Eye prevents accuracy reduction, Illuminate has no in-battle effect in the original Generation V games, and the Hidden Ability Analytic boosts attacks when Watchog moves after its target, though deliberately relying on moving second is awkward on a Pokemon with mediocre defenses. Super Fang is especially useful because it removes half of the target's current HP regardless of Watchog's attacking stats, while Hypnosis can create free turns but its 60 percent accuracy makes it unreliable. Adamant is the simplest offensive nature, but Watchog is generally most useful as an early-game utility Pokemon that peaks quickly rather than a long-term centerpiece.
competitive: Watchog has never developed a meaningful high-tier competitive niche. Smogon places it in BW ZU, where its base 85 Attack and broad physical coverage can support a wallbreaking set using Normal STAB, Low Kick, Knock Off or Crunch, and Seed Bomb, while Analytic can provide a 30 percent damage boost when Watchog moves after the opponent. The problem is that 60/69/69 bulk is poor, base 77 Speed is neither fast enough to consistently attack first nor slow enough to exploit Analytic safely, and stronger Normal-types such as Stoutland and Ursaring usually perform the same offensive role with better numbers. Later analyses remained similarly negative, with Watchog still restricted to very low-tier wallbreaking or novelty utility. Its competitive value therefore comes from specific tools such as Super Fang, Hypnosis, and coverage rather than from a stat profile that supports sustained success.
nuzlocke: Patrat is easy to obtain and reaches its final evolution at level 20, so Watchog can provide useful early-game power before many encounters have fully evolved. Super Fang is one of its safest high-value tools because it guarantees substantial progress against bulky enemies without depending on Watchog's mediocre Attack, while Crunch and Normal STAB give reliable damage in ordinary matchups. Hypnosis is tempting but only 60 percent accurate, making it too unreliable to serve as the primary safety plan in a permadeath battle. Watchog's defenses are not strong enough to absorb repeated neutral hits, and Fighting attacks are super effective, so its early evolution should not be mistaken for long-term durability. It is best used to weaken or finish selected targets rather than being trusted as a general-purpose pivot once stronger teammates become available.

pokemon.name: Patrat
pokemon.biologyAndBehavior: Patrat stores food in large cheek pouches so it can remain on watch for long periods without leaving its post. Groups maintain constant surveillance of their nest by taking turns as sentries, and individuals become uneasy when no lookout is present. Patrat raises its long tail to signal that it has spotted an enemy and uses the tail to communicate with others. Its vigilance has a blind spot, however: Pokédex records specifically note that a Patrat focused forward may fail to notice an opponent approaching from behind.

pokemon.name: Watchog
pokemon.biologyAndBehavior: Watchog contains luminescent compounds that allow the yellow markings on its body and its eyes to glow, and it uses the illumination to threaten predators in dark environments. Its vision is adapted for nighttime observation, allowing it to monitor its surroundings after sunset. Watchog also stores large quantities of seeds in its cheeks and can spit those seeds at opponents as projectiles.

playthrough: Lillipup evolves into Herdier at level 16 and Stoutland at level 32, making the family one of Unova's most dependable early-route choices because it reaches strong middle and final stages at reasonable levels. In Generation V Stoutland has base 100 Attack, which was increased to 110 from Generation VI onward, alongside solid 85 HP, 90 Defense, and 90 Special Defense; Return in older games, Strength, Crunch, elemental fangs, Wild Charge, Superpower, and later Play Rough provide broad physical coverage. Intimidate is usually the safest all-purpose ability because lowering an opponent's Attack on entry creates immediate defensive value, while Sand Rush doubles Speed in sand and can transform base 80 Speed into a sweeping advantage; the Hidden Ability Scrappy lets Normal- and Fighting-type attacks hit Ghost Pokemon. Lillipup's early Pickup can also generate useful held items during a playthrough, although its ability changes when it evolves. Adamant is an excellent straightforward nature for Stoutland, while Jolly can improve matchups outside sand, and the combination of early availability, good bulk, strong Attack, and useful abilities makes this one of the better regional Normal families for ordinary play.
competitive: Stoutland developed a legitimate competitive niche because Sand Rush doubles its Speed in sand, turning an otherwise middling base 80 Speed stat into elite speed control. Smogon currently classifies it in BW PU, where Choice Band plus Return, Crunch, Superpower, and coverage makes it a strong wallbreaker, while historical sand teams also used Stoutland as a revenge killer capable of outrunning even many Choice Scarf users once sand was active. In later generations its Attack rose from 100 to 110, improving the damage output of the same basic strategy, and it found additional sand niches in NU and UU when paired with setters such as Hippowdon or Gigalith. Intimidate and Scrappy offer useful alternatives, but Sand Rush is the ability that defines Stoutland's competitive identity because without sand its Speed and pure Normal typing are much less impressive. Rock- and Steel-types, Fighting priority, and dependence on a weather-setting teammate have consistently prevented it from becoming a broadly splashable upper-tier attacker.
nuzlocke: The Lillipup line is excellent in Nuzlockes because it is available early, evolves quickly, and becomes a genuinely bulky fully evolved Pokemon at level 32. Intimidate is particularly valuable under permadeath rules because every switch into a physical opponent immediately lowers incoming damage, while Scrappy can remove uncertainty around Ghost-type immunities in games where the Hidden Ability is available. Stoutland's 85/90/90 bulk is balanced enough to survive many neutral mistakes, and reliable Normal attacks plus Crunch and broad coverage allow it to finish battles without depending heavily on inaccurate moves or recoil. Fighting attacks remain its only conventional type weakness, and pure Normal provides no normal resistances besides the Ghost immunity, so it should not be used as an indiscriminate switch-in despite its good defenses. Adamant Stoutland with Intimidate is one of the simplest and most dependable ways to use the family in a Nuzlocke.

pokemon.name: Lillipup
pokemon.biologyAndBehavior: Lillipup uses the thick cream-colored fur covering its face as a sensory organ, reading subtle information about its surroundings and an opponent's condition almost like radar. It is unusually intelligent and can judge whether an enemy is too strong to fight, fleeing when necessary rather than confusing courage with recklessness. Lillipup is quiet, obedient, and easy to raise, which makes it popular with beginning Trainers and people living in apartments. It also remembers both affection and mistreatment for a very long time.

pokemon.name: Herdier
pokemon.biologyAndBehavior: Herdier's dense dark fur grows continuously and becomes springy enough to repel claws and fangs that try to penetrate it. The coat provides excellent physical protection but is expensive and difficult to groom, making proper care a significant responsibility for a Trainer. Herdier is intelligent, loyal, and willing to help humans raise other Pokemon, but it refuses to obey people who treat it without respect. Cave-wall evidence has led researchers to theorize that Herdier or its ancestors may have been among the earliest Pokemon to form enduring partnerships with humans.

pokemon.name: Stoutland
pokemon.biologyAndBehavior: Stoutland is famous for rescuing people stranded in blizzards, mountains, and at sea, and its intelligence and calm temperament have made it a trusted partner on rescue teams. Its extremely thick fur can protect both itself and humans from freezing temperatures; older Pokédex records say households in cold regions once commonly kept Stoutland for warmth, and parents have even trusted the species to babysit children. In Alola, Stoutland's powerful sense of smell is used to locate hidden objects as a Ride Pokemon. Stoutland also warms to humans quickly, and within its own species the length of the large mustache is said to determine social standing.

playthrough: Purrloin evolves into Liepard at level 20, producing a very fast Dark-type with base 106 Speed and equal base 88 Attack and Special Attack but frail 64/50/50 defenses. Dark STAB through Crunch, Night Slash, Dark Pulse, or later Knock Off combines with U-turn, Fake Out, Sucker Punch, Play Rough, Seed Bomb, and support such as Encore, Taunt, Thunder Wave, or Nasty Plot depending on the generation. Limber prevents paralysis, Unburden doubles Speed after the held item is consumed or lost, and the Hidden Ability Prankster gives non-damaging moves +1 priority; from Generation VII onward, however, opposing Dark-type Pokemon are immune to Prankster-boosted status moves directed at them. Liepard's Psychic immunity provides one excellent switch opportunity, but its poor defenses mean it is much safer entering through that immunity or after a knockout than taking ordinary neutral attacks. Jolly or Timid can maximize its natural Speed, while Adamant or Modest increase damage, but the line is best understood as a fast utility attacker rather than a durable story battler.
competitive: Liepard was a legitimate BW NU disruptor because Prankster gave priority to an unusually broad set of support moves. Smogon highlighted Encore as the centerpiece: Liepard could lock setup sweepers or defensive Pokemon into a non-damaging move before they acted, then use U-turn to bring in a teammate or combine Encore with Sucker Punch and Pursuit to create difficult prediction loops. Priority Rain Dance, Sunny Day, Taunt, Thunder Wave, and other support options also gave it roles that its unimpressive 88 offenses would not otherwise support. Its base 106 Speed is genuinely good, but 64/50/50 bulk means almost any strong direct hit can KO or severely damage it, and later generations also added the rule that Dark-type targets are immune to Prankster status moves used by an opponent. Liepard therefore earned a real lower-tier niche through disruptive mechanics rather than raw statistics, and its effectiveness depends heavily on prediction and matchup knowledge.
nuzlocke: Liepard's base 106 Speed and Psychic immunity can be useful in a Nuzlocke, but its extremely poor physical and special bulk leaves little margin for mistakes. Prankster can make Encore, Taunt, or Thunder Wave act before faster opponents, creating valuable control without spending health, though Dark-type targets become immune to opposing Prankster status moves from Generation VII onward. Sucker Punch offers priority damage but fails if the opponent does not use an attacking move, so relying on it without knowing the AI's likely choice can create unnecessary risk. Limber is a simple and reliable defensive ability because paralysis cannot remove Liepard's major Speed advantage, while Unburden can create enormous Speed but depends on item management. The family is safest as a fast cleaner or utility specialist brought in through a free switch rather than a Pokemon expected to trade hits.

pokemon.name: Purrloin
pokemon.biologyAndBehavior: Purrloin steals from people for amusement and seems to enjoy the frustration of its victims as much as the objects themselves. It deliberately acts cute and harmless to lower a target's guard, then takes valuables and responds to discovery with scratches and apparent laughter. Its charm is effective enough that people frequently forgive the theft even after catching Purrloin in the act. In Galar, the species has a particularly fierce rivalry with Nickit.

pokemon.name: Liepard
pokemon.biologyAndBehavior: Liepard has highly developed muscles that allow it to move almost silently and attack prey or opponents from behind before they notice its approach. It is elusive enough to seem to vanish and reappear without warning, reinforcing its reputation as a stealth predator. Trainers are often attracted to the species' elegant body and spotted fur despite its moody and vicious temperament. In Galar, Liepard competes with Thievul for territory.

playthrough: Pansage evolves into Simisage with a Leaf Stone rather than by level, and in Black and White a Pansage is given at the Dreamyard if the player chose Tepig, specifically to help against the Striaton Gym matchup. Simisage has identical base 98 Attack and Special Attack plus base 101 Speed, giving it the flexibility to use physical Grass moves such as Seed Bomb, special attacks such as Giga Drain or Energy Ball, or mixed coverage including Superpower, Rock Slide, Acrobatics, Crunch, and other generation-specific options. Because evolution requires a stone, the player should check which useful level-up moves Pansage learns before evolving in games where the evolved form has a more restricted natural learnset; modern move-relearning systems reduce this concern in later titles. Gluttony causes Berries to activate at half HP rather than the usual quarter threshold, while the Hidden Ability Overgrow strengthens Grass attacks at low health. Simisage hits reasonably hard and is fast enough for much of a normal story, but 75/63/63 bulk and five common Grass weaknesses make it much safer as an attacker than as a switch-in; Hasty or Naive work for mixed sets, while Jolly and Timid support purely physical or special approaches.
competitive: Simisage has spent its competitive history in lower tiers, but it is substantially more functional than its reputation sometimes suggests. Smogon places it in BW PU, where base 101 Speed and equal base 98 offenses allow mixed sets using Giga Drain, Superpower, and coverage to threaten a wide range of defensive answers, while Nasty Plot provides a faster route to special sweeping than many competing Grass-types. In SM ZU, Smogon describes Simisage as an extremely effective breaker because its expansive coverage and mixed attacking stats make switching into it difficult, even though stronger or bulkier Grass-types may be easier to fit on teams. Its main problem is defensive: 75/63/63 bulk gives it very few safe entry opportunities, and pure Grass creates five common weaknesses. Simisage therefore has a genuine niche as a fast mixed lower-tier breaker, but its frailty and competition have prevented it from establishing a sustained high-tier role.
nuzlocke: Pansage can be genuinely useful early in Black and White when received alongside a Tepig starter because it is intentionally placed to cover the Water-type Striaton matchup. After evolution, Simisage's base 101 Speed helps it avoid damage by attacking first, and access to both physical and special Grass offense means the player can use whichever reliable moves are available. Its defenses are mediocre and Fire, Ice, Flying, Bug, and Poison attacks are all super effective, so it should not be treated as a bulky Grass-type despite useful Water, Ground, Grass, and Electric resistances. Gluttony can cause healing or defensive Berries to activate earlier, which may occasionally save a run, but deliberately dropping into low HP for Overgrow is much riskier under permadeath rules. The safest approach is to use Simisage as a fast matchup specialist and avoid unnecessary mixed neutral exchanges.

pokemon.name: Pansage
pokemon.biologyAndBehavior: Pansage lives deep in forests and gathers Berries that it shares with its friends rather than keeping all of its food for itself. The leaves growing from the sprout on its head are edible and can relieve exhaustion when consumed. This makes the plant growth on Pansage's body both a personal biological feature and a resource it can provide to other creatures.

pokemon.name: Simisage
pokemon.biologyAndBehavior: Simisage has an ill temper and fights primarily with its long tail, whose leafy end is lined with small sharp barbs. It swings the thorn-covered tail as a bludgeoning weapon when attacking enemies. The leaves growing on its head are extremely bitter.

playthrough: Pansear evolves into Simisear with a Fire Stone, and in Black and White a Pansear is given at the Dreamyard if the player chose Oshawott, providing an immediate answer to the Grass-type Striaton Gym matchup. Simisear has base 98 Attack, 98 Special Attack, and 101 Speed, allowing physical, special, or mixed offense through Flamethrower or Fire Blast, Fire Punch, Acrobatics, Crunch, Superpower, Focus Blast, Grass Knot, Nasty Plot, and other coverage depending on generation. As with the other elemental monkeys, stone evolution can make move timing important in older games, so it can be worthwhile to let Pansear learn desired level-up attacks before using the Fire Stone. Gluttony activates held Berries at half HP, while the Hidden Ability Blaze strengthens Fire attacks at low health. Base 75/63/63 bulk is poor and Fire typing brings Water, Ground, and Rock weaknesses, so Simisear is best used to exploit its Speed and offensive coverage rather than attempting to absorb attacks; Timid or Jolly maximize Speed while Modest, Adamant, or mixed natures emphasize damage.
competitive: Simisear has remained a lower-tier offensive Pokemon throughout its history, but its base 101 Speed and equal base 98 offenses give it enough flexibility to be a legitimate threat in those environments. BW lower-tier analyses use it as a special attacker, Choice Scarf speed-control option, or Nasty Plot sweeper with Fire STAB and Fighting-, Grass-, or Dark-type coverage, while later XY Smogon placed it around ZUBL and described it as a threatening special sweeper and wallbreaker. Its mixed stats allow physical coverage to punish opponents expecting only special attacks, and Nasty Plot can quickly turn otherwise moderate Special Attack into serious breaking power. The consistent problem is frailty: 75/63/63 defenses, weakness to Stealth Rock, and common Water, Ground, and Rock attacks mean Simisear rarely receives many opportunities to enter or set up. It has therefore remained a viable but replaceable lower-tier attacker rather than an established high-level competitive staple.
nuzlocke: Pansear can be especially useful in Black and White when paired with an Oshawott starter because the Dreamyard gift is deliberately intended to cover Oshawott's difficult Grass-type Striaton matchup. Simisear's base 101 Speed gives it a good chance to act before ordinary story opponents, and reliable Fire STAB is valuable against Grass, Bug, Ice, and Steel Pokemon. Its defensive stats are poor enough that Water, Ground, and Rock coverage can become fatal quickly, so bringing it in through a free switch is safer than asking it to absorb even neutral attacks repeatedly. Gluttony can trigger healing Berries earlier, while Blaze offers extra power at low HP but should not be activated deliberately in a permadeath run unless the situation is tightly controlled. Flamethrower or another accurate Fire move is usually safer than relying on Fire Blast when the extra power is unnecessary.

pokemon.name: Pansear
pokemon.biologyAndBehavior: Pansear carries a flame inside the tuft on its head that can exceed 600 degrees Fahrenheit, and the fire burns more intensely when the Pokemon becomes angry. It lives in both forests and volcanic caves and is intelligent enough to roast Berries before eating them. Its natural behavior therefore combines a high-temperature internal fire with deliberate food preparation rather than uncontrolled burning.

pokemon.name: Simisear
pokemon.biologyAndBehavior: Simisear loves sweet foods and converts the energy from those foods into fuel for the flame burning inside its body. When it becomes excited, its body temperature rises and embers begin lifting from both the head tuft and the flame-shaped tail. It can scatter those embers directly at opponents as an attack.

name: Leafeon
biologyAndBehavior: Leafeon's fur contains cells that behave more like plant cells than ordinary animal tissue, allowing it to obtain energy through photosynthesis rather than relying entirely on food. While resting in sunlight it also purifies the surrounding air, and it is commonly described as a peaceful Pokemon that prefers avoiding combat. When friends are threatened, however, Leafeon can harden and sharpen its leaf-like tail into a cutting weapon whose edge is said to exceed that of a manufactured sword and can sever a large tree in a single strike. Its biology therefore combines an unusually passive, plantlike lifestyle with formidable defensive weaponry used primarily when protection is necessary.
playthrough: Leafeon combines excellent 130 Defense with 110 Attack and respectable 95 Speed, giving it an unusual mixture of physical durability and offensive pressure. Strong physical Grass STAB such as Leaf Blade lets it handle Water-, Ground-, and Rock-types effectively while taking physical attacks much better than its appearance might suggest. Its primary limitations are pure Grass typing, weak 65 Special Defense, and a relatively shallow coverage movepool, leaving it vulnerable to numerous common types and special coverage attacks. Its usefulness also depends on team composition, since Grass starters and other readily available Grass-types can make spending Eevee on Leafeon redundant.
competitive: Leafeon's 130 Defense, 110 Attack, and 95 Speed allow it to function as either a physically defensive Pokemon or an offensive threat, but its pure Grass typing and limited coverage restrict both roles. It can check certain physical Ground-, Water-, and Grass-type attackers while still threatening opponents with its respectable Attack rather than becoming completely passive. Chlorophyll provides an alternative offensive niche by doubling its Speed in sun, allowing Leafeon to operate as a fast physical sweeper when supported by the appropriate weather. Competition from Grass-types with better secondary typings, coverage, abilities, or utility has generally kept Leafeon from establishing itself consistently in higher competitive tiers.
nuzlocke: Leafeon's 130 Defense gives it excellent safety against known physical attackers, particularly Water-, Ground-, and Rock-types that it can also threaten with strong Grass STAB. Its 95 Speed and 110 Attack are valuable because Leafeon does not have to rely entirely on defensive stalling and can often remove favorable opponents quickly. However, its 65 Special Defense and numerous Grass weaknesses make unexpected special coverage particularly dangerous, especially in blind runs where enemy movesets are unknown. Leafeon consequently performs best when encounters can be planned in advance and its strong physical matchups can be exploited without exposing it to special Fire-, Ice-, Flying-, Bug-, or Poison-type attacks.
description: Leafeon is a Grass-type Pokémon introduced in Generation IV and a final stage of its evolution line, with a base stat total of 525.

name: Glaceon
biologyAndBehavior: Glaceon can deliberately lower its body temperature to approximately -75 degrees Fahrenheit, freezing its fur into needle-like icicles that can be fired at threats or prey. The same temperature control allows it to freeze atmospheric moisture almost instantly, producing ice crystals, diamond-dust flurries, and powdery snow. It can even surround food with ice pellets, while its frozen fur serves as protection when it sleeps. The glittering snowfall it creates is beautiful enough to distract observers before they realize they are being frozen, and humans make practical use of Glaceon's snow-producing ability at ski resorts.
playthrough: Glaceon's 130 Special Attack makes its Ice-type attacks extremely powerful, giving it strong offensive matchups against Dragon-, Flying-, Grass-, and Ground-types that can become especially valuable late in many games. Contrary to its reputation as a conventional glass cannon, 110 Defense and 95 Special Defense give it respectable raw defenses, but 65 HP, 65 Speed, and pure Ice typing make that bulk difficult to exploit consistently. Its low Speed frequently forces it to absorb an attack before retaliating, while weaknesses to Fire, Fighting, Rock, and Steel expose it to several common offensive types. Availability has also historically hurt Glaceon's playthrough value, as some games place the location or method required to evolve Eevee into Glaceon very late in the main story.
competitive: Glaceon functions primarily as a slow special wallbreaker, using its enormous 130 Special Attack to threaten heavy damage with moves such as Ice Beam and Blizzard. Freeze-Dry significantly improves its offensive profile in later generations by allowing an Ice-type attack to hit Water-types super effectively, reducing one of the traditional limitations of relying heavily on Ice STAB. Its respectable defensive stats are undermined by pure Ice typing, low Speed, entry-hazard vulnerability in relevant generations, and limited coverage, making it difficult to position safely against offensive teams. Glaceon can be extremely threatening once given an opportunity to attack, but faster and more versatile special wallbreakers generally provide similar damage with fewer structural weaknesses.
nuzlocke: Glaceon's powerful Ice STAB can provide an important answer to dangerous Dragons and other Ice-weak bosses, and its 110 Defense means it can survive many neutral physical attacks better than its reputation suggests. The problem is that pure Ice typing provides very little defensive utility while creating weaknesses to several common attacking types, and its 65 Speed means Glaceon often has to withstand a hit before acting. This makes matchup knowledge especially important: against a known Ice-weak opponent without dangerous coverage, Glaceon can be an excellent specialist, while unexpected Fighting-, Rock-, Steel-, or Fire-type attacks can make it risky. Late evolution availability in some games further reduces its Nuzlocke value because Eevee may need to remain unevolved for a significant portion of the run.
description: Glaceon is an Ice-type Pokémon introduced in Generation IV and a final stage of its evolution line, with a base stat total of 525.

playthrough: Panpour evolves into Simipour with a Water Stone, and in Black and White a Panpour is given at the Dreamyard if the player chose Snivy, specifically providing a Water-type answer to the Fire-type Striaton Gym matchup. Simipour has base 98 Attack, 98 Special Attack, and 101 Speed, letting it use physical Waterfall, special Surf or Scald, or mixed coverage such as Ice Beam, Crunch, Low Kick, Grass Knot, and Acrobatics depending on the game. Nasty Plot gives special sets a way to turn the otherwise merely good base 98 Special Attack into serious sweeping power. Gluttony causes Berries to activate at half HP rather than the normal quarter threshold, while the Hidden Ability Torrent strengthens Water attacks at low health. Because evolution requires a Water Stone, move timing can matter in older games where stone-evolved Pokemon learn fewer moves naturally, so it may be worthwhile to let Panpour learn desired attacks before evolving; Timid or Jolly preserve Simipour's excellent Speed, while Modest or Adamant increase damage.
competitive: Simipour has remained a lower-tier offensive Pokemon, but its base 101 Speed and equal base 98 offenses give it more flexibility than many similarly ranked Water-types. BW competitive analyses describe it as capable of physical, special, or mixed offense, with Water STAB backed by Ice Beam, Grass Knot, Crunch, Low Kick, and other coverage, although its 75/63/63 bulk makes it easy to revenge kill. It faced heavy competition from stronger Water-types such as Samurott and Carracosta in Generation V, with Speed being the main characteristic that distinguished it. By SM, Smogon still placed Simipour in ZU but described it as one of the tier's stronger special wallbreakers because Nasty Plot, Hydro Pump, Ice Beam, Focus Blast, and base 101 Speed could overwhelm slower defensive teams. Its ceiling has always been limited by poor bulk, imperfectly accurate strongest attacks, and competition from Water-types with better raw power, defenses, or utility, but it is a legitimate fast lower-tier breaker rather than a completely unviable elemental monkey.
nuzlocke: Panpour is especially useful in Black and White when received alongside a Snivy starter because it is deliberately positioned to cover Snivy's difficult Fire-type Striaton matchup. Simipour's base 101 Speed helps it avoid damage by moving first, and Water typing leaves only Grass and Electric weaknesses while resisting Fire, Water, Ice, and Steel. Its defenses are poor enough that strong neutral attacks can still be dangerous, so the line is better used offensively than as a pivot. Waterfall, Surf, or Scald are safer than Hydro Pump when the extra power is unnecessary, and Gluttony can occasionally cause a healing Berry to activate early enough to prevent a death. Nasty Plot can create sweeps but costs a turn on a frail Pokemon, making straightforward attacks preferable when they already secure the knockout.

pokemon.name: Panpour
pokemon.biologyAndBehavior: Panpour stores nutrient-rich water in the crest on its head. It can spray water from the tip of its tail to keep itself damp or to water plants, and it is normally found near natural water sources.

pokemon.name: Simipour
pokemon.biologyAndBehavior: Simipour stores water in the long tufts of hair on its head and gathers additional water with its tail. The plume at the end of that tail can fire water at enough pressure to destroy a concrete wall. It prefers habitats near clean water.

playthrough: Munna evolves into Musharna with a Moon Stone, producing one of Unova's slowest but bulkiest Psychic-types. Musharna has base 116 HP, 85 Defense, 95 Special Defense, and 107 Special Attack but only base 29 Speed, making it an excellent candidate for Trick Room and a poor choice for strategies that depend on naturally moving first. Psychic or Psyshock provides dependable STAB, while Moonlight, Calm Mind, Hypnosis, Thunder Wave, Reflect, Light Screen, Energy Ball, Shadow Ball, and other support or coverage moves let it function as a durable special attacker or team supporter. Synchronize reflects burn, poison, or paralysis back to the opponent that inflicted it, while Forewarn reveals one of the opponent's most powerful moves and can provide useful scouting information; the Hidden Ability Telepathy is primarily valuable in double battles because it protects Musharna from damaging moves used by allies. Because Moon Stone evolution can restrict later natural move learning in older games, players should check Munna's desired level-up moves before evolving; Quiet is excellent under Trick Room, while Modest, Bold, or Calm suit offensive or defensive builds.
competitive: Musharna was a substantial BW-era lower-tier Pokemon rather than merely a slow story Psychic. Its 116/85/95 bulk, base 107 Special Attack, Moonlight, Calm Mind, Heal Bell, Thunder Wave, Baton Pass or support options, and extremely low Speed let it function as a bulky win condition, defensive pivot, or Trick Room setter. In VGC 2011, Smogon identified Musharna as one of the premier Trick Room users because base 29 Speed works in its favor under reversed turn order, while Telepathy lets it safely stand beside allies using moves such as Earthquake, Surf, or Explosion. In singles it also developed a strong NU reputation as a catch-all physical check, with Moonlight giving it reliable recovery and Psychic preventing complete passivity. Dark-, Ghost-, and Bug-type attacks remain serious weaknesses, and competition from Psychic-types such as Reuniclus limits its offensive uniqueness, but Musharna's combination of huge HP, recovery, and genuinely useful special offense gives it a much stronger competitive résumé than many early-Unova Pokemon.
nuzlocke: Musharna is one of the safer early-access Psychic-types for Nuzlockes because 116 HP and solid defenses give it a large margin against neutral attacks, while Moonlight can provide repeatable healing. Its base 29 Speed means it will almost always take a hit before acting outside Trick Room, so Dark, Ghost, and Bug coverage must be identified carefully rather than relying on raw bulk to save every matchup. Forewarn can be unusually valuable under permadeath rules because revealing an opponent's strongest move may expose dangerous coverage before the player commits to a plan, while Synchronize can punish status without requiring a prediction. Hypnosis is too inaccurate to serve as the primary survival strategy, whereas Reflect, Light Screen, Thunder Wave, Calm Mind, or Trick Room provide more controlled forms of support. A Bold or Calm Musharna is particularly forgiving, and Quiet becomes excellent when the team is deliberately built around Trick Room.

pokemon.name: Munna
pokemon.biologyAndBehavior: Munna floats through the air and feeds on the dreams of people and Pokemon. A person whose dream has been eaten forgets its contents, while the mark on Munna's forehead releases Dream Mist that can project what it has consumed. Pleasant dreams produce pink mist and make the flower-like patterns on Munna's body glow with apparent happiness; nightmares create dark mist. Munna can also seek out sleeping beings suffering from nightmares and remove those dreams by eating them.

pokemon.name: Musharna
pokemon.biologyAndBehavior: Musharna continues to feed on dreams and releases Dream Mist from the mark on its forehead, with shapes from consumed dreams appearing inside the mist. The color reflects the nature of the dreams it has eaten, and dark Dream Mist is considered dangerous because nightmares can appear within it. Musharna is effectively always asleep and dreaming even when its eyes are open, and freshly waking one can leave it extremely irritable. Researchers believe Munna and Musharna share a distant common ancestry with Drowzee.

playthrough: Pidove evolves into Tranquill at level 21 and Unfezant at level 32, giving Unova an early regional bird that reaches its final stage at a reasonable point in the story. Unfezant has base 93 Speed and strong physical Attack—105 in Generation V and increased to 115 from Generation VI onward—but its physical Flying movepool has historically been much less impressive than that Attack stat suggests. Fly, Return in older games, Facade, U-turn, Quick Attack, Steel Wing, and later options can still provide useful story damage, while Super Luck raises the critical-hit ratio, Big Pecks prevents Defense drops, and the Hidden Ability Rivalry modifies damage according to the target's gender and is therefore inconsistent. Normal/Flying provides complete Ghost and Ground immunities plus Grass and Bug resistances, while Electric, Ice, and Rock attacks are dangerous. Adamant gives the line more physical power and Jolly preserves Speed, and although Unfezant is perfectly serviceable for the main story, its limited high-quality physical Flying options prevent it from exploiting its statistics as cleanly as regional birds such as Staraptor.
competitive: Unfezant has had a weak competitive history despite respectable-looking Attack and Speed. Smogon places it in BW ZU and explicitly notes that it was badly outclassed in NU because its offensive movepool was exceptionally shallow; even with base 105 Attack, it lacked a strong, dependable physical Flying STAB and often resorted to Return, U-turn, Pluck, Aerial Ace, or support moves. Tailwind, Hypnosis, Taunt, U-turn, and Super Luck provided limited utility, but inaccurate sleep and mediocre 80/55 special bulk made those strategies inconsistent. Generation VI raised Unfezant's Attack from 105 to 115, yet SM analysis still placed it in ZU because the movepool problem remained, with other Normal/Flying attackers offering stronger STAB or broader coverage. Its competitive lesson is a useful one for the site: strong base stats alone do not guarantee viability when a Pokemon cannot translate those stats into high-quality moves.
nuzlocke: The Pidove line is useful in Nuzlockes because it is obtainable early, reaches Unfezant at level 32, and gains both Ground and Ghost immunities that create completely safe switches against known attacks. Base 93 Speed and respectable physical Attack let Unfezant remove many ordinary opponents before they retaliate, and Fly can serve as both field utility in older games and usable physical STAB. Its poor Special Defense makes strong Electric or Ice attacks particularly dangerous, and Rock moves are also super effective while Stealth Rock can gradually wear it down in games where opponents use hazards. Super Luck can produce helpful critical hits but should never be treated as a guaranteed damage plan, while Rivalry is too matchup-dependent to be relied upon. Adamant or Jolly Unfezant is safest as a fast attacker and immunity pivot rather than a Pokemon expected to absorb repeated special attacks.

pokemon.name: Pidove
pokemon.biologyAndBehavior: Pidove is friendly and sincerely tries to obey its Trainer, but it is notoriously forgetful and may fail to remember instructions almost immediately after receiving them. It likes following people and is commonly comfortable around humans. Its poor memory is a defining behavioral trait rather than a lack of willingness to cooperate.

pokemon.name: Tranquill
pokemon.biologyAndBehavior: Tranquill has an exceptional sense of direction and memory for places, allowing it to return to its Trainer and nest no matter how far it travels. This homing ability makes the species useful to delivery workers. Legends also associate Tranquill with peaceful deep forests said to contain places free from conflict.

pokemon.name: Unfezant
pokemon.biologyAndBehavior: Unfezant shows pronounced differences between the sexes. Males use the long plumage around the head to threaten rivals, while females are described as more capable fliers, particularly in endurance and control. The species is highly proud and intelligent and normally forms close bonds only with its Trainer. Females may take longer than males to become comfortable around people.

playthrough: Blitzle evolves into Zebstrika at level 27, producing a very fast pure Electric Pokemon with base 116 Speed, 100 Attack, and 80 Special Attack. Wild Charge provides powerful physical Electric STAB at the cost of recoil, while Spark offers a safer physical alternative and Thunderbolt or Volt Switch let Zebstrika attack specially; Flame Charge and Overheat provide valuable Fire coverage against Grass-types that resist Electric. Motor Drive grants an Electric immunity and raises Speed by one stage when activated, Lightning Rod also grants Electric immunity while raising Special Attack, and the Hidden Ability Sap Sipper creates a Grass immunity and raises Attack, giving Zebstrika three abilities that can all create free switches under the right conditions. Pure Electric typing normally has only a Ground weakness, making the line easy to understand defensively despite mediocre 75/63/63 bulk. Jolly suits physical sets, Timid supports special Volt Switch and Overheat sets, and mixed approaches can take advantage of both offensive stats, but Wild Charge recoil should be avoided when Spark or another move already secures the knockout.
competitive: Zebstrika was one of BW PU's premier offensive pivots because base 116 Speed was the highest in the tier and Volt Switch allowed it to maintain momentum against slower teams. Thunderbolt and Volt Switch formed the core of most special sets, while Overheat punished Grass-types that would otherwise switch comfortably into Electric attacks and Hidden Power or item choice supplied the remaining customization. Lightning Rod could provide both an Electric immunity and a Special Attack boost, while Motor Drive offered an alternative Speed increase; despite base 100 Attack, recoil from Wild Charge and the greater utility of Volt Switch often pushed competitive sets toward special offense. Its primary weakness was power rather than tempo: base 80 Special Attack is merely average, its bulk is poor, and specially defensive Pokemon can survive its attacks without much difficulty. Zebstrika therefore built a real niche around being extremely fast and difficult to pin down rather than around overwhelming wallbreaking strength.
nuzlocke: Zebstrika's base 116 Speed is excellent for Nuzlockes because many opponents simply never get to move once Zebstrika has a favorable matchup. Pure Electric typing gives it only a Ground weakness, while Motor Drive or Lightning Rod can create complete Electric immunities and Sap Sipper can instead create a Grass immunity, making ability knowledge useful for planning safe switches. Its 63 Defense and 63 Special Defense are poor, so unexpected Ground coverage or strong neutral priority can still be dangerous despite the simple typing. Wild Charge is powerful but recoil is unnecessary when Spark or another reliable move already produces the knockout, and Overheat sharply lowers Special Attack after use. Jolly physical or Timid special Zebstrika is safest when its Speed and immunities are used to prevent damage rather than asking it to trade hits.

pokemon.name: Blitzle
pokemon.biologyAndBehavior: Blitzle generates electricity through its heartbeat and stores charge in the white mane along its body. The mane flashes when electricity is discharged, and individuals communicate with one another by changing the rhythm and frequency of those flashes. When Blitzle is startled, its faster heartbeat increases the voltage it produces. Herds deliberately venture out during thunderstorms so lightning can recharge their manes.

pokemon.name: Zebstrika
pokemon.biologyAndBehavior: Zebstrika is aggressive and quick-tempered, firing lightning bolts from its mane when angered. It can run at speeds compared to lightning, and a herd galloping at full speed produces sounds like thunder. Zebstrika leads groups of Blitzle into thunderstorms so the herd can recharge itself from lightning strikes. The glowing mane provides an obvious warning that an agitated individual is preparing to discharge electricity.

playthrough: Roggenrola evolves into Boldore at level 25 and then into Gigalith through trading, making access to the final stage dependent on another player or an equivalent trade feature in most games. Gigalith is extremely slow at base 25 Speed but has enormous base 135 Attack and 130 Defense, while its Special Defense increased from 70 to 80 beginning in Generation VII. Rock Slide or Stone Edge provides strong STAB, with Rock Blast, Earthquake, Heavy Slam, Body Press in later games, Stealth Rock, and Explosion or utility options giving it both offensive and support roles. Sturdy guarantees survival from full HP against a single otherwise fatal hit in modern mechanics, Sand Force boosts Rock-, Ground-, and Steel-type attacks in sand, and from Generation VII onward Gigalith gained Sand Stream as a standard ability, automatically summoning sand and increasing its own Special Defense by 50 percent because it is a Rock-type. Brave is excellent under Trick Room and Adamant suits ordinary physical offense, while the trade requirement means Boldore itself may need to serve as the final form in runs where trading is unavailable.
competitive: Gigalith began BW competitive play as a slow lower-tier Rock attacker whose defining tools were base 135 Attack, base 130 Defense, Sturdy, and excellent performance under Trick Room. Smogon placed it in BW NU and highlighted Sturdy as effectively providing a built-in Focus Sash, while Rock Slide or Rock Blast, Earthquake, Choice Band, and even Explosion made it capable of dealing enormous physical damage despite rock-bottom base 25 Speed. Generation VII dramatically improved Gigalith by increasing Special Defense from 70 to 80 and giving it Sand Stream; sand automatically boosts a Rock-type's Special Defense by 50 percent, turning Gigalith into an unusually durable weather setter rather than merely a slow attacker. In SM it reached RU and also became an important VGC 2017 weather Pokemon, supporting partners such as Sand Rush Stoutland while functioning exceptionally well under Trick Room. Later formats continued to use it as a bulky sand setter, Stealth Rock user, and physical tank, making Gigalith one of the clearer examples of a Pokemon whose competitive relevance improved substantially because of later-generation mechanical changes rather than a new evolution or form.
nuzlocke: The Roggenrola line is very safe against many physical attacks because Boldore and Gigalith have enormous Defense and modern Sturdy can guarantee survival from full HP against a single otherwise lethal hit. That guarantee disappears once chip damage, status, weather, or hazards break full health, so keeping Sturdy intact can be more important than maximizing damage in a dangerous fight. Water, Grass, Fighting, Ground, and Steel attacks are all super effective, and Gigalith's extremely low Speed means one of those attacks will almost always land before it responds. Sand Stream from Generation VII onward improves special durability substantially but can also chip teammates that are not immune to sand, while Stone Edge and Rock Slide introduce accuracy concerns compared with weaker but safer alternatives. The biggest practical issue is the trade evolution: where trading is unavailable, Boldore may be the endpoint, so a Nuzlocke should not assume access to Gigalith unless its evolution method is actually possible under the run's rules.

pokemon.name: Roggenrola
pokemon.biologyAndBehavior: Roggenrola is born deep underground and was first discovered after an earthquake exposed a rock layer containing the species. Its steel-hard body is formed from ancient compressed earth and contains a warm energy core. The hexagonal opening on the front of its body is an ear rather than an eye and leads directly toward that core, giving Roggenrola extremely sensitive hearing. It follows sounds that it detects and can panic when they suddenly disappear; Dwebble and even Rhyperior sometimes mistake it for an ordinary rock.

pokemon.name: Boldore
pokemon.biologyAndBehavior: Boldore's reddish-orange crystals are hardened forms of energy that continuously leaks from the core inside its body, and the crystals glow intensely when the Pokemon is preparing to release that power. The material is extraordinarily hard and valuable, with even a fragment described as capable of supplying immense amounts of energy, so Boldore is sometimes targeted for its crystals. It searches cave systems for underground water but dislikes becoming wet and drinks cautiously. Boldore relies heavily on sound to understand its surroundings and has unusual movement habits, tending to keep its body facing the same direction even while attacking.

pokemon.name: Gigalith
pokemon.biologyAndBehavior: Gigalith compresses tremendous energy inside its core and can release blasts powerful enough to destroy large objects or even blow away parts of mountains, although firing at maximum output can crack its own rocky body. Its orange crystals absorb sunlight and magnify that energy before Gigalith fires it from its mouth; this particular process cannot function effectively at night or during rain. The species lives deep in caves and tunnels and possesses enough raw strength to work alongside humans in mines and construction sites. In Galar, Gigalith is specifically known to partner with Copperajah on heavy construction and mining work.

playthrough: Woobat evolves into Swoobat through high friendship rather than at a fixed level, so a player who catches one early can potentially obtain the final form relatively quickly by keeping it in the party and avoiding fainting. Swoobat is a Psychic/Flying special attacker with excellent base 114 Speed but only base 77 Special Attack and frail 67/55/55 bulk, making tempo much more important than durability. Psychic or Psyshock and Air Slash provide reliable STAB, while Calm Mind, Energy Ball, Heat Wave, Shadow Ball, U-turn, Roost in applicable games, and Stored Power give it several offensive or support directions. Unaware ignores opposing stat changes when calculating damage, which can make Swoobat surprisingly useful against setup opponents, while Klutz suppresses most held-item effects and is usually awkward in a normal playthrough. The Hidden Ability Simple is the most explosive option where legitimately available because every stat-stage change affecting Swoobat is doubled: one Calm Mind effectively raises both Special Attack and Special Defense by two stages, and Stored Power immediately becomes much stronger. Timid is usually the best nature because preserving Swoobat's elite Speed is central to surviving with such poor defenses.
competitive: Swoobat has spent most of its competitive history in lower tiers, but it has developed two genuinely distinct niches. In BW PU, Unaware allowed Choice Specs Swoobat to ignore defensive boosts and act as an unusually fast anti-setup attacker, with base 114 Speed outrunning almost the entire tier. Its more famous strategy uses the Hidden Ability Simple with Calm Mind and Stored Power: because Simple doubles the stat changes from Calm Mind, a single use provides four total positive stat stages and raises Stored Power to 100 base power while also sharply increasing Swoobat's Special Attack and Special Defense. Substitute can protect that setup from priority or status, and Heat Wave gives coverage against Steel-types, but Swoobat's low base 77 Special Attack before boosting and extremely poor defenses make finding a safe setup turn difficult. It has therefore remained a specialized lower-tier sweeper or anti-setup weapon rather than a broadly reliable high-tier Pokemon.
nuzlocke: Swoobat's Ground immunity, quadruple Fighting resistance, base 114 Speed, and access to Psychic and Flying STAB create several excellent planned matchups in a Nuzlocke. The danger is that 67 HP and only 55 in both defenses leave almost no room for unexpected Electric, Ice, Rock, Ghost, Dark, or strong neutral attacks. Unaware can be exceptionally useful when facing opponents that rely on stat boosts because Swoobat ignores those boosts for damage calculations, while Simple can turn one Calm Mind into enormous offensive and special-defensive momentum if the Hidden Ability is available. Setup should still be reserved for opponents that cannot threaten Swoobat immediately, and Stored Power is much less impressive before boosts. Timid Swoobat is safest when used to exploit immunities, resistances, and Speed rather than being asked to absorb damage.

pokemon.name: Woobat
pokemon.biologyAndBehavior: Woobat inhabits caves and dark forests and navigates by emitting ultrasonic waves from its nose. It can cling to cave walls through suction from its nostrils while sleeping, leaving a distinctive heart-shaped mark behind when it detaches. Folklore says that receiving one of these marks brings good fortune. Woobat also preys on Bug-type Pokemon.

pokemon.name: Swoobat
pokemon.biologyAndBehavior: Swoobat produces many different ultrasonic waves from its heart-shaped nose and can generate especially powerful sound waves by shaking its tail. Those vibrations can be strong enough to destroy concrete, but using them at full power exhausts Swoobat so severely that it may be unable to fly for a short time afterward. Male Swoobat use sound waves during courtship, and the waves they produce are said to make those who hear them feel happier. Its heart-shaped nose is also regarded as a symbol of good luck in some regions.

playthrough: Drilbur evolves into Excadrill at level 31, producing one of Unova's strongest non-legendary physical attackers with base 135 Attack, 110 HP, and Ground/Steel typing. Earthquake and Iron Head form excellent physical STAB, while Rock Slide, Swords Dance, Rapid Spin, Stealth Rock, Brick Break, Shadow Claw, and other coverage or utility let Excadrill act as a sweeper and team supporter at the same time. Sand Rush doubles Speed in sand, turning base 88 Speed into an enormous advantage; Sand Force instead boosts Rock-, Ground-, and Steel-type attacks in sand, while the Hidden Ability Mold Breaker lets Excadrill ignore abilities such as Levitate when attacking. Ground/Steel gives Electric and Poison immunities plus numerous resistances, but base 60 Defense and 65 Special Defense are much less impressive than the 110 HP suggests, and Water, Fire, Fighting, and Ground attacks remain dangerous. Adamant maximizes the already exceptional Attack, while Jolly improves important Speed thresholds outside sand. Mega Excadrill, introduced in Pokémon Legends: Z-A, remains Ground/Steel but rises to base 165 Attack, 100 Defense, and 103 Speed; in ability-enabled data its signature Ability Piercing Drill allows contact moves to strike through protection for reduced damage, making the Mega form far stronger and more physically durable without changing the line's core weaknesses.
competitive: Excadrill has one of the most important competitive histories of any Generation V Pokemon. During BW's original active metagame, Sand Rush doubled its Speed under permanent sand while base 135 Attack, Swords Dance, Earthquake, Rock Slide, and Rapid Spin let the same Pokemon function as both a devastating sweeper and one of the game's best hazard removers; it was banned from OU in October 2011 after that combination proved overwhelming. Excadrill later returned to BW OU under weather-speed restrictions that prevent the original Sand Stream plus Sand Rush abuse, and current BW sets instead make extensive use of Sand Force or Mold Breaker, where it remains one of the tier's best Pokemon and arguably its best Rapid Spinner. In later generations Sand Rush Excadrill became legal again under normal temporary sand and repeatedly returned as a major OU sand sweeper, while Mold Breaker sets provided Stealth Rock and Rapid Spin support and could Earthquake Levitate users such as Rotom-W. Mega Excadrill is far newer than standard Excadrill, so it does not yet have the same mature historical singles résumé; confirmed competitive data gives it 165 Attack, 100 Defense, 103 Speed, and Piercing Drill, but long-term tier conclusions should remain separate from the established history of the base form.
nuzlocke: Excadrill is excellent in Nuzlockes because base 135 Attack frequently secures one-hit knockouts, Ground/Steel provides two immunities and numerous resistances, and it evolves at the manageable level 31 without requiring an item or trade. Mold Breaker is particularly useful for removing uncertainty around defensive abilities such as Levitate, while Sand Rush can make Excadrill nearly impossible for ordinary opponents to outspeed when sand is available. Its bulk is uneven, however: 110 HP is good but 60 Defense and 65 Special Defense mean strong Water, Fire, Fighting, or Ground attacks can kill it much faster than its Steel typing may suggest. Swords Dance is powerful but often unnecessary when a direct Earthquake already wins safely, and Rock Slide's imperfect accuracy can be avoided when reliable STAB is sufficient. Mega Excadrill improves physical bulk and Speed enormously where available, but it retains the same four type weaknesses, so Mega Evolution does not make blind switching safe.

pokemon.name: Drilbur
pokemon.biologyAndBehavior: Drilbur joins the claws on its forelimbs together and spins its body like a drill, allowing it to burrow through the ground at roughly 30 miles per hour. Its digging is fast enough to compete with a car traveling aboveground. Farmers often dislike the species because its underground tunneling can damage vegetable fields and other crops.

pokemon.name: Excadrill
pokemon.biologyAndBehavior: Excadrill's claws and head blade harden into steel after evolution, allowing it to form its entire body into a powerful rotating drill. It can cut through iron and steel plate and tunnel underground at more than 90 miles per hour. Excadrill constructs complicated mazelike nests more than 300 feet below the surface, earning the nickname 'Drill King.' Humans value its extraordinary digging ability for tunnel construction, but wild colonies can also damage subway tunnels and other underground infrastructure.

pokemon.name: Excadrill
pokemon.biologyAndBehavior: Mega Evolution enlarges the drill blades on Excadrill's head and arms into massive spiraling structures built around high-speed rotation. By bringing its head and forelimbs together into a streamlined drill shape and spinning at extreme speed, Mega Excadrill can destroy virtually anything in its path. The transformation therefore magnifies the same tunneling anatomy that defines ordinary Excadrill rather than replacing it with a fundamentally different fighting style.

playthrough: Audino is a single-stage Normal-type built around support and durability rather than damage, with base 103 HP, 86 Defense, 86 Special Defense, and only base 60 in both attacking stats. Regenerator is its strongest ordinary single-battle Ability because switching out restores one-third of maximum HP, allowing Audino to repeatedly absorb damage without spending turns healing; Healer instead has a chance to cure an ally's status in doubles, while Klutz suppresses most held-item effects. Wish, Protect, Heal Bell, Thunder Wave, Toxic in older games, Reflect, Light Screen, and broad but weak offensive coverage let Audino act as a team medic, and its unusually high experience yield also made wild Audino famous as training targets throughout Unova. Mega Audino becomes Normal/Fairy, raises both Defense and Special Defense to 126, gains a Dragon immunity and Dark resistance, and uses Healer rather than Regenerator; its offense remains modest, so Mega Evolution improves survivability far more than damage. Calm or Bold are natural defensive natures, and Audino is most effective in a playthrough when the team actually benefits from healing and status support rather than expecting it to sweep.
competitive: Base Audino has spent most of its singles history in lower tiers as a defensive cleric, where Regenerator, 103 HP, Wish, Protect, Heal Bell, Knock Off, Encore, and status support allow it to pivot repeatedly and pass large Wishes to teammates. BW tiering places Audino in PU, and its role has remained broadly similar in later generations: it is difficult to wear down through chip damage but can become passive because both offensive stats are only base 60. Mega Audino gave the species a substantially stronger competitive identity in Generation VI and especially SM NU. The Mega form's 103/126/126 bulk, Normal/Fairy typing, Wish, Heal Bell, Encore, Toxic, and broad support movepool made it one of NU's premier walls, capable of handling a wide range of special and physical attackers. A key tactical wrinkle is that base Audino has Regenerator while Mega Audino has Healer, so competitive sets can delay Mega Evolution to collect Regenerator healing before committing to the Mega form's superior defenses and typing.
nuzlocke: Audino is exceptionally safe as a support Pokemon in Nuzlockes because base 103 HP, balanced defenses, and Regenerator allow it to absorb moderate damage and heal simply by switching out. Wish can restore Audino or teammates, while Heal Bell removes debilitating status from the party in generations where it is available, giving the species value that does not depend on dealing much damage. Pure Normal has only a Fighting weakness and a Ghost immunity, but its lack of ordinary resistances means Audino should still be switched into attacks selectively. Mega Audino is much harder to break and gains a Dragon immunity, but losing Regenerator means it relies more on active healing once it Mega Evolves. Bold or Calm are the safest conventional natures, and the main drawback is passivity: long battles create more opportunities for critical hits, so Audino works best when its healing enables stronger teammates rather than trying to slowly win every matchup itself.

pokemon.name: Audino
pokemon.biologyAndBehavior: Audino's curled ear feelers function like extremely sensitive stethoscopes. By touching another Pokemon with them, it can detect heartbeat, emotional state, and overall physical condition, and it can even tell when an Egg is close to hatching. Its hearing is extraordinarily sharp, with Pokédex descriptions claiming it can hear a small pebble rolling from a mile away. Audino is consistently described as kind-hearted, fitting its strong association with medical care and healing.

pokemon.name: Audino
pokemon.biologyAndBehavior: Mega Audino develops longer sensory feelers and a white, coat-like body covering that strengthens its medical appearance. It can emit calming pulses that reduce hostility in nearby beings. The secondary feelers extending from its body can induce deep sleep in anything that touches them, giving the Mega form an additional way to pacify injured or aggressive creatures.

playthrough: Timburr evolves into Gurdurr at level 25 and Gurdurr evolves into Conkeldurr by trading, so players without access to trading may need to treat Gurdurr as the practical endpoint of the family. Conkeldurr is an extraordinarily strong but slow pure Fighting attacker with base 140 Attack, 105 HP, 95 Defense, and only base 45 Speed. Drain Punch combines reliable Fighting STAB with healing, Mach Punch provides priority, and Knock Off, Ice Punch, Thunder Punch, Rock Slide, Earthquake, Bulk Up, and other coverage let it pressure nearly anything that does not resist Fighting. Guts raises Attack by 50 percent while statused and ignores burn's normal Attack reduction, Sheer Force boosts moves with secondary effects while removing those effects, and the Hidden Ability Iron Fist boosts punching moves such as Drain Punch and Mach Punch. Adamant is ideal for straightforward offense, Careful can patch the weak Special Defense, and Brave is useful under Trick Room. Gurdurr itself remains very capable with Eviolite where available, so the trade requirement is inconvenient rather than completely crippling.
competitive: Conkeldurr was a major BW OU Pokemon and one of the generation's defining bulky physical attackers. Base 140 Attack, 105 HP, Guts, Bulk Up, Drain Punch, Mach Punch, Payback, and later elemental punches let it pressure common sand staples such as Tyranitar and Ferrothorn while using priority to compensate for base 45 Speed. Guts made status dangerous to use against it because burns and poison could increase its Attack rather than neutralize it, while Iron Fist supported four-attacks sets centered on Drain Punch, Mach Punch, Ice Punch, and Thunder Punch. It remained a serious wallbreaker in later generations, including SS UU and modern SV UU, where Flame Orb Guts, Knock Off, Drain Punch, Facade, and Mach Punch continue to exploit the same enormous Attack stat. Gurdurr also developed its own lower-tier niche with Eviolite, which turns its already solid defenses into a sturdy bulky attacker when Conkeldurr is unavailable or inappropriate for the tier. Conkeldurr's enduring limitations are low Speed, mediocre Special Defense, and later Fairy weakness, but very few Fighting-types combine comparable immediate power, priority, status absorption, and healing.
nuzlocke: The Timburr family is highly reliable in Nuzlockes because it reaches Gurdurr at level 25 and both Gurdurr and Conkeldurr combine strong physical bulk with excellent Fighting damage.
