Smogon's XY analyses treat the varieties almost like separate lower-tier Pokemon because their stat tradeoffs meaningfully change which threats they outspeed or withstand. Frisk is generally the most useful ability because scouting Choice items, Eviolite, or other key held items can guide a switch or burn decision, while Insomnia has niche value against sleep. The family remains constrained by five weaknesses, limited immediate Ghost STAB in early generations, and competition from bulkier or stronger Grass- and Ghost-types. Its best competitive value therefore comes from physical checking, Will-O-Wisp, Leech Seed, and size-specific utility rather than raw sweeping.
nuzlocke: Gourgeist can be very safe against physical attackers because every size has base 122 Defense, and Will-O-Wisp can further cut opposing physical damage. Normal and Fighting immunities create predictable switch opportunities, while Synthesis and Leech Seed can provide recovery without recoil. The size matters in a Nuzlocke: larger Gourgeist generally offer a larger HP buffer and stronger physical attacks, while smaller forms are more likely to move first and avoid a second hit. Fire, Ice, Flying, Ghost, and Dark attacks should still be scouted carefully, and Destiny Bond is generally too dangerous for routine permadeath play because it requires Gourgeist to faint. Like Trevenant, Gourgeist's greatest accessibility problem is trading—without it, Pumpkaboo cannot evolve.

pokemon.name: Pumpkaboo
pokemon.biologyAndBehavior: Pumpkaboo is a spirit inhabiting a pumpkin-like body and becomes most active around sundown. It carries wandering spirits inside its body and is said to guide them to the afterlife, while the glowing openings in its pumpkin can hypnotize and control humans or Pokemon that look into the light. Four recognized varieties exist—Small, Medium, Large, and Jumbo—and modern records associate those sizes with the size or number of lost souls present where the Pumpkaboo formed. The varieties also show preferences for the kinds of spirits they guide, with smaller forms favoring children and larger forms favoring adults or unusually large spirits.

pokemon.name: Gourgeist
pokemon.biologyAndBehavior: Gourgeist wanders towns on nights of the new moon while singing an eerie song said to curse anyone who hears it. Its long hair-like tendrils function as arms and can wrap around prey while Gourgeist sings happily, giving the species a much more predatory reputation than Pumpkaboo. Like its pre-evolution, Gourgeist occurs in four size varieties whose size preferences are linked to the people or spirits they target; Small forms may imitate children, Large forms may imitate adults, and Jumbo forms are described as less selective. Gourgeist can also retract its upper body into the pumpkin-like lower body, temporarily resembling a conventional jack-o'-lantern.

playthrough: Bergmite evolves into Avalugg at level 37. Standard Avalugg is a pure Ice physical wall with 95 HP, 117 Attack, and an extraordinary base 184 Defense, but only 46 Special Defense and 28 Speed; Avalanche, Body Press in later generations, Earthquake, Rapid Spin, Recover, Curse, and Roar let it absorb physical hits while providing hazard control or pressure. Own Tempo prevents confusion, Ice Body restores HP during hail or snow, and the Hidden Ability Sturdy guarantees survival from full HP against a single otherwise fatal hit. Hisuian Avalugg instead becomes Ice/Rock with base 127 Attack, the same 184 Defense, only 36 Special Defense, and 38 Speed; it can have Strong Jaw, Ice Body, or Sturdy and uses moves such as Mountain Gale, Rock Slide, Stone Edge, Body Press, and Earthquake. Standard Ice typing has four common weaknesses and only an Ice resistance, while Hisuian Ice/Rock gains additional resistances but suffers quadruple Fighting and Steel weaknesses plus Water, Grass, Ground, and Rock weaknesses. Careful is usually safest for standard Avalugg because physical Defense needs little help, while Adamant or Brave can make better use of Hisuian Avalugg's higher Attack.
competitive: Standard Avalugg's niche is extremely concentrated but legitimate: base 184 Defense, Recover, Rapid Spin, and enough Attack to avoid complete passivity make it one of the strongest pure physical tanks available in lower tiers. Smogon's XY analysis emphasizes that it can repeatedly remove hazards and withstand neutral physical attacks that would overwhelm most spinners, while Recover allows it to maintain Sturdy and continue checking threats. Its crippling weaknesses are poor Ice defensive typing, vulnerability to entry hazards, awful Speed, and very low Special Defense, all of which make even modest special attacks dangerous. Hisuian Avalugg pushes the physical specialization further with base 127 Attack and the same enormous Defense, but Ice/Rock is even harder to defend with because Fighting and Steel deal quadruple damage and several other types are super effective. Strong Jaw gives the Hisuian form more offensive potential with biting moves, but neither form is broadly splashable; they succeed only when a team specifically values extreme physical bulk and can cover their many special and type-based vulnerabilities.
nuzlocke: Standard Avalugg can make physical Nuzlocke encounters extraordinarily safe because base 184 Defense and Recover allow it to absorb repeated neutral contact better than almost any ordinary Pokemon. Sturdy is excellent insurance if Avalugg enters at full HP, while Rapid Spin can remove hazards without sacrificing the team's own hazards in older mechanics. The danger is special offense: base 46 Special Defense is poor enough that even neutral special moves deserve respect, and Fire, Fighting, Rock, and Steel attacks are super effective. Hisuian Avalugg is even more dangerous to use blindly because Fighting and Steel attacks deal quadruple damage and its Special Defense falls to base 36. Careful investment can patch standard Avalugg's weakest stat, but neither form should be left in against an unknown special attacker merely because its physical Defense is enormous.

pokemon.name: Bergmite
pokemon.biologyAndBehavior: Bergmite lives in cold regions and covers its small body with a protective shell of ice. It creates and repairs that armor by blasting freezing air from its body, and groups of Bergmite often gather together on or around much larger Avalugg. They can cling to Avalugg's broad back while it carries them across water and between icy habitats. Bergmite's body temperature is extremely low, and cracks or damage in the ice armor can be repaired by refreezing moisture around it.

pokemon.name: Avalugg
pokemon.biologyAndBehavior: Standard Avalugg is a massive Pokemon covered almost completely in semi-transparent ice that is described as being as hard as steel. Its broad, flat back can support groups of Bergmite, making a traveling group resemble an aircraft carrier as Avalugg transports the smaller Pokemon across oceans to new habitats. Avalugg advances by crushing obstacles in its path rather than maneuvering around them. Cracks in its icy body deepen during the day and return to normal overnight as the Pokemon's ice repairs itself.

pokemon.name: Avalugg
pokemon.biologyAndBehavior: Hisuian Avalugg is smaller and lighter than the modern standard form, with a body made largely of durable brown stone beneath a layer of solid ice. Huge ice plates around its jaw form a distinctive plow-like structure that it uses to smash through obstacles and attack with tremendous physical force. The rocky body explains its Ice/Rock typing and makes it look more like a moving mountain or glacier face than a solid slab of ice. Its jaw structure is powerful enough that biting attacks become an important part of the regional form's fighting style.

playthrough: Noibat evolves into Noivern at level 48, so the line requires carrying a relatively weak unevolved Pokemon for a long time before reaching its full value. Noivern is Flying/Dragon with excellent base 123 Speed, base 97 Special Attack, and balanced 85/80/80 bulk. Draco Meteor or Dragon Pulse and Hurricane or Air Slash provide dual STAB, while Flamethrower, Boomburst, U-turn, Roost, Taunt, Switcheroo, Super Fang, and other coverage or utility make Noivern an effective fast attacker and pivot. Frisk reveals opposing held items, Infiltrator lets damaging and status moves ignore Substitute plus several screen effects, and the Hidden Ability Telepathy prevents damage from allies' attacks in doubles. Flying/Dragon grants a Ground immunity and strong resistances to Grass plus resistances to Fire, Water, Fighting, and Bug, but Rock, Dragon, and Fairy are super effective and Ice deals quadruple damage. Timid is usually ideal because base 123 Speed is the defining strength, while Modest is viable only when external speed control is reliable.
competitive: Noivern was placed in RUBL in XY but maintained a real UU niche because base 123 Speed lets it outrun a large portion of the unboosted metagame. Choice Specs Draco Meteor and Hurricane provide strong wallbreaking pressure, while Flamethrower covers Steel-types and U-turn or Switcheroo can preserve momentum or cripple defensive answers. Infiltrator is especially valuable because it ignores Substitute and screen effects, preventing several otherwise safe setup strategies from blocking Noivern's attacks. Smogon's XY analysis describes it as a moderate wallbreaker and offense killer whose Speed and utility differentiate it from stronger but slower Dragon-types. The drawbacks are the quadruple Ice weakness, Stealth Rock vulnerability, merely base 97 Special Attack, and the imperfect accuracy or stat drops attached to its strongest STAB moves. Noivern is therefore strongest as a fast opportunistic attacker rather than a Pokemon that brute-forces every neutral matchup.
nuzlocke: Noivern is very useful once Noibat finally reaches level 48, but the long unevolved period is the most dangerous part of raising the family. Base 123 Speed allows Noivern to avoid many attacks outright, while Roost and U-turn provide recovery and escape options. Air Slash and Dragon Pulse are safer than Hurricane and Draco Meteor when the additional power is unnecessary, especially because Hurricane can miss and Draco Meteor sharply reduces Special Attack after use. Ice attacks are the critical danger because they deal quadruple damage, while Rock, Dragon, and Fairy moves are also super effective. Frisk is unusually useful in a Nuzlocke because revealing an opposing held item can expose a Choice item, damage booster, or Berry before the player commits to a risky line.

pokemon.name: Noibat
pokemon.biologyAndBehavior: Noibat lives in pitch-dark caves, rests during the day, and emerges at night to search for ripe fruit. Its enormous speaker-like ears can emit virtually any wavelength of sound, including ultrasonic waves up to roughly 200,000 hertz, strong enough to make much larger creatures dizzy or unable to stand. Noibat uses those waves for echolocation, communication, stunning prey, and testing the ripeness of fruit. Its dependence on sonar is so strong that it can navigate total darkness without relying on normal vision.

pokemon.name: Noivern
pokemon.biologyAndBehavior: Noivern is a nocturnal aerial predator whose huge ears generate ultrasonic waves powerful enough to shatter large boulders. It uses those waves both to locate targets and to disorient or immobilize them before attacking from the air. Wild Noivern is known for a violent temper, but it can become surprisingly tame when approached with ripe fruit, which remains a favorite food from the Noibat stage. Its combination of sonic weaponry, high-speed flight, and fruit-seeking behavior makes it both a predator and an opportunistic frugivore.

playthrough: Xerneas is a pure Fairy Legendary with base 126 HP, 131 Attack, 131 Special Attack, 95 Defense, 98 Special Defense, and 99 Speed. Fairy Aura increases the power of Fairy-type moves used by any Pokemon on the field by roughly one-third, making Moonblast or Dazzling Gleam substantially stronger even before setup. Geomancy is Xerneas's signature move and normally spends one turn charging before raising Special Attack, Special Defense, and Speed by two stages each; a Power Herb allows that charge to complete immediately, creating one of the strongest one-turn setup combinations in the series. Thunder, Focus Blast, Grass Knot, Psyshock or Psychic in relevant games, Aromatherapy in older generations, and coverage can support the Fairy STAB. Pure Fairy is immune to Dragon, resists Fighting, Bug, and Dark, and is weak only to Poison and Steel. Xerneas has Neutral Mode and Active Mode, but the modes do not change its stats or ability; it simply appears in Active Mode when battling or using its power. Modest maximizes Geomancy sweeping power, while Timid can secure important Speed thresholds before setup or against other boosted threats.
competitive: Xerneas has been an Ubers-defining Pokemon since its introduction. Power Herb Geomancy raises Special Attack, Special Defense, and Speed by two stages in a single turn, while Fairy Aura boosts Moonblast beyond ordinary STAB and makes a boosted Xerneas capable of sweeping teams immediately if its checks have been weakened. Smogon's XY Ubers analysis describes Geomancy as a set that shapes the metagame around itself, forcing teams to carry dedicated Steel-types, Poison-types, phazing, priority, or other emergency counterplay. Xerneas is not limited to one set: Choice Scarf, Choice Specs, bulky support, Aromatherapy, and mixed or defensive approaches have all appeared because 126 HP and balanced offensive stats give it unusual flexibility. It was also a defining restricted Pokemon in VGC 2016, where Geomancy plus spread Dazzling Gleam created tremendous doubles pressure. Its Neutral and Active Modes are competitively identical; the mode shift is visual rather than a stat transformation.
nuzlocke: If Legendary Pokemon are permitted, Xerneas is one of the safest offensive choices available because 126 HP, only two weaknesses, a Dragon immunity, and Geomancy's simultaneous Special Defense and Speed boosts create an enormous margin for error. Power Herb Geomancy can turn a controlled setup opportunity into an immediate sweep without spending a vulnerable charging turn. Moonblast is accurate and powerful, making it safer than relying unnecessarily on Focus Blast or Thunder when neutral Fairy damage is enough. Poison and Steel attacks remain the principal dangers, especially before Geomancy or from strong physical attackers, and a critical hit can still bypass much of the planned defensive advantage. Modest is excellent for raw power, while Timid is safer when acting first before setup matters more than maximum damage.

pokemon.name: Xerneas
pokemon.biologyAndBehavior: Neutral Mode is Xerneas's resting state, recognizable by pale blue antlers and subdued markings rather than the multicolored antlers seen when its power is active. Xerneas is associated throughout Kalosian mythology with life, renewal, and the ability to share life energy with other beings. When it expends too much of that energy, lore says it transforms into a tree and sleeps for roughly 1,000 years to restore itself. Its calm resting appearance therefore represents a dormant state of an extraordinarily powerful life-giving Pokemon rather than a weaker species form.

pokemon.name: Xerneas
pokemon.biologyAndBehavior: Xerneas enters Active Mode during battle or when fully using its power, causing its antlers and body markings to glow in multiple colors. Pokédex lore says that when the horns shine in seven colors, Xerneas can share everlasting life, and other portrayals show it causing plants to grow simply through contact or restoring beings petrified by Yveltal. Xerneas can also calm Yveltal when the destruction Pokemon becomes enraged. Active Mode has the same game stats as Neutral Mode, but biologically and visually it represents Xerneas actively channeling the life energy for which it is revered.

playthrough: Yveltal is a Dark/Flying Legendary with base 126 HP, 131 Attack, 131 Special Attack, and 99 Speed, giving it genuine mixed-offense flexibility on top of strong natural bulk. Dark Aura strengthens Dark-type moves used by any Pokemon on the field, making Dark Pulse, Knock Off, Sucker Punch, or other Dark attacks noticeably more threatening. Oblivion Wing is Yveltal's signature Flying-type special attack and restores HP based on the damage dealt, giving it rare offensive recovery; Hurricane, Heat Wave, Focus Blast, U-turn, Taunt, Roost in relevant games, and utility such as Defog or Snarl broaden its role further. Dark/Flying grants complete Ground and Psychic immunities and resistances to Ghost, Grass, and Dark, but Electric, Ice, Rock, and Fairy attacks are super effective. Its mixed stats allow either physical or special sets, but Timid is often safest for special offense while Jolly or Adamant can support physical approaches. Because Yveltal is already powerful without setup, it is usually better to exploit its bulk, recovery, and immunities than to force risky boosting strategies in an ordinary playthrough.
competitive: Yveltal has been a defining Ubers Pokemon since Generation VI. Dark Aura makes its Dark STAB exceptionally difficult to absorb, while Oblivion Wing provides offensive recovery and its 126/95/98 bulk lets it repeatedly check threats that frailer attackers cannot. In XY and ORAS Ubers, Yveltal could function as a wallbreaker, Choice Scarf revenge killer, mixed attacker, bulky pivot, or defensive utility Pokemon using combinations of Dark Pulse, Knock Off, Sucker Punch, Foul Play, Taunt, Roost, and Defog. Later generations gave Yveltal an even more important defensive role because its Dark typing and bulk made it one of the most reliable answers to powerful Psychic- and Ghost-type restricted Pokemon, especially Calyrex-Shadow in Sword and Shield. Its main flaws are the Stealth Rock weakness, susceptibility to Fairy and Electric attacks, and the fact that Dark Aura also strengthens opposing Dark moves. Even with those drawbacks, Yveltal's combination of offense, sustain, immunities, and utility gives it one of the broadest competitive resumes among Kalos Legendaries.
nuzlocke: If Legendary Pokemon are permitted, Yveltal is extremely safe in Nuzlockes because of its high HP, two immunities, and access to recovery through Oblivion Wing or Roost in games where available. Oblivion Wing is especially valuable because dealing damage and healing on the same turn reduces the number of vulnerable recovery turns the player must spend. Ground and Psychic moves can provide completely safe switch opportunities, while Dark Aura helps Yveltal secure knockouts without needing setup. Electric, Ice, Rock, and Fairy attacks remain the principal dangers, and Stealth Rock can wear Yveltal down over repeated entries. Timid can be safer than a power-boosting nature when moving first avoids damage, while defensive or mixed natures are reasonable when Yveltal is being used primarily as a bulky pivot.

pokemon.name: Yveltal
pokemon.biologyAndBehavior: Yveltal is the Legendary Pokemon associated with destruction and the absorption of life energy. When its wings and tail spread fully, it can drain life from surrounding living beings, and stories say that at the end of its own roughly thousand-year lifespan it absorbs the life force around it before transforming into a cocoon-like state to sleep. Animated portrayals show victims of this energy drain becoming petrified, while plants can wither simply from Yveltal's contact. Yveltal is not consistently portrayed as malicious, but it is extremely dangerous when enraged or disturbed, and Xerneas is one of the few beings shown capable of calming it or restoring some of the life it removes.

playthrough: Zygarde is a Dragon/Ground Legendary built from Zygarde Cells and Cores and can exist in 10% Forme, 50% Forme, Complete Forme, and now Mega Zygarde. The 10% Forme is the fastest at base 115 Speed but has only base 54 HP and 71 Defense; 50% Forme rises to 108 HP and 121 Defense with base 95 Speed; Complete Forme reaches an extraordinary base 216 HP while retaining 121 Defense and dropping to base 85 Speed. Aura Break reverses the normal power boost from Fairy Aura and Dark Aura, while Power Construct changes a 10% or 50% Zygarde into Complete Forme when its HP falls to half or below under standard ability-enabled mechanics. Thousand Arrows is the family's defining Ground move because it can hit Flying-types, Levitate users, and targets holding Air Balloon, removing one of Ground's normal defensive answers; Extreme Speed, Dragon Dance, Coil, Thousand Waves, Outrage, Core Enforcer, Glare, and Rest add physical, special, or support options. Complete Forme can Mega Evolve using the Zygardite in Legends: Z-A; Mega Zygarde has 216 HP, 216 Special Attack, and 100 Speed but lower Attack and defenses than Complete Forme, and Core Enforcer is replaced by Nihil Light while Mega Evolved. Legends: Z-A itself does not use Abilities, and no ability-enabled Mega Zygarde is currently confirmed, so the Mega should not be assigned an invented Ability. Dragon/Ground is immune to Electric, resists Fire, Poison, and Rock, but is weak to Dragon and Fairy and takes quadruple damage from Ice.
competitive: Zygarde's competitive history changes dramatically by generation and form. In XY, only the 50% Forme was available; it spent most of the generation in UUBL because base 100 Attack and 95 Speed made it look underwhelming beside Garchomp, although its bulk, Dragon/Ground STAB, Dragon Dance, Coil, and Extreme Speed still gave it real OU niches. Sun and Moon transformed Zygarde into a metagame-defining threat by introducing Thousand Arrows and Power Construct: Thousand Arrows bypasses ordinary Ground immunities, while Complete Forme's 216 HP makes it one of the bulkiest Pokemon ever used in standard formats. Power Construct Zygarde proved too strong for OU and became an Ubers fixture, where defensive Coil, Dragon Dance, Glare, Rest, Thousand Arrows, and other sets could pressure both offense and balance. The 10% Forme developed a separate lower-tier identity as a very fast Choice Band or utility attacker because base 115 Speed and Thousand Arrows compensate for its low bulk. Mega Zygarde is too new for an honest long-term singles history; current canon gives it a radical special-attacking stat shift and Nihil Light, so it should be presented as a new Legends: Z-A form rather than retroactively assigned an established competitive resume.
nuzlocke: Zygarde is unusually forgiving if Legendary Pokemon and form mechanics are allowed. The 50% Forme already has strong physical bulk, while a Power Construct Zygarde effectively gains a huge amount of maximum HP when it changes into Complete Forme after falling below half health, creating a dramatic emergency durability boost. The 10% Forme is much frailer but can avoid attacks through base 115 Speed, making it better suited to quick offense than prolonged tanking. Thousand Arrows is exceptionally reliable because it removes the need to predict around Flying-types or Levitate, while Coil can increase Attack, Defense, and accuracy at once for controlled physical setup. Ice attacks are the critical danger to every form because they deal quadruple damage, and strong Fairy or Dragon attacks are also dangerous. Mega Zygarde's 216 Special Attack creates enormous offensive potential, but its Defense and Special Defense are lower than Complete Forme's and its strongest new mechanics are specific to Legends: Z-A, so it should not be treated as simply a bulkier Complete Forme.

pokemon.name: Zygarde
pokemon.biologyAndBehavior: Zygarde 10% Forme forms when roughly one-tenth of the distributed Zygarde Cells gather around a Core. It resembles a fast canine and can run across the ground at speeds exceeding 60 miles per hour, using sharp fangs for close-range attacks. The form cannot be maintained indefinitely because too few Cells are present to stabilize it permanently, and it eventually breaks apart if sustained too long. Its role appears to be rapid response: a Core can assemble a small portion of the overall organism quickly when an ecosystem threat needs immediate investigation.

pokemon.name: Zygarde
pokemon.biologyAndBehavior: Zygarde 50% Forme is the large serpentine body originally encountered in Kalos and is created from roughly half of Zygarde's available Cells. It monitors ecosystems and emerges when it detects serious disruption to the balance of nature. Pokédex lore describes it as merciless toward anything that threatens that balance, while its many hexagonal components emphasize that the body is a coordinated colony rather than a conventional single organism. In Kalos, this form is strongly associated with the mysterious depths of Terminus Cave and with observation rather than constant intervention.

pokemon.name: Zygarde
pokemon.biologyAndBehavior: Complete Forme assembles when Zygarde gathers nearly all of its Cells to confront a threat too dangerous for the 10% or 50% bodies. The resulting humanoid form has immense mass and multiple wing- and arm-like structures built from individual Cell clusters. It is described as Zygarde's full power for protecting the ecosystem, emerging only when the natural order faces an extreme crisis. Different portions of its body can act as specialized structures, and the central Core coordinates the enormous network of Cells as a single organism.

pokemon.name: Zygarde
pokemon.biologyAndBehavior: Mega Zygarde can only be reached from Complete Forme. Mega Evolution redistributes many of the Cells that make up Complete Zygarde, opening much of the lower body and replacing the old wing structures with six smaller arm-like appendages that support a gigantic cannon above its head. When the cannon fires, symbols resembling X, Y, and Z illuminate across the muzzle before it releases Nihil Light, an attack described as defying the laws of nature and powerful enough to counter catastrophic energy threatening Lumiose City. The form has been called Lumiose's Guardian and represents Zygarde concentrating the ecosystem's defensive power into a much more specialized ranged-energy configuration.

playthrough: Diancie is a Rock/Fairy Mythical Pokemon and a rare spontaneous mutation of Carbink rather than an evolution of Carbink. Standard Diancie has base 150 Defense and Special Defense but only base 50 HP and Speed, with balanced base 100 Attack and Special Attack; Moonblast, Diamond Storm, Power Gem, Stealth Rock, Body Press in later generations, Calm Mind, Trick Room, and coverage support either a bulky attacker or slow utility role. Clear Body prevents opposing effects from lowering Diancie's stats. Mega Diancie keeps Rock/Fairy typing but radically redistributes the stats to base 160 Attack, 160 Special Attack, 110 Speed, and 110 in both defenses; Magic Bounce reflects many status moves, entry hazards, Taunt, and other non-damaging effects back at the user. Rock/Fairy grants a Dragon immunity and useful Normal, Fire, Flying, Bug, and Dark resistances, but Water, Grass, and Ground are super effective and Steel deals quadruple damage. Standard Diancie appreciates Brave, Quiet, Relaxed, or Sassy natures under Trick Room, while Mega Diancie usually prefers Hasty, Naive, Timid, or other offensive Speed-oriented natures.
competitive: Standard Diancie has historically been a niche lower-tier defensive Pokemon despite its Mythical status because base 50 HP and Speed limit the value of its 150/150 defenses. Stealth Rock, Heal Bell in older formats, Diamond Storm, Moonblast, and Trick Room can still give it useful support roles. Mega Diancie is a completely different competitive threat. In ORAS OU, base 160 mixed offenses, base 110 Speed, strong Rock/Fairy STAB, Earth Power, Hidden Power or other coverage, and Magic Bounce made it one of the generation's premier offensive Mega Evolutions: it could punish hazard setters and status users while threatening immediate damage from either side. Diamond Storm also gained extra value as a physical Rock attack with a chance to raise Defense, allowing mixed sets to punish special walls. Mega Diancie's main drawback is that the Mega form's defenses fall from 150 to 110 while base HP remains only 50, so it depends heavily on Speed, prediction, and Magic Bounce rather than conventional tanking.
nuzlocke: Diancie is very durable against neutral attacks but must respect type effectiveness because its small HP pool magnifies mistakes. Standard Diancie's base 150 defenses make it excellent for setting Stealth Rock, Trick Room, or Calm Mind against opponents that lack Water, Grass, Ground, or Steel coverage, while Clear Body prevents unexpected stat drops. Steel attacks are the critical danger because they deal quadruple damage and can overwhelm even the huge defensive stats. Mega Diancie becomes much faster and vastly more powerful while Magic Bounce can completely reverse hazards, status, Taunt, and similar disruption, but its defensive stats fall to 110 and it still has only base 50 HP. For a Nuzlocke, Mega Diancie is therefore safest when used to move first and eliminate threats rather than trying to absorb the same hits standard Diancie can.

pokemon.name: Diancie
pokemon.biologyAndBehavior: Diancie is an extraordinarily rare spontaneous mutation of Carbink, although the exact cause of that transformation is unknown. It can compress carbon molecules in the surrounding air between its hands and instantly create diamonds, which it uses for defense, attacks, or ornamentation. Groups of Carbink often gather around Diancie and may treat it like a princess or ruler, while stories describe Diancie protecting companions and living in underground jewel kingdoms. Its body is unusually symmetrical and reflects light with striking brilliance, contributing to its reputation as one of the world's most beautiful Pokemon.

pokemon.name: Diancie
pokemon.biologyAndBehavior: Mega Evolution transforms much of Diancie's rocky lower body into an enormous pink crystal and produces long diamond formations that hang around it like a gown. The diamond on Mega Diancie's forehead is described as weighing roughly 2,000 carats, contributing to the title 'Royal Pink Princess.' Mega Diancie can create and manipulate enormous quantities of diamond material at once and has been depicted shaping those crystals into weapons such as swords. The form trades some of ordinary Diancie's fortress-like appearance for a lighter, faster, more radiant body specialized around overwhelming crystalline power.

playthrough: Hoopa has two major forms with radically different typing and stats. Hoopa Confined is Psychic/Ghost with base 150 Special Attack, 130 Special Defense, 110 Attack, and only 70 Speed; Psychic or Psyshock, Shadow Ball, Hyperspace Hole, Focus Blast, Energy Ball, Thunderbolt, and Nasty Plot or utility allow strong special offense. Using the Prison Bottle changes Hoopa into Hoopa Unbound for a limited period in games that use the original mechanic; Unbound becomes Psychic/Dark and rises to base 160 Attack, 170 Special Attack, and 80 Speed while keeping 130 Special Defense. Magician is the Ability of both forms and steals the target's held item after Hoopa lands a damaging move while holding no item. Confined is immune to Normal and Fighting but is quadruple weak to Ghost and Dark, while Unbound becomes immune to Psychic and is quadruple weak to Bug plus weak to Fairy. Hoopa Unbound uniquely uses Hyperspace Fury, a powerful Dark move that bypasses protection but lowers its Defense. Timid or Modest fit Confined special sets; Unbound can use Timid, Modest, Hasty, Naive, or other mixed natures because both offensive stats are exceptional.
competitive: Hoopa Confined has always been overshadowed by Hoopa Unbound in serious singles play. The Confined form's 150 Special Attack and 130 Special Defense are excellent, but base 60 Defense, base 70 Speed, and quadruple Ghost and Dark weaknesses make it difficult to use consistently. Hoopa Unbound immediately became one of ORAS's most feared wallbreakers: base 170 Special Attack, 160 Attack, Psychic/Dark STAB, Hyperspace Fury, Psyshock, Focus Blast, Gunk Shot, Drain Punch, and broad special coverage allow it to attack almost every defensive Pokemon on the weaker side. It was ultimately banned from standard ORAS OU to Ubers because defensive teams struggled to construct reliable answers without sacrificing too much elsewhere. The price for that power is terrible physical bulk, only base 80 Speed, and a quadruple Bug weakness that makes U-turn especially punishing. Hoopa-U is therefore a historically elite breaker rather than a fast sweeper or defensive pivot.
nuzlocke: Hoopa is powerful but much less forgiving than many Mythical Pokemon because both forms have glaring quadruple weaknesses. Confined Hoopa must avoid Ghost and Dark attacks, while Unbound Hoopa must avoid Bug attacks and should be especially wary of U-turn from faster opponents. Its enormous special offense can still make many battles safe by ending them immediately, and 130 Special Defense gives both forms good protection against neutral special moves. Hyperspace Hole and Hyperspace Fury are reliable against Protect-like defenses, but Hyperspace Fury lowers Hoopa Unbound's Defense after use and can make the already weak physical bulk even more dangerous. Unbound provides far more offensive power but also changes the matchup chart completely, so form choice should be treated as a strategic decision rather than a simple upgrade.

pokemon.name: Hoopa
pokemon.biologyAndBehavior: Hoopa Confined is a mischievous Mythical Pokemon that bends space through golden rings. Those rings can expand dramatically and function as portals, allowing Hoopa to move objects, food, people, or even itself across huge distances without crossing the space in between. It has a strong appetite for valuable or interesting objects and is known for stealing things simply because it finds the act entertaining. The small body represents Hoopa with most of its true power sealed away, but even in this state its control over dimensional portals is extraordinary.

pokemon.name: Hoopa
pokemon.biologyAndBehavior: Hoopa Unbound is described as Hoopa's true form and releases the tremendous power sealed by the Prison Bottle. It gains six enormous arms and can enlarge its rings to several miles across, using them to bend dimensions strongly enough to transport entire islands or enormous structures. One legend says Hoopa greedily moved an entire castle roughly 3,000 years ago to seize treasure hidden inside. The form is far more destructive and arrogant than Confined Hoopa and can remain unsealed only temporarily under the traditional Prison Bottle mechanic before reverting.

playthrough: Volcanion is a single-stage Fire/Water Mythical Pokemon with base 130 Special Attack, 120 Defense, 110 Attack, and only base 70 Speed. Steam Eruption is its signature Water-type special move and combines very high power with a significant burn chance, while Flamethrower or Fire Blast, Sludge Bomb, Earth Power, Focus Blast, Solar Beam, Body Press in later games, Defog in some generations, and coverage give it several offensive or utility roles. Water Absorb grants a complete Water immunity and restores one-quarter of Volcanion's maximum HP when hit by a Water-type attack, which is especially valuable because Water would otherwise hit its Fire typing super effectively. Fire/Water heavily resists Fire, Ice, and Steel, also resists Bug and Fairy, and is weak only to Electric, Ground, and Rock. Its solid 80/120/90 bulk makes it much safer than many wallbreakers, although Stealth Rock and the base 70 Speed can cause problems. Modest is generally best for special offense, while Quiet works well under Trick Room and Bold can support more defensive variants.
competitive: Volcanion made an immediate impact on ORAS OU when it was released late in the generation. Fire/Water typing, Water Absorb, 130 Special Attack, and Steam Eruption let it check or punish many of the metagame's important Water-, Fire-, Steel-, and Fairy-types while still functioning as a powerful wallbreaker. Steam Eruption was often compared to an extremely powerful Scald because its burn chance made physical switch-ins risky even when they resisted Water, while Fire Blast, Sludge Bomb, Earth Power, and other coverage punished traditional Water answers. In later generations Volcanion commonly occupied UU or similar tiers, where Choice Specs, bulky utility, Toxic, and Defog sets all took advantage of its strong defensive profile. Its main limitations are base 70 Speed, Stealth Rock vulnerability, and common Electric-, Ground-, and Rock-type attacks. Unlike many Mythical attackers, Volcanion combines genuine defensive utility with immediate offensive pressure rather than depending entirely on speed or setup.
nuzlocke: Volcanion is unusually safe for an offensive Mythical because Water Absorb creates a full Water immunity and its base 120 Defense makes many physical attacks manageable. Steam Eruption is extremely powerful, but its imperfect accuracy means Flamethrower or another reliable attack can be safer when the matchup does not require maximum damage. Fire/Water gives many useful resistances and only Electric, Ground, and Rock weaknesses, creating a relatively simple matchup chart compared with most dual-type Legendaries and Mythicals. Base 70 Speed means Volcanion often takes the first hit, so known Ground or Electric coverage should not be challenged merely because its overall bulk is good. Modest provides excellent damage without recoil, while a bulkier nature can create an even larger margin in long fights.

pokemon.name: Volcanion
pokemon.biologyAndBehavior: Volcanion stores water inside its body and contains an organ that can instantly heat that water into steam. The two cannon-like arms on its back vent the steam at extraordinary pressure, producing blasts powerful enough to reshape terrain, gouge the earth, or according to legend blow away mountains. Volcanion can also use the cannons as propulsion to fly or maneuver, create dense fog for concealment, and manipulate objects. Its water supply is finite; when depleted it cannot use its Water-based abilities until it finds another source, and stories portray Volcanion as a centuries-old Pokemon inhabiting remote mountains or swamps where humans rarely travel.

playthrough: Rowlet evolves into Dartrix at level 17. In most regions Dartrix evolves into Decidueye at level 34, while in Hisui it evolves into Hisuian Decidueye at level 36. Standard Decidueye is Grass/Ghost with base 107 Attack, 100 Special Attack, 100 Special Defense, and 70 Speed, giving it unusual freedom to run physical, special, or mixed sets. Leaf Blade, Spirit Shackle, Shadow Sneak, Brave Bird, U-turn, Roost, Swords Dance, Nasty Plot, and later coverage let it attack or support according to the game. Overgrow boosts Grass moves at low HP, while Long Reach prevents its attacks from making contact, avoiding effects such as Rocky Helmet, Static, Flame Body, or contact-triggered abilities. Hisuian Decidueye becomes Grass/Fighting with 112 Attack, 88 HP, and only 60 Speed; Scrappy lets its Normal- and Fighting-type moves hit Ghost-types and also prevents Intimidate from lowering its Attack. Triple Arrows is its defining Fighting STAB, combining reliable damage with multiple useful secondary effects. Adamant or Jolly suit physical standard Decidueye, Timid or Modest can support special sets, and Adamant or Jolly are natural for Hisuian Decidueye.
competitive: Standard Decidueye spent Generation VII primarily in NU but had meaningful UU utility as a flexible wallbreaker and support Pokemon. Nasty Plot allowed special sets to pressure defensive answers, while Spirit Shackle, Swords Dance, U-turn, Roost, and Defog gave physical or utility sets very different matchups. Its Grass/Ghost typing provides two immunities and several useful resistances, but base 70 Speed leaves it vulnerable to faster Dark-, Ghost-, Fire-, Flying-, and Ice-type attackers. Hisuian Decidueye has developed a separate lower-tier identity in Generation IX: its stronger base 112 Attack, Scrappy, Triple Arrows, Leaf Blade, Close Combat, and U-turn make it a strong Choice Scarf user or physical breaker. Scrappy is particularly important because it removes both Ghost immunity to Fighting and Intimidate as conventional counterplay. Neither form is a sustained upper-tier staple, but both have legitimate niches built around very different attacking profiles.
nuzlocke: The Rowlet line is generally reliable in Nuzlockes because it evolves on a normal starter schedule and gains useful immunities or resistances in either final form. Standard Decidueye is immune to Normal and Fighting and can recover with Roost in games where available, but Fire, Ice, Flying, Ghost, and Dark attacks are all dangerous. Long Reach is excellent insurance because physical attacks can avoid many contact-triggered effects that would otherwise create surprise chip or status. Hisuian Decidueye trades the two immunities for stronger physical offense and Scrappy, but gains a quadruple Flying weakness plus weaknesses to Fire, Ice, Poison, Psychic, and Fairy. Triple Arrows is powerful and reliable enough to be one of the safer offensive tools in the family. Adamant is a strong general choice, while Jolly can be safer when an important speed threshold prevents a retaliation.

pokemon.name: Rowlet
pokemon.biologyAndBehavior: Rowlet is a nocturnal owl-like Pokemon that stores energy during the day through photosynthesis. It glides almost silently toward targets before attacking with kicks or with leaf-like feathers sharp enough to function as projectiles. Rowlet has excellent night vision and can rotate its head almost 180 degrees to watch its surroundings without moving its body. It feels especially secure in tight, dark spaces.

pokemon.name: Dartrix
pokemon.biologyAndBehavior: Dartrix carries sharp blade quills beneath the leafy plumage of its wings and can throw them with enough precision to strike targets it cannot directly see. By bending the quills before launch, it can alter their flight path in mid-attack. Dartrix is extremely image-conscious and spends a large amount of time preening; dirty or damaged plumage can distract it badly enough to affect its performance. A patient Trainer who helps it through this self-conscious stage can bring out much more of its potential.

pokemon.name: Decidueye
pokemon.biologyAndBehavior: Alolan Decidueye is a cool, cautious archer that hides arrow quills among the feathers of its wings. It can pluck, aim, and fire one in roughly a tenth of a second and is accurate enough to strike tiny targets from well over a hundred yards away. Pulling the vines on its leafy hood narrows its field of view and helps it concentrate when a shot absolutely cannot miss. Despite its composure, sudden surprises can make Decidueye panic.

pokemon.name: Decidueye
pokemon.biologyAndBehavior: Hisuian Decidueye has thicker legs, reduced wing area, and feather structures that trap air to insulate it against Hisui's extreme cold. It is more nomadic and more willing to fight at close range than the Alolan form, wandering widely in search of food. Its kicks are powerful enough to knock down trees and shatter boulders. In battle it often closes distance with flying kicks before following with hidden arrow quills, combining an archer's precision with a much more physical style.

playthrough: Litten evolves into Torracat at level 17 and Incineroar at level 34. Incineroar is Fire/Dark with base 115 Attack, 95 HP, 90 Defense, 90 Special Defense, and only 60 Speed, making it a slow but powerful physical attacker and pivot. Flare Blitz, Darkest Lariat, Knock Off, U-turn or Parting Shot depending on generation, Fake Out, Drain Punch or Close Combat, Earthquake, Will-O-Wisp, and Bulk Up give it both offensive and support options. Blaze strengthens Fire moves at low HP, while the Hidden Ability Intimidate lowers opposing Attack on entry and is usually the most valuable ability by a wide margin. Fire/Dark grants a Psychic immunity and resistances to Fire, Grass, Ice, Ghost, Dark, and Steel, but Water, Fighting, Ground, and Rock are super effective. Adamant is excellent for straightforward play, Careful or Impish fit bulkier sets, and Brave is useful under Trick Room.
competitive: Incineroar has one of the most important doubles resumes of any starter Pokemon. Intimidate, Fake Out, Knock Off, U-turn or Parting Shot, Snarl, solid 95/90/90 bulk, and useful Fire/Dark resistances allow it to control board position while repeatedly reducing incoming damage for its team. It became a cornerstone of VGC and other doubles formats because almost every team appreciates some combination of Intimidate, Fake Out disruption, item removal, and safe pivoting. In Generation VII singles it was only NU by usage, but Smogon still regarded it as a flexible wallbreaker and defensive pivot whose base 115 Attack and broad coverage were genuinely threatening. Its low base 60 Speed, Stealth Rock weakness, Flare Blitz recoil, and lack of dependable instant recovery keep it from being equally dominant in singles. Competitive Incineroar is therefore a rare case where its doubles legacy is substantially greater than its singles tier history.
nuzlocke: Incineroar is one of the safer physical starters in a Nuzlocke because Intimidate effectively improves the entire team's physical durability every time it enters battle. Its own 95/90/90 bulk is solid, and the Psychic immunity creates a completely safe switch against known Psychic moves. Flare Blitz is extremely strong but recoil can accumulate quickly, so a lower-power Fire option may be preferable when it still secures the knockout. Water, Fighting, Ground, and Rock attacks are the main dangers, and the low Speed means Incineroar commonly takes damage before acting. Fake Out, U-turn, and later Parting Shot can all reduce risk by creating controlled turns rather than forcing Incineroar to remain exposed.

pokemon.name: Litten
pokemon.biologyAndBehavior: Litten is a solitary cat Pokemon that rarely displays its emotions openly and may scratch people who try to pet it before earning its trust. While grooming, it swallows large amounts of loose fur and stores that material inside its body. It later ignites the accumulated fur and coughs it out as fireballs, with different coughing patterns producing different flame attacks. Regular grooming is therefore directly tied to both its cleanliness and its fire-producing biology.

pokemon.name: Torracat
pokemon.biologyAndBehavior: Torracat has a bell-like flame sac hanging at its neck that brightens and burns hotter as its emotions and fighting spirit rise. The organ rings when Torracat produces fire and can even absorb flames from outside sources and convert them into its own power. Its forelegs become dramatically stronger during this stage, with blows powerful enough to bend iron. Torracat remains agile and feline, but its growing physical power foreshadows Incineroar's close-range fighting style.

pokemon.name: Incineroar
pokemon.biologyAndBehavior: Incineroar produces a belt of fire from its waist and navel that intensifies with its fighting spirit, reaching temperatures of roughly 3,600 degrees Fahrenheit. It fights like a theatrical heel wrestler, using brutal punches, kicks, and fire attacks while deliberately playing to the crowd. Incineroar can be rough, egotistical, and difficult to command when uninterested, but it loses enthusiasm for fighting weak or injured opponents and becomes genuinely excited by strong challengers. Beneath the villainous persona it enjoys admiration from children and young Pokemon and is willing to protect or help them.

playthrough: Popplio evolves into Brionne at level 17 and Primarina at level 34. Primarina is Water/Fairy with base 126 Special Attack, 116 Special Defense, 80 HP, and only 60 Speed, making it a powerful slow special attacker and special tank. Surf or Hydro Pump, Moonblast, Sparkling Aria, Ice Beam, Psychic, Energy Ball, Calm Mind, Encore, Haze, and later Psychic Noise or Flip Turn give it excellent offensive and utility options. Torrent strengthens Water attacks at low HP, while Liquid Voice converts sound-based moves into Water-type moves, allowing Hyper Voice and later sound moves to function as Water STAB. Water/Fairy is an excellent defensive typing with a Dragon immunity and resistances to Fire, Water, Ice, Fighting, Bug, and Dark, while Electric, Grass, and Poison are super effective. Modest is usually ideal, while Bold or Calm can emphasize Primarina's bulk and Timid is rarely necessary because base 60 Speed remains low.
competitive: Primarina entered Generation VII as a strong UU wallbreaker thanks to base 126 Special Attack, Water/Fairy STAB, excellent special bulk, and the ability to punish common Dragon-, Dark-, Fire-, and Fighting-types. Choice Specs, Calm Mind, bulky RestTalk, and later Assault Vest or pivot sets all exploited the difficulty of switching safely into Moonblast plus strong Water attacks. Its main historical weakness is base 60 Speed and only base 74 Defense, forcing it to absorb physical attacks before moving. In Generation IX Primarina rose all the way to OU and became a legitimate special tank and offensive pivot, checking threats such as Walking Wake, Dragapult, Darkrai, and Iron Valiant while using tools like Psychic Noise and Flip Turn. Liquid Voice creates specialized sound-based Water sets, although Torrent is often preferred when direct Water moves provide better immediate value. Primarina's competitive trajectory is therefore unusually strong for a slow starter: its typing, special stats, and expanding utility movepool have aged extremely well.
nuzlocke: Primarina is one of the safest Alola starters against special attackers because base 116 Special Defense, Water/Fairy typing, and a Dragon immunity create a large margin for error. Surf and Moonblast are both accurate, dependable STAB moves, while Sparkling Aria is another strong Water option and Calm Mind can make special matchups increasingly secure. Electric, Grass, and Poison attacks remain dangerous, and strong physical neutral hits deserve respect because base 74 Defense is much lower than the special bulk. Encore and Haze can provide valuable emergency control in games where they are available. Modest usually offers the best balance of power and safety because Primarina is slow regardless of nature.

pokemon.name: Popplio
pokemon.biologyAndBehavior: Popplio creates water bubbles through its nose and controls them with exceptional precision. On land it uses the bubbles' elasticity to perform acrobatic jumps and battle maneuvers, practicing every day with progressively larger bubbles until their bursting force becomes a serious weapon. It can swim at roughly 25 miles per hour. Popplio is notably hardworking and learns its performance skills through persistent repetition rather than effortless talent.

pokemon.name: Brionne
pokemon.biologyAndBehavior: Brionne is a highly skilled dancer that learns new routines by imitating both other members of its colony and humans. Groups can perform in perfect synchronization under moonlight, sometimes following the singing of a Primarina. Brionne creates colorful water balloons while dancing and uses the motion to distract opponents before striking the balloons toward them to explode. It is emotionally sensitive but normally hides sadness, revealing genuine distress only to individuals it deeply trusts.

pokemon.name: Primarina
pokemon.biologyAndBehavior: Primarina treats battle like a stage performance, combining dance, song, and precisely controlled water balloons. Its voice is essential to its fighting style and must be carefully maintained; songs used by the species are passed down through generations. Some of its water balloons are harmless platforms that Primarina uses for movement, while others explode when touched. In moonlight the floating balloons create a glittering display, allowing Primarina to disguise dangerous attacks inside an elaborate performance.

playthrough: Pikipek evolves into Trumbeak at level 14 and Toucannon at level 28, making the line fully evolved unusually early for a regional bird. Toucannon is Normal/Flying with base 120 Attack, 80 HP, 75/75 defenses, and only 60 Speed. Brave Bird and Beak Blast provide strong Flying STAB, while Boomburst, Bullet Seed, Rock Blast, Knock Off, Brick Break, Overheat, U-turn, and other coverage let it attack from both sides despite the physical bias. Skill Link guarantees the maximum number of hits from multi-hit moves, turning Bullet Seed into a reliable 125-base-power coverage attack and similarly strengthening Rock Blast; Keen Eye prevents accuracy reduction, while the Hidden Ability Sheer Force boosts moves with secondary effects by 30 percent while removing those effects. Beak Blast is particularly distinctive because Toucannon heats its beak before firing, burning an opponent that makes contact during the charging phase. Normal/Flying grants Ghost and Ground immunities but is weak to Electric, Ice, and Rock. Adamant or Brave work well for physical sets, while Rash or Quiet can support mixed offense.
competitive: Toucannon has remained a lower-tier Pokemon, but its wallbreaking niche is real. Base 120 Attack makes Brave Bird immediately dangerous, while Skill Link turns Bullet Seed into reliable high-power Grass coverage that can break Rock- and Water-types that would otherwise handle Flying STAB. Its usable base 75 Special Attack also supports Boomburst and Overheat, allowing mixed sets to punish physical walls and Steel-types. Smogon's Sun and Moon analyses describe Toucannon as a strong PU or ZU wallbreaker but emphasize its poor base 60 Speed, merely average bulk, Stealth Rock weakness, and recoil from Brave Bird or Life Orb. Beak Blast can punish contact attackers with burn, but its negative priority means Toucannon must survive the incoming hit first. It is best viewed as a slow breaker with excellent coverage rather than a conventional fast regional bird.
nuzlocke: Toucannon is useful in Nuzlockes because it reaches its final form at level 28 and has base 120 Attack much earlier than many comparable physical attackers. Ground and Ghost immunities create safe switch opportunities, while Skill Link makes Bullet Seed and Rock Blast fully reliable in hit count rather than leaving damage to chance. Brave Bird is extremely strong but recoil can accumulate quickly, so Drill Peck or other safer Flying moves are preferable when they already secure a knockout. Electric, Ice, and Rock attacks are the main dangers, and Stealth Rock can wear Toucannon down before it acts. Beak Blast can burn contact attackers before their move lands, which is valuable defensive utility if Toucannon can safely absorb the hit.

pokemon.name: Pikipek
pokemon.biologyAndBehavior: Pikipek has unusually powerful neck muscles and can strike wood as many as sixteen times per second without injuring itself. It drills holes in trees for nests, food storage, and collections of small shiny objects, while the rhythm of its pecking also functions as communication with other Pikipek. It eats Berries and can spit the leftover seeds with enough force to embed them in tree trunks. Talonflame is a known predator, while Pikipek itself preys on small Bug Pokemon such as Metapod.

pokemon.name: Trumbeak
pokemon.biologyAndBehavior: Trumbeak has a flexible beak capable of producing more than one hundred distinct calls, making it notoriously noisy in wooded habitats. It stores Berry seeds in its beak and fires them in rapid bursts at enemies or prey. Many of the seeds it scatters later germinate, giving Trumbeak an unintended role in spreading plants through the forests it inhabits. Its vocal flexibility and seed-projectile behavior form the transition between Pikipek's drilling and Toucannon's weaponized beak.

pokemon.name: Toucannon
pokemon.biologyAndBehavior: Toucannon stores combustible gases inside its enormous beak and can heat the structure beyond the boiling point of water. It ignites those gases to launch seeds with enough force to shatter boulders, while direct contact with the heated beak can cause severe burns. The colors of the beak intensify as its temperature rises. Toucannon can also use that warmth gently, including warming eggs, showing that the same biological furnace functions in both combat and care.

playthrough: Yungoos evolves into Gumshoos starting at level 20 during the day. Gumshoos is a pure Normal physical attacker with base 110 Attack, 88 HP, and only 45 Speed, so it functions as a slow wallbreaker rather than a sweeper. Return in older generations or Body Slam, Double-Edge, Crunch, Earthquake, Fire Fang, Ice Fang, Thunder Fang, U-turn, and coverage give it straightforward physical options. Stakeout doubles the power of Gumshoos's moves against a target that switched in that turn, making predicted switches extremely punishing; Strong Jaw boosts bite-based moves by 50 percent, while the Hidden Ability Adaptability raises Normal STAB from 1.5× to 2×. Pure Normal grants a Ghost immunity and only one weakness, Fighting, but provides almost no resistances. Adamant is usually the best nature because Gumshoos's base 45 Speed is difficult to salvage, while Brave is appropriate under Trick Room.
competitive: Gumshoos has historically remained in ZU or similarly low tiers despite its impressive base 110 Attack. Stakeout can make predicted switches enormously costly because the damage multiplier effectively punishes the opponent for trying to bring in a defensive answer, and Choice Band or strong Normal STAB can produce real wallbreaking power. Strong Jaw expands bite-based coverage, while Adaptability can make Normal attacks consistently stronger without relying on a switch. Smogon nevertheless describes Gumshoos as difficult to justify over more complete Normal-type wallbreakers because base 45 Speed and only 88/60/60 bulk make it easy to revenge kill and hard to bring onto the field repeatedly. Its niche is therefore prediction-heavy immediate damage rather than sustained competitive consistency.
nuzlocke: Gumshoos can be useful in a Nuzlocke because pure Normal has only one conventional weakness and base 110 Attack provides strong damage very early after evolving at level 20. Ghost immunity can create safe switches, while Adaptability or Stakeout can shorten fights without requiring setup. The main weakness is speed: base 45 means Gumshoos usually takes the first hit, and 60/60 defenses are not strong enough to absorb repeated neutral damage comfortably. Fighting moves are especially dangerous and should be avoided rather than tested against its HP stat. Adamant makes the most of its best attribute, while reliable Body Slam or similar attacks are safer than lower-accuracy coverage when neutral damage is enough.

pokemon.name: Yungoos
pokemon.biologyAndBehavior: Yungoos has an enormous appetite and spends most of its waking time roaming its territory in search of fresh food. Much of its body is devoted to its stomach, and it digests meals so quickly that hunger returns almost immediately. Its teeth are strong enough to crush very hard objects, and it may continue foraging until it collapses from exhaustion. Yungoos is not native to Alola; it was introduced from elsewhere as part of an attempt to control other pest Pokemon.

pokemon.name: Gumshoos
pokemon.biologyAndBehavior: Gumshoos is a patient ambush hunter that studies the routes used by prey and waits in one place until the target appears. It can tolerate hunger for long periods while staking out a location, but its stamina runs out around sunset and it falls asleep wherever it happens to be. Alolan Rattata and Raticate are preferred prey, yet Gumshoos is active during the day while those Pokemon are primarily nocturnal, making encounters between them less common than intended. Like Yungoos, Gumshoos was introduced to Alola rather than originating there.

playthrough: Grubbin is an early-game Bug-type in Alola and evolves into Charjabug at level 20, so the line can contribute for most of a playthrough rather than arriving only near the end. Charjabug gains the useful Bug/Electric typing and respectable physical bulk, but its low Speed and modest Special Attack make it feel more like a durable transitional stage than the finished attacker; its Battery Ability is primarily valuable in doubles because it boosts an ally's special moves rather than Charjabug's own attacks. The largest issue in the original Sun and Moon is evolution timing: Charjabug must level up in Vast Poni Canyon's special magnetic field, delaying Vikavolt until very late, whereas Ultra Sun and Ultra Moon add the much earlier Blush Mountain as another valid magnetic field. From Generation VIII onward a Thunder Stone can evolve Charjabug, removing that major pacing problem in games where the line is available. Vikavolt is extremely slow at base 43 Speed but compensates with enormous base 145 Special Attack, Levitate, only two normal type weaknesses in Fire and Rock, and strong special STAB such as Thunderbolt or Discharge and Bug Buzz; Energy Ball and Volt Switch can add coverage and momentum where available. Modest is generally the most straightforward beneficial Nature for ordinary use because Vikavolt rarely wins important Speed races anyway, while Quiet is sensible on deliberately slow or Trick Room-oriented teams.
competitive: Vikavolt has spent most of its singles history in the lower usage tiers, but it has repeatedly earned real niches rather than functioning as a generic low-tier attacker. In Generation VII it was classified as NU while also receiving RU and VGC 2017 analyses: its base 145 Special Attack made it a dangerous wallbreaker, while Bug/Electric typing plus Levitate let it exploit matchups against several Grass-, Fighting-, Steel-, and Ground-reliant Pokémon. Its very low Speed could actually be useful on pivoting sets because a slow Volt Switch often brought a teammate onto the field without that teammate taking the opponent's attack, although Vikavolt itself had to be able to absorb the hit. In VGC 2017, the combination of Levitate, strong special damage, respectable bulk, and Electroweb gave it a distinct speed-control role, even though it was never one of the format's defining stars. Later generations expanded its identity through Sticky Web, letting it operate as a bulky hazard setter as well as a wallbreaker; in Scarlet and Violet it is currently listed in ZU, where Smogon describes it as a powerful Sticky Web setter and tank that pressures opposing removal with its STAB and coverage. Its recurring limitations are the same across eras—base 43 Speed, vulnerability to Rock hazards before Heavy-Duty Boots became available, and competition from faster Electric-types—but its exceptional Special Attack and Levitate have kept it from being wholly outclassed.
nuzlocke: This line is most dependable in a Nuzlocke when treated as a slow, sturdy attacker rather than something expected to sweep without taking damage. Grubbin is available early in Alola, but the long period spent as Charjabug can be awkward in Sun and Moon because Vikavolt is locked behind the late-game magnetic field; Ultra Sun and Ultra Moon substantially improve the line by permitting evolution at Blush Mountain, and Thunder Stone evolution in later games is safer still. Charjabug's good Defense can make it surprisingly resilient to physical neutral hits, and Eviolite can improve that role further when available, but its low Speed means critical hits and unexpected coverage must always be respected. Vikavolt's Levitate creates a valuable Ground immunity, and its Electric, Fighting, Grass, and Steel resistances give it several comparatively safe switch opportunities, while reliable attacks such as Thunderbolt and Bug Buzz avoid the unnecessary variance of inaccurate alternatives. Its biggest Nuzlocke liability is base 43 Speed: even when it can score a knockout, it often has to survive an attack first, so blind switching against an unknown moveset is risky. A slow Volt Switch can be excellent for bringing a frailer teammate in safely after Vikavolt absorbs a hit, but that tactic should be reserved for matchups where Vikavolt's bulk and typing make the incoming damage predictable.

pokemon.name: Grubbin
pokemon.biologyAndBehavior: Grubbin normally lives underground, where its oversized mandibles serve as weapons, digging tools, and implements for scraping trees to obtain sap. It can fire sticky threads from its mouth to swing from surfaces or immobilize prey and opponents before seizing them with jaws strong enough to snap thick branches. Bird Pokémon such as Rookidee and Hoothoot are natural enemies, yet they may avoid confronting it because being trapped by those mandibles is dangerous. Grubbin is attracted to electricity and may live near power plants or Electric-type Pokémon; gathering around Electric Pokémon also helps discourage attacks from bird-like predators. It constructs nests underground with its mandibles and has been observed sleeping buried in dirt.

pokemon.name: Charjabug
pokemon.biologyAndBehavior: Charjabug spends much of its time half-buried in earth or fallen leaves, remaining comparatively still while it consumes humus in preparation for further evolution. Digestion generates electricity inside an electric sac, and a fully charged Charjabug can store enough power to run a household for an entire day. That energy can be supplied to other Pokémon, making Charjabug a literal biological battery and explaining its unique Battery Ability; people on camping trips are also said to appreciate having one nearby. Its stout shell gives it protection while it remains relatively immobile, and particularly persistent threats can be shocked from the tips of its jaws. Charjabug can communicate with nearby Grubbin using sound waves, and Vikavolt may physically carry one as an auxiliary power source.

pokemon.name: Vikavolt
pokemon.biologyAndBehavior: Vikavolt is a beetle-like predator with a large electric organ in its abdomen and enormous mandibles that focus the stored energy into powerful electromagnetic beams; it is specifically described as using these attacks to strike down bird Pokémon. It can clasp a Charjabug between its legs and use the smaller Pokémon as an additional battery, allowing it to fire electrical beams in rapid succession. During especially demanding aerial battles it releases Charjabug, sacrificing the extra energy supply to become lighter and more maneuverable. Despite its very low battle Speed statistic, canon describes Vikavolt as an exceptionally agile flier in its natural environment, capable of tailspins, sharp turns, and high-speed movement through tangled forest branches. It has documented rivalries with Pinsir and Heracross and has been shown feeding on tree sap. Pokémon Sleep further depicts it remaining airborne while sleeping after exhausting its electricity in battle, then hanging upside down while asleep to replenish electrical energy in its abdomen.

playthrough: Crabrawler provides strong physical Fighting-type damage fairly early in Alola, but its evolution has one of the most game-dependent timing differences in this batch. In Sun and Moon it must level up at Mount Lanakila, an area the player cannot properly enter until very late in the story, so a large portion of the game is spent using the much weaker Crabrawler; Ultra Sun and Ultra Moon allow access to the mountain's base after reaching Tapu Village, making Crabominable obtainable substantially earlier. From Scarlet and Violet onward an Ice Stone can trigger the evolution, eliminating the location restriction entirely. Crabominable brings an excellent base 132 Attack and powerful Fighting/Ice STAB, with Iron Fist strengthening many of the punching moves it naturally wants to use, but base 43 Speed and weaknesses to Fire, Fighting, Flying, Psychic, Steel, and Fairy make it far less durable in practice than its 97 HP may initially suggest. Drain Punch is especially attractive in normal play because it combines STAB, Iron Fist synergy, and recovery; Ice Hammer hits much harder than Ice Punch but its imperfect accuracy and Speed drop add drawbacks, while Close Combat's defensive drops matter more in a long route or boss sequence than they do on a one-off damage calculation. Mega Crabominable, introduced much later in Pokémon Legends: Z-A's Mega Dimension content and now usable in Pokémon Champions, dramatically raises Attack and both defenses while becoming even slower, so Adamant suits maximum ordinary damage while Brave becomes especially natural under Trick Room.
competitive: Standard Crabominable has always been defined by an excellent offensive concept fighting against severe structural flaws. In Generation VII it found a meaningful PU niche as a wallbreaker: base 132 Attack, Fighting/Ice STAB, Iron Fist, and coverage let it punish defensive teams, while Assault Vest and Trick Room sets could partially compensate for its poor Speed and awkward defensive typing. It never became a high-tier singles staple because base 43 Speed forces it to take hits, its six weaknesses make those hits difficult to manage, and other Fighting-types often provide more Speed, defensive utility, or consistency. Scarlet and Violet currently place the base form in ZU, where Choice Band and Bulk Up sets still exploit Ice Hammer, Close Combat or Drain Punch, Knock Off, and broad coverage, but its basic limitations remain unchanged. Mega Crabominable is a genuinely new competitive chapter rather than an old reputation: its 2026 form has 157 Attack, 122 Defense, 107 Special Defense, only 33 Speed, and Iron Fist, producing a very bulky physical breaker with exceptionally strong priority Mach Punch and powerful Drain Punch or Ice Hammer. Smogon's current Pokémon Champions dex lists Mega Crabominable in UU, and early 2026 tournament/ladder data show real usage, particularly alongside forms of speed control such as Trick Room; because the Mega has existed for only a short time, it is more accurate to describe it as an emerging competitive threat than to assign it a decades-long historical standing.
nuzlocke: Crabrawler can hit hard for an unevolved Pokémon, but its mediocre bulk means it is not a safe answer to every opponent that happens to be weak to Fighting. The biggest run-to-run issue in original Sun and Moon is keeping Crabrawler alive until the very late Mount Lanakila evolution point; Ultra Sun and Ultra Moon's earlier access and Scarlet/Violet's Ice Stone method greatly reduce that risk. Crabominable's high HP and enormous Attack are useful, but its Fighting/Ice typing carries six weaknesses and no immunities, while base 43 Speed means it commonly takes damage before acting. Iron Fist-boosted Drain Punch is one of its best Nuzlocke tools because it converts its offensive strength into healing, whereas Ice Hammer's 90% accuracy and Speed reduction and Close Combat's Defense and Special Defense drops introduce avoidable danger when safer alternatives can secure the same knockout. Mach Punch can provide valuable emergency priority in games where it is available, while Anger Point should never be treated as a safety strategy because intentionally relying on an enemy critical hit is the opposite of variance control. If Mega Crabominable is available under the ruleset being played, its huge defensive gains make it much more forgiving of a damage estimate that is slightly wrong, but its very low Speed and numerous common weaknesses still demand careful matchup selection.

pokemon.name: Crabrawler
pokemon.biologyAndBehavior: Crabrawler is intensely competitive and seeks both social superiority and literal high ground, clinging to buildings, tall people, and large Pokémon and becoming violent when someone tries to remove it. Its hard pincers protect vulnerable areas such as its head and stomach while it closes distance to punch, and those blows are powerful enough to split tree trunks. The pincers frequently break off from overuse but regenerate quickly; the small amount of meat inside detached claws is considered rich and delicious and has culinary uses. Crabrawler is particularly fond of Berries and punches trees to knock ripe fruit down, but groups may gather at the same tree and fight until only one remains to eat. It also preys on Exeggcute and has been known to mistake Alolan Exeggutor for a coconut tree, sometimes provoking the much larger Pokémon into shaking it off and stomping it.

pokemon.name: Crabominable
pokemon.biologyAndBehavior: Crabominable's thick fur and Ice typing are described as adaptations that developed after a Crabrawler became lost while climbing into the bitter cold of snowy mountains. Its pincers store cold energy and are freezing to the touch, and its punches can break thick ice walls or, according to recorded accounts, force back avalanches. It is impulsive and tends to start punching before it thinks, yet its actual movement is sluggish; it compensates by blowing icy bubbles from its mouth to immobilize opponents before closing in. In desperate situations it can even launch its own pincers like rockets, while detached pincers are again considered edible enough that some Trainers bring Lechonk into the mountains specifically to search for them. This combination of powerful cold-storing claws, insulating fur, and slow terrestrial movement makes the species' mountain adaptation much more explicit than a simple cosmetic change from Crabrawler.

pokemon.name: Crabominable
pokemon.biologyAndBehavior: Mega Evolution makes Crabominable substantially larger and bulkier, covering the ends of its enormous pincers in dense, spiked layers of ice while its body is supported primarily by its rearmost pair of ice-encased legs. Its strength rises enough that a light swing of an ice-covered fist can pulverize reinforced concrete, and it can use the oversized pincers along with its legs to help propel itself forward. Canon specifically warns that a battle between two Mega Crabominable can threaten to destroy the surrounding area, giving this newly introduced form an unusually direct statement about the environmental danger of its physical power.

playthrough: Oricorio does not evolve, but its four Styles effectively let one team slot change secondary role by using Red, Yellow, Pink, or Purple Nectar: Baile is Fire/Flying, Pom-Pom is Electric/Flying, Pa'u is Psychic/Flying, and Sensu is Ghost/Flying. All four share the same 75/70/70/98/70/93 base stats and the same core special-attacking identity, while Revelation Dance becomes the user's primary type and therefore supplies a reliable 90-power STAB attack that automatically follows the chosen Style. In Alola, Pom-Pom is available very early at Melemele Meadow and the other wild Styles appear on later islands, while Nectar lets the player deliberately convert between them; Scarlet and Violet likewise allow form switching with Nectar even though only some Styles are naturally encountered in the base region. Pom-Pom is often the safest all-purpose form because Electric/Flying has only Ice and Rock weaknesses and a Ground immunity, while Sensu offers three immunities to Normal, Fighting, and Ground; Baile supplies useful Fire offense but suffers a severe 4× Rock weakness, and Pa'u trades those advantages for Psychic STAB. Generation IX dramatically improved the line by giving Oricorio Quiver Dance, allowing one turn to raise Special Attack, Special Defense, and Speed; earlier games instead leaned more on Calm Mind, Roost, and direct attacking. Timid is valuable when preserving Oricorio's good but not elite base 93 Speed matters, while Modest is a legitimate alternative on bulkier or Quiver Dance sets that can obtain Speed boosts after setup.
competitive: Oricorio's competitive history is unusually form-dependent because every Style has identical stats and movepool access but a different primary typing. In Generation VII, Pom-Pom and Sensu were the most respected lower-tier variants: Pom-Pom's Electric/Flying typing offered excellent defensive efficiency, while Sensu's Ghost/Flying typing supplied Normal and Fighting immunities and even let it block Rapid Spin; Baile and Pa'u were both placed in ZU and were commonly outclassed by those two alternatives. Baile's most damaging historical flaw was its 4× Stealth Rock weakness before Heavy-Duty Boots existed, while Pa'u lacked enough unique defensive or offensive value to justify choosing it over stronger Psychic-types or the better Oricorio forms. Generation IX was the pivotal buff because Oricorio gained Quiver Dance; combined with Roost and Revelation Dance, that move transformed the species from a mostly Calm Mind-based lower-tier utility attacker into a much more dangerous setup sweeper. Current Scarlet/Violet tiering reflects the distinction between forms: Pom-Pom is RUBL and Sensu NUBL, while Baile and Pa'u are ZUBL, with Pom-Pom and Sensu again benefiting most from their typings. Dancer is situational in singles but can immediately copy another Pokémon's dance move, making it far more tactically interesting in doubles or against opposing setup; Terastallization adds another unusual interaction because Revelation Dance follows Oricorio's current primary type after Terastallizing.
nuzlocke: Oricorio's greatest Nuzlocke strength is flexibility: when the necessary Nectar is available, the same surviving individual can change typing before a dangerous boss instead of requiring the player to catch and train a replacement. Pom-Pom is usually the lowest-risk default because it has only two weaknesses and a Ground immunity, while Sensu can create completely free switches into Normal-, Fighting-, and Ground-type attacks if the opponent's coverage is known. Baile should be handled more cautiously around Rock coverage because Fire/Flying takes 4× damage from Rock, and Pa'u has five common weaknesses despite useful Fighting and Ground matchups. Base 75/70/70 bulk is serviceable rather than sturdy, so Oricorio should not be asked to absorb strong neutral physical hits merely because it has Roost. In Generation IX, Quiver Dance can turn a favorable matchup into a sweep while also raising Special Defense, but repeated setup still exposes Oricorio to critical hits and unexpected physical coverage; one safe boost is usually preferable to greedily maximizing stats. Revelation Dance's perfect accuracy and automatic form-matched typing are valuable for reducing move-selection and accuracy variance, while Timid can preserve more natural outspeeds before any setup has occurred.

pokemon.name: Oricorio
pokemon.biologyAndBehavior: Baile Style Oricorio inhabits Ula'ula Island in Alola and eastern Paldea and develops red plumage after drinking Red Nectar. It is notably passionate and forceful while dancing and can become fiercely angry when given the wrong orders. Its intense movements scatter downy fluff from its body; Oricorio can ignite that loose fluff and incorporate the resulting flames into its dance attacks. In Paldea, its passionate style of dancing has become especially popular because it is said to suit the temperament of the region's people.

pokemon.name: Oricorio
pokemon.biologyAndBehavior: Pom-Pom Style Oricorio is associated with Melemele Island in Alola and southern Paldea and takes on its yellow coloration after drinking Yellow Nectar.
