Sucker Punch supplies a second form of priority, U-turn lets Lokix attack while resetting First Impression for a later entry, and Leech Life offers accurate STAB with healing; Axe Kick provides extremely strong Fighting coverage but carries severe crash damage if it misses. Tinted Lens is the Hidden Ability and is transformative because resisted attacks deal double their normal resisted damage, but a standard story Lokix normally has Swarm unless the player obtains its Hidden Ability through special means, so its famous competitive damage profile should not automatically be assumed for a casual run. Adamant is excellent when leaning on priority, while Jolly is valuable if the player wants Lokix's natural Speed to cover more matchups without relying on First Impression or Sucker Punch.
competitive: Lokix is one of Generation IX's most successful low-BST specialists, and Smogon's current Scarlet/Violet Pokédex places it in UU while still documenting a genuine Choice Band niche in OU. Tinted Lens is the key: because resisted attacks have their damage penalty effectively cancelled, Choice Band-boosted First Impression can revenge kill targets that would normally shrug off Bug attacks, while STAB Knock Off and U-turn make progress even when an immediate knockout is unavailable. Heavy-Duty Boots sets trade some raw power for longevity and repeatedly cycle First Impression, U-turn, Knock Off, and Sucker Punch, whereas Choice Band maximizes the amount of damage each forced entry can generate. Its early Generation IX history was unusually strong for an early-route Bug line—Lokix even reached OU usage near the beginning of the metagame—before the format stabilized and it ultimately settled into lower usage while retaining a respected niche above its numerical stats. Tera Bug can push First Impression to extreme damage thresholds, and Tera also pairs naturally with Tinted Lens because defensive attempts to resist Lokix's Bug STAB are less effective than they would be against ordinary attackers. The limitations are substantial enough to keep it balanced: First Impression works only on the first turn after entering, Sucker Punch is prediction-dependent, a Rock weakness makes hazard control important on non-Boots sets, and 71/78/55 bulk gives it few comfortable defensive entries. Adamant is the most common way to maximize its priority damage, while Jolly remains viable when extra natural Speed is important.
nuzlocke: Lokix can be excellent in a Nuzlocke because it combines early availability with tools that reduce the number of turns it must remain exposed to enemy attacks. First Impression gives it a powerful priority strike immediately after switching in, Sucker Punch can finish faster attackers, and U-turn allows it to deal damage while moving directly into a safer teammate; together these moves reward controlled positioning rather than risky prolonged exchanges. Its Psychic immunity can provide completely free switches against known Psychic moves, and resistances to Ground, Grass, Ghost, and Dark create additional safe entry points, but weaknesses to Fire, Flying, Rock, Fairy, and Bug still demand careful matchup knowledge. Leech Life is especially useful in permadeath play because it is accurate and converts damage into recovery, helping offset chip without consuming a turn on a separate healing move. Axe Kick is a much more dangerous choice under Nuzlocke rules: its high power is tempting, but a miss inflicts crash damage equal to half of Lokix's maximum HP, which can turn a routine coverage attempt into an avoidable death. Tinted Lens is outstanding if legitimately available because it makes supposedly safe resistances far less able to stall Lokix, but even with ordinary Swarm the line remains useful through priority and pivoting. Its defensive stats are not strong enough for reckless switching, so Lokix is best treated as a fast tactical attacker and revenge killer rather than as a general-purpose tank.

pokemon.name: Nymble
pokemon.biologyAndBehavior: Nymble is a small gray grasshopper-like Pokémon with six legs, including an enlarged third pair that it normally keeps folded above its body. When threatened, it can unfold those powerful legs and jump more than 30 feet into the air. Its jumping ability is used defensively to evade attacks as well as offensively to strike back while moving. The species' compact body and stored jumping power foreshadow the specialized folding leg system that becomes even more pronounced after evolution.

pokemon.name: Lokix
pokemon.biologyAndBehavior: Lokix is a bipedal locust-like Pokémon whose enlarged third pair of legs normally remains folded along its back. When it chooses to fight at full power, it unfolds those legs and enters what is explicitly called Showdown Mode, standing and jumping on the extended limbs and swinging them as weapons. Showdown Mode lets Lokix subdue opponents quickly, but the posture places such a heavy strain on its body that it cannot maintain the state for long. Lokix is ecologically flexible and is documented across many Paldean environments, including grasslands, deserts, snowy mountains, and lake regions. Its transformation into Showdown Mode is therefore a temporary high-output combat behavior rather than a separate permanent form.

playthrough: Pawmi can be encountered very early in Scarlet and Violet and evolves into Pawmo at level 18, but reaching Pawmot requires one of Paldea's unusual overworld evolution methods: Pawmo must walk 1,000 steps outside its Poké Ball using the Let's Go! feature and then level up while outside the ball. The extra procedure is easy once understood but is substantially less automatic than a normal level evolution, so players can accidentally carry Pawmo for much longer than intended if they never use Let's Go! enough. Pawmot is an excellent physical attacker for ordinary play, combining base 115 Attack with base 105 Speed and Electric/Fighting STAB that pressures Water-, Flying-, Normal-, Rock-, Ice-, Dark-, and Steel-type opponents. Double Shock is its signature physical Electric attack at 120 base power, but after using it Pawmot loses its Electric typing until it leaves the field, so outside of Electric Terastallization it normally cannot use Double Shock repeatedly without switching; Close Combat supplies equally powerful Fighting STAB at the cost of lowering both defenses. Mach Punch provides priority, while Ice Punch, Knock Off, Volt Switch, Nuzzle, and other utility give it ways to cover Ground-types, pivot, or control Speed; Iron Fist strengthens punching moves, whereas Volt Absorb provides an Electric immunity and Natural Cure clears major status when Pawmot switches out. Jolly is usually the most broadly useful Nature because it preserves the value of base 105 Speed, although Adamant can be worthwhile when the player prefers maximum physical damage and is comfortable relying on priority or favorable matchups.
competitive: Pawmot's competitive identity has always been split between unusual utility and genuinely strong physical offense, and Smogon's current Scarlet/Violet Pokédex places it in PU while also maintaining NU and other format analyses. Base 115 Attack and 105 Speed let it function as a real wallbreaker or revenge killer, with Double Shock and Close Combat forming a 120-power dual-STAB core and Ice Punch or Knock Off addressing common switch-ins; Mach Punch adds priority and Volt Switch can preserve momentum. Its three abilities all support distinct roles: Iron Fist improves Mach Punch and Ice Punch, Natural Cure pairs with Rest or lets Pawmot absorb status more freely, and Volt Absorb creates a complete Electric immunity. Revival Blessing gave Pawmot one of the most novel support roles introduced in Generation IX by restoring a fainted teammate to half health, and early Battle Stadium analyses treated that move as a meaningful way to reverse games even when Pawmot was not the strongest attacker on the field. In standard current lower-tier singles, however, offensive sets often emphasize Double Shock, Close Combat, Knock Off or Ice Punch, and Mach Punch rather than relying exclusively on revival support, reflecting the fact that Pawmot's raw offensive profile is independently useful. Electric Terastallization has a special mechanical synergy with Double Shock because the fixed Tera Electric typing prevents Pawmot from losing access to its Electric type after the move, allowing repeated use of what would otherwise function as a once-per-entry STAB. Pawmot's ceiling is limited by mediocre 70/70/60 defenses and competition from sturdier or more immediately powerful Fighting- and Electric-types, so Jolly offense tends to succeed when it enters safely rather than when it is asked to absorb repeated neutral hits.
nuzlocke: Pawmi's early availability and Pawmo's level-18 evolution make the first part of the family easy to use in a Nuzlocke, but Pawmot's 1,000-step Let's Go! requirement creates a unique planning task that must be completed deliberately rather than through ordinary leveling alone. Once evolved, Pawmot's base 105 Speed and 115 Attack are excellent survival tools because they let it remove many threats before taking damage, while Mach Punch gives emergency priority and Nuzzle can provide reliable Speed control through paralysis. Volt Absorb is particularly valuable under permadeath rules because a known Electric attack becomes a free switch that also restores HP, while Natural Cure lets Pawmot escape poison, burn, paralysis, or sleep simply by switching; Iron Fist instead prioritizes damage. Double Shock is powerful and accurate but changes Pawmot's defensive profile by removing its Electric type after use until it switches, so the player should account for the resulting pure Fighting typing rather than treating the move as consequence-free. Close Combat is similarly dangerous when a battle will continue after the target survives or another opponent immediately enters, because both Defense and Special Defense fall after every use. Revival Blessing is extraordinary in ordinary Pokémon rules, but traditional Nuzlocke rules treat a fainted Pokémon as permanently dead, so using the move to restore a fallen teammate normally violates the defining restriction and should not be counted as a legitimate safety net. Pawmot is therefore a very strong but relatively fragile Nuzlocke attacker: it survives best by moving first, exploiting immunities and priority, and switching intelligently instead of attempting to tank neutral attacks with only 70/70/60 defenses.

pokemon.name: Pawmi
pokemon.biologyAndBehavior: Pawmi is a small orange rodent-like Pokémon with underdeveloped electric sacs in its cheeks and specialized pads on its forepaws that can discharge electricity. When threatened, it rubs its cheeks to generate a charge and then transfers that electricity by touching an opponent with its forepaws; the paw organs visibly change color while discharging. Its thick fur both insulates it from cold and helps store electrical energy. Pokémon Sleep observations add that Pawmi sometimes rubs its cheeks with its paws and releases electricity while asleep, behavior interpreted as possible practice in generating a charge.

pokemon.name: Pawmo
pokemon.biologyAndBehavior: Pawmo is a bipedal rodent-like Pokémon whose forepaws contain electrical pads that light up when releasing electricity. Its characteristic fighting method combines physical strikes and electrical discharge, hitting an opponent with its paws while shocking it at the same time. Pawmo live and travel in groups, and when a group is attacked Pawmo is described as being the first to fight back, using electricity to defeat the threat. Pokémon Sleep material notes that it can retain its characteristic battle stance while asleep, possibly because it is dreaming about practicing its fighting techniques. The species' active group defense and constant training make Pawmo behaviorally more combative than the small, cautious Pawmi stage.

pokemon.name: Pawmot
pokemon.biologyAndBehavior: Pawmot is a bipedal rodent-like Pokémon whose shaggy fur functions as a biological battery, storing an amount of electricity compared in the Pokédex to that of an electric car. Although its ordinary reaction speed is described as slow, it can shift into lightning-fast movement once a battle begins. Its large forepaws retain electrical pads used for discharge, and the species can sometimes direct that electricity toward injured Pokémon to heal them rather than attack. Pokémon Sleep research characterizes Pawmot as peaceful and suggests that individuals sleeping with raised paws may be dreaming of tending to other Pokémon. Pawmot is also the only known Pokémon able to learn Double Shock, linking its unusually large electrical reserves directly to a species-exclusive combat technique.

playthrough: Tandemaus is obtainable in several Paldean areas before the middle of the story, and it evolves into Maushold when it gains a level in a battle at level 25 or higher; the unusual point is that the evolution may occur without the usual post-battle evolution animation, and the resulting form is normally Family of Four, with Family of Three occurring only rarely. Maushold is a fast pure Normal-type whose base 111 Speed lets it act before much of a normal playthrough, while its otherwise modest offenses make its signature tools more important than raw stats. Tidy Up, available immediately by relearning after evolution, simultaneously raises Attack and Speed while clearing entry hazards and substitutes, giving Maushold unusually efficient setup even in ordinary battles. Population Bomb becomes its defining attack later: it can hit up to ten times, and Wide Lens greatly improves the chance of completing a long sequence of hits; Technician, however, is Maushold's Hidden Ability, so a standard story capture will not automatically have the strongest offensive version of the strategy. Friend Guard is much more valuable in doubles, while Cheek Pouch can give a story Maushold useful Berry-based recovery. Jolly is the clearest offensive Nature because Maushold wants to preserve its excellent Speed, while Adamant can be useful when extra immediate damage matters more than winning the fastest speed checks.
competitive: Maushold has had a real but specialized Generation IX competitive career, and Smogon currently places it in SV RU rather than treating it as merely a low-tier novelty. Its defining singles set combines Technician with Population Bomb and Tidy Up: one turn of Tidy Up raises both Attack and Speed, while Technician turns each weak Population Bomb hit into a much more dangerous component of a multi-hit attack that also breaks Focus Sash, Substitute, and similar protections. Wide Lens is strongly associated with this strategy because Population Bomb performs a separate accuracy check for each attempted hit, making reliability a major part of the set's damage ceiling. The same contact-heavy design creates pronounced counterplay, since Rocky Helmet, Rough Skin, Flame Body, and other contact punishment can make repeated hits costly or outright disastrous, while Maushold's 74/70/75 bulk leaves it vulnerable to strong priority and revenge killing if it has not secured enough momentum. Terastallization can either amplify Population Bomb with Tera Normal or defensively escape Fighting-type and priority interactions with types such as Ghost, but using the team's Tera on Maushold is a meaningful opportunity cost. In doubles and VGC, Maushold often takes a very different role: Friend Guard and Follow Me make it a redirection and damage-reduction support Pokémon, with Super Fang, Taunt, Beat Up, and Protect providing utility rather than relying on a Population Bomb sweep. That split between singles sweeper and doubles supporter is central to its competitive identity and explains why its modest base Attack has not prevented it from finding legitimate niches.
nuzlocke: Maushold is useful in a Nuzlocke because its high Speed and simple Normal typing give it a clear job without burdening the team with many weaknesses, but its mediocre defenses mean it should usually win through positioning rather than absorbing repeated neutral hits. The level-25 evolution is reasonably early and does not require an item, friendship threshold, or multiplayer feature, although the Pokémon must gain the relevant level in battle rather than relying exclusively on passive leveling methods. Tidy Up can turn favorable encounters into sweeps while also removing hazards, but setup should still be reserved for opponents that cannot punish the free turn. Population Bomb is powerful yet more volatile than its headline power suggests: every hit can expose Maushold to contact effects such as Rough Skin, Rocky Helmet, or Flame Body, and without Wide Lens the repeated accuracy checks add additional failure risk. For a permadeath run, a safer single-hit move can therefore be preferable against contact-punishing targets even when Population Bomb would deal more theoretical damage. Cheek Pouch can add practical sustain with Berries, and the Ghost immunity provides safe switches into predicted Ghost attacks, while the lone Fighting weakness is easy to understand and plan around. Overall, Maushold is a strong offensive and utility option when encounters are known, but it has less margin for error than genuinely bulky setup sweepers.

pokemon.name: Tandemaus
pokemon.biologyAndBehavior: Tandemaus consists of two separate small, white, mouse-like individuals that function together as a single Pokémon; one has a gray patch resembling a shirt and the other a patch resembling pants, and both have very large mouths containing a single prominent upper incisor. The pair remains together constantly and displays unusually coordinated behavior, dividing any food it finds equally between the two. They also build their nest cooperatively, cutting and gathering useful material with their incisors. How Tandemaus becomes Maushold remains unexplained in-universe, because the smaller individuals present after evolution seem to appear from nowhere.

pokemon.name: Maushold
pokemon.biologyAndBehavior: Family of Four Maushold consists of the two larger Tandemaus-like individuals accompanied by two smaller ones with shorter tails, stubbier limbs, and no gray clothing-like patches. The smaller individuals commonly stay behind the larger pair and hold the tips of their tails while walking; despite the family-like behavior of the group, their actual biological relationship is explicitly unknown. The larger pair protects the smaller members in battle, although all four will cooperate when facing a sufficiently strong opponent. Maushold builds exceptionally large nests divided into specialized rooms for functions such as eating and sleeping. This is the overwhelmingly common evolutionary form, appearing from Tandemaus about 99 percent of the time.

pokemon.name: Maushold
pokemon.biologyAndBehavior: Family of Three Maushold consists of the original-looking larger pair and a single smaller individual, whose limbs and tail are shorter and which lacks the gray patches seen on the adults-sized members. The small individual tends to shelter behind the larger two and can hold their tail tips while the group moves. As with Family of Four, the group behaves as a family even though the actual relationship between its members and the unexplained origin of the smaller individual remain mysteries. The larger members defend the smaller one, with the entire group joining together against powerful opponents, and they inhabit elaborate multi-room nests. The Family of Three form is exceptionally rare from normal evolution, occurring only about one time in one hundred.

playthrough: Fidough is available very early in Scarlet and Violet and evolves into Dachsbun at level 26, so the line can contribute for most of the game without requiring a special evolution method. Dachsbun's pure Fairy typing supplies a Dragon immunity and useful resistances to Fighting, Dark, and Bug while leaving only Poison and Steel as weaknesses, and its 115 Defense and 95 Speed make it unusually good at taking physical hits without being painfully slow. Well-Baked Body is the standout Ability: Fire-type attacks do no damage and instead raise Dachsbun's Defense by two stages, turning a normally neutral attack type into both an immunity and a potential setup opportunity. Its base 80 Attack is merely adequate, so it relies more on dependable Fairy STAB such as Play Rough, utility, and moves such as Body Press that can exploit its high Defense than on overwhelming raw damage. The low base 57 HP and only average special bulk keep it from functioning as a universal wall, especially against strong special attackers. Aroma Veil is useful against certain disruptive effects but is generally less transformative in a normal story than Well-Baked Body. Impish suits a physically defensive or Body Press-oriented role, while Jolly or Adamant can be reasonable when using Dachsbun primarily as a conventional physical attacker.
competitive: Dachsbun currently sits in SV ZU on Smogon, reflecting that its attractive defensive profile has not translated into broad high-tier viability. Its main competitive selling point is Well-Baked Body, which combines a Fire immunity with a two-stage Defense boost, while Fairy typing independently grants a Dragon immunity and several useful resistances. With base 115 Defense and 95 Speed, Dachsbun can function as a relatively fast physical wall, use Body Press to turn Defense into pressure, and employ support options such as Wish, Roar, Yawn, or other disruption depending on the format. That package can make it a useful answer to very specific physical attackers and Fire-dependent threats, and it has enough utility to appear as a niche defensive selection in draft formats. Its limitations are equally clear: base 57 HP reduces its effective bulk and the size of Wishes it passes, base 80 Attack provides limited direct pressure, and its special durability is far less imposing than its Defense statistic suggests. It therefore succeeds by exploiting favorable immunities and matchups rather than by walling an entire metagame. Impish is the most natural Nature for Body Press and physical-wall sets, with Careful sometimes useful when a team needs additional special resilience.
nuzlocke: Dachsbun is a strong Nuzlocke Pokémon because it is obtainable early, evolves at a straightforward level 26, and gains a defensive profile that creates numerous safe-switch opportunities. Pure Fairy leaves only Poison and Steel weaknesses, while Well-Baked Body adds a complete Fire immunity and can sharply increase Defense if an opponent uses a Fire move, making predicted switches especially rewarding. Its base 115 Defense is excellent for surviving physical attacks, but the line's low HP means that players should not treat it as equally safe against strong special moves or repeated neutral damage. Play Rough supplies important STAB but its imperfect accuracy adds some risk in situations where a miss could be fatal; Body Press is perfectly accurate and can exploit Dachsbun's strongest stat, though it lacks STAB. The Dragon immunity can completely blank certain attacks and is particularly valuable in known boss battles, while Fighting and Dark resistances create additional pivot opportunities. Avoid overestimating a Well-Baked Body Defense boost against mixed attackers: it does nothing to strengthen Special Defense. Used as a matchup-based physical wall rather than a catch-all tank, Dachsbun offers very good survival value for a permadeath run.

pokemon.name: Fidough
pokemon.biologyAndBehavior: Fidough is a small canine Pokémon with pastry-like ears, a large dewlap on which it can rest its head while sleeping, braided-looking protrusions along its back, and a segmented tail. Its skin is smooth and moist yet firm, soft, and elastic, and when agitated it puffs itself up in an attempt to appear larger. Fidough cultivates yeast inside its body and exhales it in its breath, causing fermentation nearby. Humans have protected and lived alongside the species since ancient times because this yeast is useful in cooking and has helped enrich human diets.

pokemon.name: Dachsbun
pokemon.biologyAndBehavior: Dachsbun is a stout, elongated canine whose brown body, bread-roll-like ears and neck folds, braided back, and flattened circular tail resemble baked breads and pastries. Its body gives off a pleasant, appetizing aroma that is said to help wheat grow, causing farming villages to treasure Dachsbun historically. Exposure to intense heat hardens the surface of its skin, a biological trait represented in battle by Well-Baked Body. More recent Legends: Z-A Pokédex information adds that Dachsbun's scent can drive an opponent's hunger into overdrive until its willpower and stamina are worn down.

playthrough: Smoliv can be caught very early in Scarlet and Violet, evolves into Dolliv at level 25, and reaches Arboliva at level 35, giving the line a convenient progression through the main story. Arboliva becomes a slow but genuinely powerful special attacker with base 125 Special Attack, 109 Special Defense, and respectable physical bulk, while its base 39 Speed means it should usually expect to take a hit before acting. Grass/Normal provides a useful Ghost immunity and resistances to Water, Electric, Grass, and Ground, but it also carries six weaknesses—Fire, Ice, Fighting, Poison, Flying, and Bug—so the typing demands more matchup awareness than its bulk initially suggests. Seed Sower automatically creates Grassy Terrain when Arboliva is hit, boosting grounded Grass attacks and providing passive recovery, which can combine naturally with Giga Drain or other sustaining tools during longer fights. Its Hidden Ability Harvest instead supports Berry-based longevity, particularly in sun, but Seed Sower is usually more immediately useful without specialized planning. Arboliva has strong special options such as Leaf Storm, Giga Drain, Hyper Voice, Earth Power, and Terrain Pulse, letting it choose between immediate power, recovery, and coverage rather than relying on one attack. Modest is an excellent general Nature for maximizing its special damage, while Quiet can suit very slow or Trick Room-oriented teams and Calm is appropriate when emphasizing special bulk and sustain.
competitive: Arboliva is currently an SV ZU Pokémon, but within that environment it has a meaningful identity as a bulky special attacker rather than merely a low-stat Grass type. Its base 125 Special Attack gives Choice Specs sets substantial immediate power, with Grass STAB such as Leaf Storm or Giga Drain complemented by Hyper Voice and coverage such as Earth Power; Smogon's current ZU material also emphasizes its ability to pressure many neutral switch-ins despite the tier placement. Seed Sower improves longevity by establishing Grassy Terrain after Arboliva is struck, and defensive variants can stack that recovery with Leftovers, Leech Seed, Giga Drain, or other healing tools. Harvest offers an alternate Berry-centered route and becomes perfectly reliable at restoring a consumed Berry under sun, but it is more team- and set-dependent than Seed Sower. Arboliva's excellent Special Attack and Special Defense are held back by base 39 Speed and a Grass/Normal typing with six weaknesses, making it vulnerable to being forced out or overwhelmed before it can exploit its staying power. Terastallization can repair that defensive typing or strengthen a chosen offensive role, but the need to spend Tera illustrates one of the costs of making Arboliva function against stronger threats. Modest is the most natural Nature for offensive sets, while Calm and occasionally Quiet support bulkier or speed-indifferent approaches.
nuzlocke: The Smoliv line is attractive in a Nuzlocke because it is available near the beginning of Paldea and reaches its final evolution at level 35 without an item, friendship requirement, or other risky evolution condition. Arboliva's 78/90/109 bulk and strong special offense allow it to win many neutral matchups, while its Ghost immunity and four resistances can create valuable planned switches. The chief danger is its extremely low Speed combined with six weaknesses: even a healthy Arboliva often has to absorb a hit before responding, so blind use against opponents with broad coverage can be hazardous. Seed Sower helps compensate by creating Grassy Terrain whenever an attack connects, adding passive recovery and powering Grass moves, while Giga Drain offers direct and perfectly accurate healing through offense. Leaf Storm delivers much higher immediate power but sharply lowers Special Attack afterward, potentially forcing a switch at an awkward moment, and Leech Seed introduces accuracy variance if used as the foundation of a defensive plan. Because Grassy Terrain affects the field rather than only Arboliva, players should also remember that opposing grounded Pokémon receive its recovery benefits and can exploit boosted Grass moves. Used against known Water-, Ground-, Electric-, or Ghost-oriented targets rather than thrown into unknown coverage, Arboliva can be a durable and high-value team member.

pokemon.name: Smoliv
pokemon.biologyAndBehavior: Smoliv is a small olive-like Pokémon that stores oil inside the fruit on top of its head, producing that oil from nutrients gathered through photosynthesis. Its stored reserves are sufficient for it to go about a week without eating or drinking. The oil is extremely bitter and astringent rather than edible; when startled or attacked, Smoliv sprays it to slow the threat and then flees. It favors dry, sunny climates and spends much of its time sunbathing.

pokemon.name: Dolliv
pokemon.biologyAndBehavior: Dolliv is a plant-like Pokémon with leaf-shaped arms and two olive fruits growing from its head. Unlike Smoliv's defensive bitter oil, Dolliv shares tasty, fresh-scented oil with others and has lived alongside humans in settlements since ancient times. It spends long periods basking in sunlight until the fruits on its head have ripened, after which it leaves the settlement and sets out on a journey. Observed sleeping Dolliv sit with their legs angled to one side, their dress-like lower bodies spread outward, arms resting by their sides, and heads tilted down.

pokemon.name: Arboliva
pokemon.biologyAndBehavior: Arboliva resembles a small olive tree, with a woody lower body, leafy upper growth, and two large branches bearing six purplish olive fruits in total. It is described as calm and compassionate and shares its fragrant, nutrient-rich oil with weakened Pokémon. That gentleness does not leave it defenseless: when threatened, Arboliva can launch its oil with enough force to smash a boulder. When sleeping, it remains upright but lowers its branch-like arms and head as its body relaxes.

playthrough: Squawkabilly does not evolve, so a captured individual immediately provides its full base 417 stat total instead of asking the player to carry a weaker early stage, and Green Plumage Squawkabilly can be found extremely early around Cabo Poco while the other colors appear elsewhere in Paldea. Its Normal/Flying typing supplies valuable Ground and Ghost immunities plus Bug and Grass resistances, though Electric, Ice, and Rock weaknesses punish careless switching. Base 96 Attack and 92 Speed are adequate for the story, and physical Flying and Normal moves, priority, and pivoting options such as U-turn or Parting Shot give it useful flexibility. Intimidate is generally the safest playthrough Ability because lowering an opponent's Attack improves both Squawkabilly's and the team's survival, whereas Hustle increases physical power at the cost of accuracy and is much less reliable. The forms differ mechanically only in Hidden Ability: Green and Blue Plumage receive Guts, while Yellow and White Plumage receive Sheer Force; all four otherwise share the same stats and standard Ability choices. Recoil attacks such as Brave Bird and Double-Edge can provide needed power but should be weighed against their durability cost during long routes or difficult boss sequences. Jolly emphasizes Squawkabilly's useful Speed tier, while Adamant is reasonable when the team values stronger immediate damage.
competitive: Squawkabilly currently resides in SV ZU, and its competitive record is best described as a collection of narrow offensive and pivoting niches rather than sustained high-tier success. Green and Blue Plumage have the most distinctive offensive option through their Hidden Ability Guts, which can amplify Facade while Brave Bird supplies powerful Flying STAB; U-turn or Parting Shot can instead capitalize on forced switches and keep momentum. Intimidate offers a more supportive identity and can soften physical attackers before Squawkabilly pivots out, while Hustle supplies a large Attack boost but makes already-fragile games significantly less reliable because physical moves lose accuracy. Yellow and White Plumage replace Guts with Sheer Force as their Hidden Ability, but the species' movepool and middling base 96 Attack give them fewer compelling ways to exploit that distinction. The major problem across all forms is defensive: 51 Defense and 51 Special Defense make Squawkabilly easy to revenge kill, and its Rock weakness means Stealth Rock further reduces the number of times it can pivot. Base 92 Speed is useful but no longer exceptional in a fast metagame, while recoil from Brave Bird or Double-Edge can accelerate its own defeat. Its low-tier placement therefore reflects genuine limitations, even though Guts wallbreaking, Intimidate utility, priority, and pivoting prevent it from being completely without purpose.
nuzlocke: Squawkabilly can be a useful early Nuzlocke capture because it requires no evolution investment and immediately offers two immunities, respectable Speed, and access to Intimidate. Intimidate is by far the most safety-oriented Ability, reducing physical damage on entry and sometimes enabling safer switches for the rest of the party even when Squawkabilly itself does not stay in. Its Ground and Ghost immunities are excellent for planned pivots, but base 51 defenses on both sides mean a mistaken prediction or strong neutral attack can still be fatal. Hustle is especially dangerous under permadeath rules because the 50 percent Attack boost comes with a substantial physical-accuracy penalty, turning otherwise routine knockouts into possible missed turns. Likewise, Brave Bird and Double-Edge should be treated as situational finishing tools rather than default buttons when their recoil could put Squawkabilly into range of priority or an unexpected second opponent. U-turn and Parting Shot are valuable because they control positioning without requiring Squawkabilly to remain exposed, while Quick Attack can finish weakened targets before they retaliate. An Intimidate Squawkabilly used as a fast pivot is therefore much safer than trying to force it into the role of a durable sweeper.

pokemon.name: Squawkabilly
pokemon.biologyAndBehavior: Green Plumage Squawkabilly is a parrot-like, zygodactyl-footed bird with a prominent black pompadour-like crest, and it belongs to a species noted for noisy territorial behavior, strong group loyalty, and a dislike of solitude. Green is the most common plumage because its coloration is the most likely to be inherited, and green birds consequently form the largest and most powerful flocks. Those flocks can contain more than fifty individuals, forage noisily through towns, cities, forests, and other areas in the morning and evening, and are treated as rivals by Blue Plumage groups. Squawkabilly favor urban habitats, serve as the Flying Taxi Pokémon of Paldea, and some individuals have demonstrated the ability to mimic human speech.

pokemon.name: Squawkabilly
pokemon.biologyAndBehavior: Blue Plumage Squawkabilly shares the species' parrot-like body, black pompadour-shaped crest, zygodactyl feet, territorial nature, and tendency to form color-based flocks. It is the second most populous variety after Green Plumage and explicitly regards the more numerous green groups as rivals or foes. Large blue flocks can number more than fifty individuals and move noisily through forests and human settlements while searching for food, with cities being a favored habitat for the species. Squawkabilly have historically fought violent territorial disputes with Fletchling, and the species is sufficiently integrated into Paldean life to power the region's Flying Taxi service.

pokemon.name: Squawkabilly
pokemon.biologyAndBehavior: Yellow Plumage Squawkabilly is the particularly aggressive variety of an already territorial parrot-like species whose members organize themselves into plumage-based flocks. Yellow individuals are described as hotheaded and especially fierce, willingly leaping into close combat and even driving other bird Pokémon out of towns. Legends: Z-A adds that their aggression increased as a way of forcing the more populous Squawkabilly varieties to take them seriously. Like the species generally, they are social rather than solitary birds, forage in and around settlements as well as forests, and are adapted to living closely around people.

pokemon.name: Squawkabilly
pokemon.biologyAndBehavior: White Plumage Squawkabilly is the least populous of the four varieties and is temperamentally distinct from the more aggressive groups, preferring to avoid conflict when possible. It still fights with determination when forced to defend itself or its group, and the species' strong communal instinct means these birds dislike being alone and survive through cooperation. Their off-white feathers provide useful camouflage against pale urban buildings, helping the rare variety live successfully in towns despite its small numbers. They otherwise share Squawkabilly's parrot-like anatomy, pompadour-shaped crest, city-favoring habits, and broader capacity for flocking and close association with human settlements.

playthrough: Nacli is widespread across Paldea, evolves into Naclstack at level 24, and reaches Garganacl at level 38, making the entire line straightforward to obtain and fully evolve during a normal Scarlet or Violet story. Garganacl combines base 100 HP, 130 Defense, and 90 Special Defense with a respectable base 100 Attack, but its base 35 Speed means it is built to absorb attacks rather than move first. Purifying Salt is the defining Ability, preventing nonvolatile status and effectively halving damage from Ghost-type attacks; Sturdy is an excellent alternate story Ability that can guarantee survival from full HP, while Clear Body is the Hidden Ability and prevents opponents from lowering its stats. Salt Cure is extraordinarily useful as soon as Naclstack learns it: in Scarlet and Violet it is a perfectly accurate 40-power Rock attack that continues removing one eighth of the target's maximum HP each turn, doubled to one quarter against Water- and Steel-types, and Garganacl can pair it with Recover for extremely durable progress. Rock typing still gives Garganacl five common weaknesses—Water, Grass, Fighting, Ground, and Steel—so its numerical bulk should not be mistaken for universal safety, particularly against special Water and Grass attacks. Body Press works well with its enormous Defense, while Earthquake, Rock STAB, Curse, Iron Defense, and Stealth Rock support either offensive or defensive approaches; Terastallization is especially useful for escaping Rock's weak defensive profile. Careful is excellent for balancing Garganacl's already huge physical Defense with greater special resilience, while Impish strengthens physical-wall and Body Press-oriented roles.
competitive: Garganacl is the clear competitive standout of this batch and is currently an SV OU Pokémon on Smogon, a status rooted in an unusually effective combination of bulk, recovery, ability utility, and unavoidable residual pressure. Purifying Salt denies ordinary status-based wear while reducing Ghost damage, and Salt Cure allows Garganacl to make progress even when its direct attacks are weak; in Scarlet and Violet the residual damage is one eighth of maximum HP per turn and one quarter against Water- and Steel-types. Stealth Rock, Recover, Protect, Curse, Iron Defense, Body Press, and Earthquake have all supported different variants, allowing Garganacl to serve as a wall, hazard setter, attrition engine, or late-game win condition rather than occupying only one defensive slot. Terastallization has been fundamental to that success because types such as Water or Fairy can replace Rock's five weaknesses with a much safer defensive profile while Garganacl retains Purifying Salt and Salt Cure. Counterplay exists through overwhelming wallbreakers, Taunt, favorable Terastallization, and tools such as Covert Cloak that can negate Salt Cure's secondary effect, so its reputation does not make it invulnerable. Its competitive history is also a good example of why generation-specific mechanics must be separated: newer Pokémon Champions data uses a weakened Salt Cure residual effect compared with Scarlet and Violet, so the established SV OU pressure should not simply be copied unchanged into that ruleset. Careful is the most common defensive Nature for balancing its special side, while Impish is appropriate for dedicated physical or Body Press sets.
nuzlocke: The Nacli line is one of Paldea's strongest Nuzlocke defensive investments because the encounter is broadly available, both evolutions occur at ordinary levels, and Naclstack already gains several of the tools that define Garganacl. Purifying Salt eliminates one of permadeath play's largest sources of variance by preventing ordinary status conditions, while Sturdy can provide emergency one-hit insurance when the Pokémon begins at full HP; a specific individual has only one Ability at a time, so these benefits should not be conflated. Salt Cure is especially safe for a long battle because it is perfectly accurate, has no recoil, and keeps damaging a target after the initial hit, while Recover gives Garganacl reliable in-battle healing and allows it to exploit that residual damage. Its immense physical Defense and solid special bulk create a large margin for error, and Body Press can convert that Defense into dependable offense without asking Garganacl to sacrifice durability. The principal danger is Rock typing: Water, Grass, Fighting, Ground, and Steel attacks are all super effective, and base 35 Speed means Garganacl will usually have to survive those attacks rather than outrun their users. Players should therefore resist the temptation to leave it in simply because its HP bar looks sturdy, especially against special Water- or Grass-type coverage, and should favor reliable moves over lower-accuracy Rock options when a miss would risk a death. With those matchup checks respected, Garganacl's status protection, recovery, residual damage, and sheer bulk make it one of the safest long-term members available in a Scarlet or Violet Nuzlocke.

pokemon.name: Nacli
pokemon.biologyAndBehavior: Nacli is a Rock-type Pokémon whose body is composed in part of rock salt and which is born in subterranean salt layers. As it travels, the ground scrapes salt from its body, but the lost salt is continuously produced and replenished internally; the trails it leaves have been called 'salt roads' since ancient times. People historically treasured Nacli because it shared a substance that was once a particularly valuable resource, establishing a long relationship between the species and humans. Its entire evolutionary family is uniquely capable of possessing Purifying Salt, linking the line's mineral physiology directly to its battle properties.

pokemon.name: Naclstack
pokemon.biologyAndBehavior: Naclstack is a quadrupedal mass of block-like rock salt whose legs appear physically disconnected from its body while remaining fixed beneath it. It compresses salt inside its body into hard pellets and launches them with enough force to punch through an iron sheet. The species also sprays salt over prey to draw out moisture and dry-cure it, although Naclstack is notably forgetful and may lose track of the prey afterward; the same absent-mindedness can make it forget a Trainer's commands. Bits of salt remain in its footprints, and people collect these grains for use as sandwich seasoning.

pokemon.name: Garganacl
pokemon.biologyAndBehavior: Garganacl is a massive blocky Rock Pokémon covered with patches of mineral-rich salt whose composition has restorative and medicinal properties. By scraping its fingertips together, it can sprinkle salt over injured Pokémon and rapidly heal even serious wounds. Other Pokémon consequently gather around Garganacl in hopes of licking the salt from its body, giving the species a direct ecological relationship with the animals around it rather than depicting the salt as merely decorative armor. The line's exclusive Purifying Salt Ability reflects the same cleansing mineral theme, while Garganacl and Naclstack are the only known Pokémon capable of learning Salt Cure.

playthrough: Charcadet is obtainable across many parts of Paldea and can become either Armarouge or Ceruledge without a level requirement, but the branch is tied to special armor: Auspicious Armor evolves it into Armarouge and Malicious Armor evolves it into Ceruledge. In Scarlet, Auspicious Armor is obtained in Zapapico by exchanging ten Bronzor Fragments, whereas Violet provides Malicious Armor for ten Sinistea Chips; obtaining the opposite branch normally requires trading for the armor or the evolved Pokémon. Armarouge is the special-oriented branch, combining base 125 Special Attack and 100 Defense with Fire/Psychic typing, while Ceruledge is the physical branch with base 125 Attack, 100 Special Defense, and Fire/Ghost typing; both have a 525 base-stat total. Armarouge's 120-power Armor Cannon is a devastating STAB option but lowers both defenses after use, while Ceruledge's 90-power Bitter Blade heals half the damage dealt and gives it unusually strong sustain for an offensive Pokémon. Flash Fire is generally the most straightforward story Ability for either evolution because it grants a Fire immunity and can strengthen their own Fire attacks, while Weak Armor can create sweeping opportunities after a physical hit at the cost of Defense. Armarouge can combine its STAB with coverage and setup such as Calm Mind, whereas Ceruledge appreciates physical coverage, Shadow Sneak priority, and Swords Dance; Adamant or Jolly commonly suits Ceruledge, while Modest or Timid is usually appropriate for offensive Armarouge. Both later became available in Pokémon Legends: Z-A through Mega Dimension content, but that game's real-time battle system does not use conventional Abilities directly, so Scarlet/Violet Ability interactions should not be projected onto Z-A.
competitive: The two Charcadet evolutions developed very different competitive identities in Scarlet/Violet. Armarouge is currently listed in RUBL on Smogon's SV Pokédex: it has been too strong for standard RU usage while remaining far less established in OU, and its singles niches revolve around its high Special Attack, Weak Armor speed boosts, and the threat of Armor Cannon, Psychic-type attacks, or Stored Power setup. Weak Armor can be deliberately triggered alongside Endure or a Focus Sash, while Calm Mind and Iron Defense variants can turn Stored Power into a win condition; the downside is that its five common weaknesses and middling base 75 Speed make positioning important. Armarouge also has a much more significant doubles history than that singles tier alone suggests: early Scarlet/Violet VGC prominently paired it with Indeedee-F, using Psychic Terrain and Expanding Force while Armarouge could function as a powerful Trick Room attacker or setter, often with a Quiet nature and very low Speed investment. Ceruledge, by contrast, is currently OU in SV and has remained a dangerous physical setup attacker because Swords Dance, Bitter Blade, strong Ghost STAB, and Shadow Sneak combine immediate pressure, priority, and self-healing; Weak Armor can also turn an otherwise modest base 85 Speed into sweep-level Speed after a physical hit. Focus Sash, Heavy-Duty Boots, Air Balloon, and offensive items have all supported different Ceruledge sets, with Terastallization able either to intensify its offense or remove exploitable defensive weaknesses. By 2026, Pokémon Champions also treats the branches differently: current Smogon Champions material places Armarouge in UU and Ceruledge in OU, with Ceruledge already receiving contemporary Swords Dance analyses. These later-format results should be kept distinct from the much longer Scarlet/Violet history rather than treated as retroactive evidence about their original Generation IX standing.
nuzlocke: Charcadet's biggest Nuzlocke weakness is the period before evolution: its base stats are low enough that leaving it unevolved for long exposes it to unnecessary risk, so obtaining the appropriate armor promptly is valuable. The branch choice matters considerably for survival. Armarouge has better physical Defense and powerful ranged special offense, but Armor Cannon's guaranteed Defense and Special Defense drops can make the following turn much more dangerous; a safer Fire move is often preferable when its extra power is not needed. Ceruledge is usually the more self-sufficient long-term survivor because Bitter Blade combines accurate Fire STAB with substantial healing, and Fire/Ghost supplies full immunities to Normal and Fighting attacks in addition to several resistances. Both final evolutions remain weak to Water, Ground, Rock, Ghost, and Dark, so neither should be treated as a universal safe switch despite their useful resistances. Flash Fire is particularly valuable under permadeath rules because an extra immunity creates predictable switch opportunities, whereas Weak Armor is more volatile: the Speed boost can save a sweep, but intentionally accepting physical attacks while lowering Defense increases the punishment for a bad damage estimate. Ceruledge's Shadow Sneak can finish weakened foes without exposing it to another attack, while Armarouge's strong special damage can often remove threats before they retaliate. For either branch, avoiding unnecessary setup against unknown coverage and respecting Armor Cannon's defense drops or Ceruledge's weaker physical bulk gives the line a good survival profile once it has evolved.

pokemon.name: Charcadet
pokemon.biologyAndBehavior: Charcadet is said to have formed when burnt charcoal came to life, giving its small humanoid body an intensely fiery nature. It possesses a strong fighting spirit and will challenge opponents tougher than itself; as a battle continues, its flames can exceed 1,800°F (1,000°C). It prefers berries rich in fat, fitting its dependence on fuel for its fire. Later official depictions also connect Charcadet closely with the two ancient suits of armor that direct its evolution, with the armor determining whether its fire develops into Armarouge's psychic-powered armament or Ceruledge's spectral blades.

pokemon.name: Armarouge
pokemon.biologyAndBehavior: Armarouge evolves when Charcadet dons Auspicious Armor associated with a distinguished warrior, and the armor is both the source and focus of much of its psychic power. It is intensely loyal to its Trainer and favors fair, direct combat, first relying on its reinforced armor defensively before answering with overwhelming firepower. When attacking at full force, it shifts its shoulder armor to its hands and joins the pieces into a cannon that fires blazing projectiles, the basis of its signature Armor Cannon. Legends: Z-A adds that even after pledging loyalty to a Trainer, Armarouge repeatedly leaves on its own to train and strengthen its psychic energy, giving the species an unusually explicit independent training habit.

pokemon.name: Ceruledge
pokemon.biologyAndBehavior: Ceruledge is produced by an old set of armor steeped in grudges, and its arm blades are formed from fire and spectral energy tied to the lingering regrets of fallen warriors. Those blades can extend into great swords during battle, and Ceruledge favors close combat, exploiting openings and blind spots rather than Armarouge's head-on style. Its attacks are described as merciless, and wounds from its blades can drain life energy from the victim, a trait reflected mechanically by the healing effect of Bitter Blade. Despite that grim combat behavior, official material also characterizes Ceruledge as loyal to its Trainer; later Legends: Z-A material reinforces that loyalty by describing it as attacking those that direct hostility toward its Trainer.

playthrough: Tadbulb evolves into Bellibolt with a Thunder Stone, so there is no level threshold forcing the player to keep the much weaker first stage for a particular amount of time. Bellibolt is a slow but unusually sturdy special attacker, with base 109 HP, 91 Defense, 83 Special Defense, and 103 Special Attack; its pure Electric typing also leaves Ground as its only type weakness. Its signature Ability Electromorphosis gives it the Charge effect after it is struck by an attacking move, strengthening its next Electric attack and making its low Speed less purely disadvantageous because it often moves after absorbing a hit. Static trades that offensive retaliation for a 30% paralysis chance against contact, while Damp is much more situational. Reliable Electric attacks such as Discharge or Thunderbolt are simple story staples, and Bellibolt can supplement them with Water coverage such as Muddy Water or with Parabolic Charge, which heals based on damage dealt; Slack Off provides direct recovery in Scarlet/Violet when available to the set. Its principal limitation is base 45 Speed, meaning it frequently takes damage before acting, and Ground Pokémon can completely shut down careless Electric-only play. Bold can emphasize its physical bulk for a defensive role, while Modest or Quiet can suit more offensive or slow-room-oriented use.
competitive: Bellibolt is currently NU on Smogon's Scarlet/Violet Pokédex, but its usefulness has extended into analyses for higher tiers because its combination of mixed bulk, recovery, and pure Electric typing is uncommon. Rather than functioning as a conventional fast Electric attacker, it is most successful as a bulky pivot or wall: Volt Switch maintains momentum, Slack Off restores health, and Toxic or Water coverage can stop opponents from exploiting it too freely. Static is often preferred on defensive sets because punishing physical contact with paralysis can permanently alter a game, while Electromorphosis is more threatening on sets built to absorb a hit and answer with a boosted Electric attack. Its 103 Special Attack is enough to make that retaliation meaningful, but base 45 Speed and a complete lack of Ground resistance mean that strong Ground-types and repeated high-powered attacks can overwhelm it. Terastallization can remove the Ground weakness or improve particular defensive matchups, although spending Tera on a slow wall is a real opportunity cost. Bellibolt has also appeared in Battle Stadium and official-format experimentation, but it has never been a universal metagame centerpiece; its strength is a specific defensive and momentum niche. Current Pokémon Champions material lists Bellibolt in UU and even uses Recover on defensive pivot sets, a useful example of why Champions move availability and its emerging metagame should be described separately from Bellibolt's established Scarlet/Violet sets, which commonly use Slack Off.
nuzlocke: Bellibolt is well suited to Nuzlockes because the Thunder Stone evolution can be obtained without waiting for a risky late level and the final form has substantial mixed bulk. Pure Electric typing is easy to plan around: Electric, Flying, and Steel resistances are useful, while Ground is the one direct weakness that must be respected absolutely. Its low Speed means it cannot rely on moving first to avoid damage, so checking enemy coverage is more important than it is for faster Electric-types. Static is a very safe Ability choice because contact attackers can be paralyzed without Bellibolt needing to predict or set anything up; Electromorphosis is powerful, but deliberately taking a dangerous hit simply to activate it is poor permadeath strategy. Parabolic Charge can turn damage into healing and Slack Off gives even more reliable recovery, dramatically improving long-route endurance when those moves are available. Volt Switch also helps limit exposure by letting Bellibolt attack and then bring in a teammate, although its low Speed means the incoming Pokémon often receives a comparatively safe slow pivot after Bellibolt has absorbed the opposing move. For accuracy-sensitive runs, dependable Electric STAB is preferable to gambling on Thunder, and Muddy Water's imperfect accuracy should be weighed against safer coverage when a miss could cost the Pokémon.

pokemon.name: Tadbulb
pokemon.biologyAndBehavior: Tadbulb is a small amphibious Pokémon dominated by a spherical, light-producing head, which it flashes on and off to warn its allies. By shaking its tail, it generates electricity and can store enough electrical energy to help power a city such as Levincia. It can also use electricity to float in the air, reaching higher altitudes when storm clouds provide favorable conditions. Tadbulb is associated with wetlands and riverbanks, where its electrical and amphibious adaptations overlap.

pokemon.name: Bellibolt
pokemon.biologyAndBehavior: Bellibolt's semi-transparent belly contains a yellow organ known as its belly-button dynamo; contractions of its well-developed abdominal muscles generate electricity there, which is discharged through the bumps on its head. Those bumps resemble eyes and can glow while electricity is being released, contributing to Bellibolt's intimidating appearance even though its actual eyes are much smaller. Bellibolt is capable of rapid movement but normally behaves sluggishly and is so easygoing that getting it to initiate a battle can be difficult; it may fail to react to an opponent until struck. At night its stomach produces a distinctive noise signaling hunger, and although the species is uncommon in the wild, it may be found around riverbanks.

playthrough: Wattrel evolves into Kilowattrel at level 25, giving the line a straightforward and relatively early power spike without an item or special condition. Kilowattrel's defining asset is base 125 Speed, backed by base 105 Special Attack; that combination makes it one of Paldea's better fast special pivots even though its 70/60/60 bulk is poor. Electric/Flying typing grants a complete Ground immunity plus useful Bug, Fighting, Flying, Grass, and Steel resistances, while leaving only Rock and Ice as type weaknesses. Volt Absorb is especially convenient in a normal playthrough because it adds an Electric immunity and heals one quarter of maximum HP when triggered; Wind Power instead grants Charge when the user is hit by a wind move or when Tailwind begins, and Competitive can turn enemy stat drops into a major Special Attack boost. Thunderbolt or Discharge supplies dependable Electric STAB, Flying attacks broaden coverage, and Volt Switch makes excellent use of Kilowattrel's Speed to preserve momentum. Its strongest Flying option, Hurricane, is powerful but only 70% accurate outside rain, so safer choices can be preferable for routine story battles. Timid is generally the cleanest Nature for maximizing its defining Speed advantage, while Modest is viable when extra damage matters more than winning already favorable Speed races.
competitive: Kilowattrel is currently listed in PU in Scarlet/Violet, but that usage tier understates the fact that it has documented niches in RU and other higher formats. Its base 125 Speed, Electric/Flying STAB combination, and access to Volt Switch or U-turn let it function as a very fast offensive pivot capable of pressuring Water-, Grass-, and many Flying-types while naturally ignoring Ground-type attacks. Volt Absorb is a consistent ability on pivot sets because it creates an additional immunity and possible healing opportunity, while Competitive can punish opposing stat reduction with a two-stage Special Attack increase and Wind Power can exploit Tailwind or wind attacks in more specialized contexts. Typical sets combine Electric STAB with Hurricane or another Flying attack, Volt Switch, and utility such as Roost or Weather Ball, often using Heavy-Duty Boots to preserve its ability to pivot repeatedly. The reasons it has not become a stable upper-tier fixture are equally clear: 70/60/60 bulk is very fragile, Hurricane is unreliable outside rain, bulky Ground-types can block Volt Switch while surviving its coverage, and its base 105 Special Attack can struggle to break dedicated special walls. Terastallization can patch matchup problems or intensify a STAB attack, but Kilowattrel usually derives more value from repeatedly entering, forcing a response, and pivoting than from attempting a long setup sweep. A Timid nature is normally preferred because remaining ahead of as much of the unboosted field as possible is central to its competitive identity.
nuzlocke: The Wattrel line is attractive in a Nuzlocke because it evolves at only level 25 and Kilowattrel's enormous Speed frequently prevents opponents from attacking at all. Electric/Flying typing gives a particularly valuable Ground immunity and several resistances, creating useful switch opportunities, while its only type weaknesses are Rock and Ice. The tradeoff is low physical and special bulk: a neutral high-powered move can still do serious damage, so its resistances should not be mistaken for blanket defensive security. Volt Absorb is the safest of its Abilities for permadeath play because it creates a second full immunity and can restore health, whereas Competitive and Wind Power are more matchup-dependent offensive rewards. Volt Switch is excellent risk management because Kilowattrel can usually move first, deal damage, and leave before the opponent acts; this is especially useful in known matchups where the replacement can absorb the expected attack safely. Hurricane's 70% accuracy is a significant liability when a miss exposes such a frail Pokémon to retaliation, so Air Slash or another reliable attack may be preferable when the extra power is unnecessary. Used as a fast attacker and pivot rather than a tank, Kilowattrel can be a strong survivor, but unexpected Rock or Ice coverage and priority attacks deserve constant respect.

pokemon.name: Wattrel
pokemon.biologyAndBehavior: Wattrel catches the wind with its wings in a way that causes the bones inside them to generate electricity. It hunts along the coast by diving toward the water and electrocuting prey, including Arrokuda. Wattrel nests near the edges of coastal cliffs, and those nests have an unusual crackling texture; humans consider the nests a popular delicacy. The species' dependence on wind for electricity foreshadows both its Flying/Electric ecology and the Wind Power Ability shared with its evolution.

pokemon.name: Kilowattrel
pokemon.biologyAndBehavior: Kilowattrel generates electricity with its wings and stores that energy in an expandable throat sac, which glows as the stored charge is amplified. It is an exceptional long-distance flier, capable of traveling more than 430 miles (700 km) in a single day by riding favorable winds. Despite its strong association with the sea and its seabird-like anatomy, Kilowattrel is a poor swimmer because its feathers contain comparatively little oil. This combination of wind-assisted endurance and electrical storage makes it more specialized for sustained aerial travel than its smaller pre-evolution.

playthrough: Maschiff is obtainable relatively early in Paldea and evolves into Mabosstiff at level 30, so the line can reach its final form by the middle portion of a normal Scarlet/Violet playthrough. Mabosstiff is a straightforward physical attacker with base 120 Attack, respectable 80/90/70 bulk, and base 85 Speed, while pure Dark typing provides a Psychic immunity and resistances to Dark and Ghost. Its main weaknesses are Fighting, Bug, and Fairy, all common enough that it should not be switched blindly into physical attackers simply because its Defense is solid. Crunch is reliable physical Dark STAB, and coverage such as Play Rough or Psychic Fangs can help punish opponents that resist Dark, although Play Rough's 90% accuracy is less dependable than Crunch. Intimidate is usually the most generally useful Ability in a story run because entering battle immediately reduces opposing Attack, while Guard Dog blocks forced switching and turns opposing Intimidate into an Attack boost; Stakeout can inflict extreme damage on a target that switches in but ordinary story AI does not switch often enough for that to define the playthrough. Its stats support either Adamant for maximum damage or Jolly when outspeeding mid-speed opponents matters. The line later appears in Legends: Z-A's Mega Dimension content, but conventional Scarlet/Violet Ability mechanics should not be assumed there because Z-A does not explicitly implement standard Abilities.
competitive: Mabosstiff is currently ZU in Scarlet/Violet and has never escaped the limitations of being a fairly linear physical Dark-type, but it possesses a real offensive niche rather than being competitively featureless. Its defining tool is Stakeout, which doubles the relevant attacking stat when hitting a target on the turn that target switches in; combined with base 120 Attack and Choice Band, this can make ostensibly safe defensive switching unexpectedly expensive. Choice Scarf is another documented option that patches its merely average base 85 Speed, while Crunch provides dependable STAB and Play Rough or Psychic Fangs covers some Dark-resistant targets. Smogon's ZU material consequently treats Mabosstiff as a prediction-heavy Choice attacker, and draft analysis similarly values it as a low-cost wallbreaker whose ceiling rises sharply when the user correctly anticipates a switch. The problems are consistency and competition: Stakeout is strongest only on a correctly predicted switch, its coverage cannot overwhelm every physical wall, and it lacks the Speed, recovery, or broad utility that would make it easy to justify in stronger tiers. Intimidate and Guard Dog provide alternative utility, but generally sacrifice the unique immediate pressure that makes Stakeout attractive in singles. Jolly is common on Choice sets to improve Speed control, though Adamant can be justified when maximizing wallbreaking damage is the priority.
nuzlocke: Mabosstiff is a useful Nuzlocke Pokémon primarily because it combines strong physical offense with one of the best safety Abilities in the game: Intimidate. Lowering an opposing physical attacker's Attack on entry can turn dangerous two-hit knockouts into manageable exchanges and can also protect the next teammate if Mabosstiff pivots away, giving the Ability team-wide defensive value. Its pure Dark typing supplies a complete Psychic immunity and useful Ghost and Dark resistances, while Fighting, Bug, and Fairy attacks remain the major hazards. Base 120 Attack lets it rely on accurate Crunch for much of its damage rather than constantly gambling on low-accuracy or recoil moves, although Play Rough's occasional miss should be considered before using it in a life-or-death turn. Guard Dog is valuable in specific fights involving Intimidate or forced switching, but Intimidate is more broadly protective; Stakeout is potent yet inconsistent because in-game opponents rarely switch predictably. Destiny Bond is fundamentally at odds with a conventional Nuzlocke because its intended payoff requires Mabosstiff to faint, so the move should normally be avoided regardless of its competitive utility. With appropriate matchup knowledge and Intimidate cycling, Mabosstiff offers a larger margin for error than its offensive appearance initially suggests.

pokemon.name: Maschiff
pokemon.biologyAndBehavior: Maschiff has a heavily developed jaw and fangs powerful enough to crunch through boulders, while a thick layer of fat beneath its body provides substantial physical protection. It habitually scowls in an effort to intimidate others and be taken seriously, but the expression is so ineffective that even crying children may laugh when they see it. Legends: Z-A adds that Maschiff live in exceptionally close-knit packs, giving the species a clearer social structure than Scarlet/Violet's entries alone established. Its attempted intimidation is therefore not simply solitary aggression but a recurring behavioral trait in a strongly bonded pack animal.

pokemon.name: Mabosstiff
pokemon.biologyAndBehavior: Mabosstiff is a large canine Pokémon whose prominent dewlap can store energy and release it all at once to drive enemies away; it is also known to shed its fur frequently. Despite its intimidating appearance, Mabosstiff is described as kind and gentle and particularly enjoys playing with children. That temperament changes sharply when its family is threatened, at which point it bares its teeth and becomes highly protective. Legends: Z-A strengthens this characterization by stating that Mabosstiff will relentlessly pursue and put an end to foes that threaten its family, making familial defense one of the species' most explicit behavioral traits.

playthrough: Shroodle evolves into Grafaiai at level 28, an uncomplicated midgame evolution that turns a weak early-stage Pokémon into a fast utility attacker. Grafaiai's Poison/Normal typing is unusual: Normal removes Poison's normal exposure to Ghost attacks by granting a Ghost immunity, while Poison supplies resistances to Fairy, Grass, Bug, and Poison; the combined typing is weak only to Ground and Psychic. Its base 110 Speed is the line's strongest conventional stat, with base 95 Attack and 80 Special Attack allowing offense but 63/65/72 bulk making prolonged direct exchanges dangerous. Poison Touch can add poison chances to contact attacks, Unburden enables specialized sweeping after an item is consumed or lost, and the Hidden Ability Prankster gives priority to status moves such as Encore or Parting Shot, though Dark-type opponents are immune to Prankster-boosted status moves. Physical sets can use Poison Jab as dependable STAB, Knock Off for excellent item disruption, and U-turn or Parting Shot to control positioning; Gunk Shot is much stronger but its 80% accuracy is a meaningful drawback in ordinary play. Grafaiai's signature Doodle can copy a target's Ability onto both the user and its ally in doubles, but the effect is highly matchup-dependent and is not a reason by itself to build around Grafaiai in a normal single-player run. Jolly best supports its fast physical role, while Adamant can be useful on Unburden-oriented sets where the Speed boost supplies enough pace on its own.
competitive: Grafaiai is currently NU in Scarlet/Violet, but its competitive identity is defined less by raw power than by the unusual amount of disruption packed into a base 110 Speed Pokémon. Prankster gives priority to status moves and has supported combinations such as Encore and Parting Shot, allowing Grafaiai to lock an opponent into an exploitable move and then reduce offensive pressure while pivoting to a teammate. Knock Off removes items, U-turn offers a damage-dealing pivot, and Gunk Shot gives substantially stronger Poison STAB when its imperfect accuracy is acceptable; Poison Touch can add incidental status to contact-heavy sets. Unburden creates a very different role, enabling Swords Dance plus Acrobatics or other physical coverage after an appropriate held item is consumed, and later SV analyses have continued to explore this terrain- or seed-enabled sweeping route. Its signature Doodle is much more specialized: by replacing both Grafaiai's and its ally's Abilities with a target's Ability, it can enable creative doubles combinations, but it depends heavily on the matchup and partner rather than representing a universally strong singles tool. Grafaiai's ceiling is held down by modest base 95 Attack, only 80 Special Attack, and poor 63/65/72 bulk, so even with excellent utility it struggles to trade directly with stronger attackers. Its NU placement therefore fits a Pokémon with genuine tactical value and multiple distinct sets, but not the raw defensive or offensive efficiency needed to dominate higher tiers consistently.
nuzlocke: Grafaiai can be valuable in a Nuzlocke when treated as a fast disruptor rather than a Pokémon expected to absorb repeated attacks. Base 110 Speed often lets it act first, and Poison/Normal typing provides a useful Ghost immunity plus several resistances, but its mediocre defenses mean unexpected Ground, Psychic, or strong neutral coverage can become lethal quickly. Prankster is particularly useful for safety: priority Encore can trap an opponent in a harmless or setup move, while priority Parting Shot can lower an enemy's offenses and bring a sturdier teammate in under reduced pressure; the important exception is that Dark-types are immune to Prankster-boosted status moves. U-turn supplies a more straightforward pivot, and Knock Off can reduce later danger by removing enemy held items. Poison Jab's perfect accuracy is generally safer than relying on 80%-accurate Gunk Shot when a miss could expose Grafaiai to a knockout. Unburden can produce a fast offensive sweep after item consumption, but setup plans that require surviving a hit are less forgiving on Grafaiai than on a bulky Pokémon. Doodle should also be used cautiously in double battles because overwriting both the user's and ally's Abilities can remove defensive protections as easily as it can create a clever advantage.

pokemon.name: Shroodle
pokemon.biologyAndBehavior: Shroodle is usually mellow, but when angered it bites with disproportionately large front teeth coated in poisonous saliva; the poison can cause paralysis. It also uses a foul-smelling poisonous liquid to paint markings around its nest, discouraging enemies from approaching its territory. Legends: Z-A reinforces the importance of both adaptations, describing Shroodle's toxic saliva and oversized front teeth as its primary means of protecting itself from foes.

pokemon.name: Grafaiai
pokemon.biologyAndBehavior: Grafaiai is a solitary, nocturnal primate Pokémon with greatly elongated middle fingers that it coats in brightly colored poisonous saliva; the saliva's color changes with a diet that includes Berries and Bug-type Pokémon. It is moody, meticulous, and highly territorial, fighting other Pokémon—including members of its own species—and using the saliva to paint trees, rocks, and other surfaces throughout its territory. Each individual repeatedly paints its own distinctive pattern for its entire life, making the markings a persistent personal signature as well as a territorial signal. The sweet scent of its painted poison attracts Bug Pokémon at night; the victims become immobilized, allowing Grafaiai to return and collect them by dawn, and when Grafaiai senses danger its poison can become concentrated enough to immobilize a victim for roughly three days. Legends: Z-A confirms that the diet-dependent saliva remains central to territorial marking, adding another main-series source for behavior first established in Scarlet/Violet and official promotional material.

playthrough: Bramblin is obtainable in dry areas of Paldea such as East Province (Area Three) and the Asado Desert, but it begins with a very low 275 base-stat total and is much more useful once evolved. In Scarlet and Violet, Bramblin evolves into Brambleghast after walking 1,000 steps with it outside its Poké Ball using Let's Go! and then leveling it while it is still outside; the unusual requirement is easy to complete deliberately but can delay the evolution if the player simply levels it normally. Brambleghast becomes a fast physical attacker with base 115 Attack and 90 Speed, and its Grass/Ghost typing grants immunities to Normal and Fighting alongside useful resistances to Water, Ground, Grass, and Electric. Wind Rider is the more distinctive Ability: wind-based moves do no damage to Brambleghast, and either being targeted by one or having Tailwind begin on its side raises its Attack, although this interaction is much more matchup-dependent in a normal story run than a simple defensive Ability would be. Its offense can be built around physical Grass and Ghost STAB with Shadow Sneak for priority, while Rapid Spin, Spikes, and Strength Sap give it far more utility than its offensive stat line alone suggests. Jolly or Adamant suits straightforward attacking sets, while more defensive utility builds can justify an Impish nature; in ordinary play, however, the main limitation is that 55 base HP and only 70 in each defense leave little room for careless switching despite the useful immunities.
competitive: Brambleghast is currently listed in NU on Smogon's Scarlet/Violet Pokédex and has developed into a genuine role-compression Pokémon rather than merely a novelty tied to Wind Rider. Its most valuable competitive combination is access to Rapid Spin, Spikes, strong physical STAB attacks, and the ability to spinblock opposing Rapid Spin because of its Ghost typing, letting it influence both sides of the entry-hazard game. Current NU analysis highlights offensive sets using Poltergeist and Power Whip, often with Heavy-Duty Boots or Choice Band, while Shadow Sneak gives it revenge-killing utility and Strength Sap can partially compensate for its weak natural bulk. Wind Rider is competitively meaningful because it can turn opposing Hurricane or other wind moves into an immunity and an Attack boost, and in doubles or Tailwind-oriented formats it can also exploit its own side's Tailwind activation. Infiltrator is a legitimate alternative when bypassing Substitute or screens is more valuable than the wind immunity, but it is generally less defining. Brambleghast's 115 Attack and 90 Speed are good enough to punish passive play, yet its 55/70/70 bulk and weaknesses to Fire, Ice, Flying, Dark, and Ghost make it easy for stronger attackers and priority users to revenge kill, which is why its success comes from combining offense with hazard utility rather than functioning as a dominant standalone sweeper.
nuzlocke: Bramblin is a risky early-stage Nuzlocke Pokémon because its very low HP and defenses leave it vulnerable to unexpected neutral hits, so completing the 1,000-step evolution requirement promptly is much safer than carrying it unevolved for many battles. Brambleghast improves dramatically and its Normal and Fighting immunities can create completely safe switches when the opposing moveset is known, but those immunities should not obscure its five common weaknesses and low HP. Wind Rider can provide another no-damage switch against known wind moves, though it is much less dependable in blind play because the player must know that the incoming attack actually belongs to that move category. Strength Sap is particularly valuable under permadeath rules because it both restores HP and lowers the target's Attack, turning some physical matchups from dangerous into sustainable ones, while Shadow Sneak can finish weakened enemies without exposing Brambleghast to a faster return hit. Rapid Spin is safe utility when hazards matter, but high-power options such as Power Whip and Poltergeist carry accuracy risk, so more reliable attacks can be preferable when a miss could cost the run.
