Shadow Sneak provides safe priority for finishing weakened targets, whereas Poltergeist and Play Rough carry 90% accuracy and therefore more miss risk when a guaranteed knockout is required. Memento causes the user to faint and is normally incompatible with preserving Houndstone, while Rest and Pain Split provide less dependable recovery than true instant healing. With known opposing coverage and careful handling of Fluffy's Fire weakness, Houndstone can be a durable and valuable team member rather than merely a Last Respects gimmick.

pokemon.name: Greavard
pokemon.biologyAndBehavior: Greavard is a shaggy Ghost-type dog Pokémon with a candle-like flame protruding from its head; it often rests underground with only this candle visible while waiting for someone to approach. It is exceptionally friendly, affectionate, playful, and lonely, and may follow someone permanently after receiving even a small amount of attention. That friendliness is dangerous because Greavard unintentionally drains the life force of nearby creatures, including by rubbing its fur against them during play. Scarlet records a rumor that Greavard is the reincarnation of a dog Pokémon that died in the wild without ever interacting with a human, while Legends: Z-A further emphasizes its roughhousing behavior and the exhausting effect of prolonged contact. Its mouth does not contain ordinary teeth; instead, its serrated lips are strong enough to shatter bones.

pokemon.name: Houndstone
pokemon.biologyAndBehavior: Houndstone is a large skeletal canine whose legs and tail appear to float beneath a heavy covering of shaggy fur rather than attaching visibly to a conventional torso. A tombstone-like protuberance rises from its head, and the species strongly dislikes having that structure touched. It spends much of its time sleeping buried in graveyards with only the tombstone visible and is described as the most loyal of all dog Pokémon. Its origin is closely tied to mourning: Violet states that a lovingly mourned Pokémon can be reborn as Houndstone, while Legends: Z-A describes a Pokémon that spent many years guarding its deceased master's gravestone before being reborn as a Ghost type. This combination of graveyard habitat, rebirth, and extreme loyalty gives Houndstone one of the clearest death-and-bereavement ecologies among ordinary Pokémon species.

playthrough: Flamigo is a standalone Fighting/Flying Pokémon that can be caught as early as South Province (Area One), giving the player access to a fully evolved 500-BST attacker extraordinarily early in Scarlet/Violet. Base 115 Attack and 90 Speed let it overpower much of the early and midgame immediately, while Fighting/Flying STAB gives broad offensive coverage and its Flying typing supplies a valuable Ground immunity. Scrappy is usually the most convenient single-player Ability because Fighting- and Normal-type attacks can hit Ghost Pokémon and, under modern mechanics, Intimidate cannot lower Flamigo's Attack; Costar is primarily a doubles Ability, copying an ally's stat-stage changes when Flamigo enters the field. Its level-up progression is practical, with Wing Attack available early, Roost at level 31 for reliable recovery, and Brave Bird later for enormous Flying damage, while TMs can provide options such as Close Combat and U-turn. The main limitation is defensive: Flamigo is weak to Flying, Electric, Psychic, Ice, and Fairy, and its 82/74/64 bulk is only moderate, so it should generally use its Speed and offensive pressure rather than absorb repeated neutral hits. Brave Bird recoil and Close Combat's Defense and Special Defense drops are also meaningful costs even when the attacks secure easy knockouts. Adamant maximizes its already strong physical damage, while Jolly is useful when keeping Flamigo ahead of faster story opponents matters.
competitive: Flamigo has established a legitimate lower-tier singles niche and is currently classified as NU in Smogon's Scarlet/Violet Pokédex. Its distinguishing traits are a strong base 115 Attack, useful base 90 Speed, the rare Fighting/Flying STAB combination, and U-turn, which lets it act as an offensive pivot rather than committing to every matchup. Scrappy is especially valuable because Close Combat remains effective into Ghost-types and Flamigo cannot have its Attack reduced by Intimidate, while Choice Scarf sets can revenge kill faster threats and Choice Band sets turn Brave Bird and Close Combat into much stronger wallbreaking tools. Roost gives non-Choice variants longevity that many similarly aggressive Fighting-types lack, although Brave Bird recoil, entry hazards, and its five weaknesses still wear it down. Costar has a more specialized doubles history: because it copies an ally's stat boosts, Flamigo was used as a partner to Commander-boosted Dondozo, allowing it to enter beside a Dondozo with +2 stages across its major stats and copy those boosts for itself. That interaction created a dangerous surprise option in early Generation IX VGC, but it required significant team structure and gave up Scrappy, so it never defined Flamigo's overall competitive identity as strongly as its straightforward singles offense. Its present NU status reflects real offensive value without overstating it as a top-tier threat.
nuzlocke: Flamigo is one of the strongest early Nuzlocke encounters in Paldea because it arrives fully evolved with base 115 Attack, base 90 Speed, and no evolution requirement or weak developmental stage to protect. Its Ground immunity and resistances to Fighting, Dark, Grass, and especially Bug can create safe switches, while Scrappy removes awkward Ghost immunities and prevents Intimidate from undermining its physical damage. Roost at level 31 is an unusually important safety tool because it provides dependable recovery without requiring items, substantially improving Flamigo's long-term survival compared with many early-route attackers. The strongest attacks require judgment: Brave Bird's recoil can turn a winning matchup into accumulated danger, and Close Combat lowers both defenses after use, so Wing Attack, Acrobatics, Low Kick, or other lower-risk moves may be preferable when they still guarantee the knockout. Its five weaknesses and only moderate defenses make blind switching unsafe despite its excellent offensive profile, particularly against unexpected Psychic, Electric, Ice, or Fairy coverage. Costar can be spectacular in double battles when paired with a boosted ally, but its value is much less consistent in a typical Nuzlocke than Scrappy's permanent utility. Used as a fast attacker rather than a general-purpose wall, Flamigo offers an excellent combination of early availability, immediate power, and reliable recovery.

pokemon.name: Flamigo
pokemon.biologyAndBehavior: Flamigo is a flamingo-like Pokémon that normally keeps the base of its long neck tied into a knot; this apparently prevents energy stored in its belly from escaping through its beak. When it attacks, it can untie the neck and rapidly swing its head. Flamigo is highly social and gathers around wetlands and bodies of water in enormous flocks that can exceed 10,000 individuals; through a behavior called synchronizing, an entire flock can move or attack together in remarkable harmony. Its ecology includes a documented predator relationship with Dondozo: Tatsugiri can lure Flamigo into position so that the much larger Dondozo can ambush it.

playthrough: Cetoddle evolves into Cetitan when exposed to an Ice Stone, so evolution timing depends on obtaining the item rather than reaching a particular level; the line itself is encountered around the later, snowy portion of Paldea such as Glaseado Mountain. Cetitan is an enormous physical attacker with base 170 HP and 113 Attack, and its 521 BST is concentrated into raw HP and offense rather than balanced defenses. Thick Fat is excellent for general play because it halves the offensive stat used by opposing Fire- and Ice-type moves, effectively cancelling the normal super-effective damage multiplier of Fire against an Ice-type under ordinary circumstances; Slush Rush instead doubles Cetitan's Speed in snow, while Sheer Force can amplify compatible attacks. Generation IX snow also increases the Defense of Ice-type Pokémon by 50%, which works particularly well with Cetitan's massive HP and can compensate for its otherwise modest base 65 Defense. Ice Spinner is a reliable 80-base-power, perfectly accurate physical STAB move, Ice Shard provides priority, and coverage such as Earthquake helps against Fire-, Rock-, and Steel-types that resist or threaten Ice. Belly Drum can maximize Attack instantly and pairs explosively with Slush Rush and priority, but losing half of maximum HP is unnecessary for most story battles and can turn Cetitan's large health pool into a liability. Jolly is useful on Slush Rush sets that want to sweep under snow, Adamant maximizes direct damage, and Careful can help compensate for Cetitan's low Special Defense on bulkier approaches.
competitive: Cetitan is currently classified as NUBL in Smogon's Scarlet/Violet Pokédex, meaning it is banned from NU despite lacking enough usage for a standard higher usage tier, and its documented higher-tier niche revolves primarily around snow offense. Slush Rush doubles its Speed in snow, while Generation IX snow simultaneously gives Ice-types a 50% Defense increase, turning Cetitan into a much harder physical target while it prepares to attack. The defining offensive set uses Belly Drum to maximize Attack, frequently with a Sitrus Berry to restore some of the health sacrificed, followed by Ice Spinner or Icicle Spear, Earthquake, and Ice Shard for priority. Base 170 HP gives Cetitan unusually high raw survivability, and base 113 Attack means it can remain threatening even before Belly Drum, but base 55 Special Defense leaves it vulnerable to strong special attackers and its pure Ice typing supplies only one natural resistance. Thick Fat can support bulkier variants by mitigating Fire damage, while Sheer Force has offensive applications, but neither reproduces the speed control and immediate sweeping potential of Slush Rush in snow. Its dependence on weather, setup time, and a type with four common weaknesses prevents it from being universally splashable, but the NUBL placement reflects that snow-supported Belly Drum sets are substantially more dangerous than Cetitan's modest Speed initially suggests.
nuzlocke: Cetitan can be a powerful Nuzlocke tank and attacker, but the line is obtained relatively late and requires an Ice Stone to evolve, so access to the final form is less automatic than a simple level evolution. Base 170 HP gives Cetitan a huge buffer against neutral damage, and Thick Fat is usually the safest Ability because it sharply reduces Fire damage while also reducing Ice attacks that it already resists. Snow is particularly valuable in Generation IX because the 50% Defense increase for Ice-types patches Cetitan's mediocre base 65 Defense, and Slush Rush can instead use the same weather to double Speed and avoid damage by moving first. Ice Spinner and Ice Shard are excellent permadeath tools because both are perfectly accurate, with Ice Shard providing emergency priority to finish weakened targets. Belly Drum is far less attractive than in competitive play: immediately sacrificing half of Cetitan's maximum HP creates substantial critical-hit and revenge-kill risk, and the offensive boost is often unnecessary against ordinary trainers. Its low base 55 Special Defense and weaknesses to Fighting, Rock, Steel, and Fire mean the huge HP stat should not be mistaken for universal bulk, especially when Thick Fat is absent. A conservative Thick Fat or snow-assisted set is generally safer than trying to reproduce an all-or-nothing competitive Belly Drum sweep.

pokemon.name: Cetoddle
pokemon.biologyAndBehavior: Cetoddle is a small land-dwelling cetacean whose ancestors are said to have lived in the ocean before migrating onto land, making its evolutionary history the reverse of the land-to-sea transition described for its suspected relative Wailmer. It inhabits cold regions in pods of roughly five individuals and enjoys eating minerals found in snow and ice. The species is strongly social and dislikes loneliness; Pokémon Sleep research has observed Cetoddle becoming restless or panicked in its sleep, possibly while dreaming that it has been separated from its group. It may also pound the ground while sleeping when agitated.

pokemon.name: Cetitan
pokemon.biologyAndBehavior: Cetitan is a huge terrestrial cetacean protected by powerful muscles and a thick layer of subcutaneous fat that allow it to support its weight and migrate through snowy environments. The horn on its upper jaw accumulates ice energy until it reaches cryogenic temperatures capable of freezing the surrounding area. Cetitan live in pods, share some habitat with Avalugg, and in Paldea primarily consume snow and ice around Glaseado Mountain. They use echolocation-like sound waves to locate and communicate with one another; their calls have been compared to flute sounds, and sleeping Cetitan have occasionally been observed emitting calls that may unconsciously seek other members of the pod. They can also slide across snow and ice on their bellies to move more quickly.

playthrough: Veluza is a standalone Water/Psychic Pokémon found in several Paldean bodies of water, including Casseroya Lake and the western and northern seas, and it arrives with a respectable base 102 Attack but only base 70 Speed before setup. Its defining combination is the Hidden Ability Sharpness and the signature move Fillet Away: Sharpness increases the power of slicing moves by 50%, strengthening attacks such as Aqua Cutter, Psycho Cut, and Night Slash, while Fillet Away sacrifices half of Veluza's maximum HP to raise Attack, Special Attack, and Speed by two stages each. That setup can turn Veluza into a devastating story sweeper, but it is often more power than a normal battle requires and the HP cost leaves the user vulnerable if it fails to secure immediate knockouts. Mold Breaker is a useful alternative Ability because it lets Veluza's attacks ignore many defensive Abilities, but it gives up the large and consistent Sharpness boost to its best physical moves. Water/Psychic provides resistances to Fighting, Steel, Fire, Water, Psychic, and Ice, but Veluza is weak to Bug, Ghost, Grass, Electric, and Dark and has only moderate 90/73/65 bulk. Aqua Jet can provide priority, and Recover is obtainable through its Egg Move access in Scarlet/Violet, giving a more conservative set actual longevity if the player chooses to prepare it. Adamant maximizes Sharpness-boosted physical damage, while Jolly can help before Fillet Away has supplied its Speed increase.
competitive: Veluza's competitive reputation was built around how closely Fillet Away resembles an even more extreme form of Shell Smash: at the cost of half of maximum HP, it raises Attack, Special Attack, and Speed by two stages without lowering either defense. Early SV NU analysis described Sharpness Veluza as a dangerous hyper-offense sweeper, because a single setup turn made Aqua Cutter, Psycho Cut, and Night Slash dramatically stronger while doubling its middling base 70 Speed. Sharpness multiplies slicing-move power by 1.5, so the Ability increases damage without requiring another turn of setup, and Tera could further increase a favored STAB or change Veluza's defensive matchups. Despite that frightening ceiling, Veluza has fallen substantially and is currently classified as ZU in Smogon's Scarlet/Violet data. The reason is practical rather than mysterious: before Fillet Away it has only moderate Speed and power, after using the move it has voluntarily lost half its HP, and its five weaknesses plus mediocre 73/65 defenses can make finding and surviving a setup opportunity difficult. Mold Breaker can bypass defensive Abilities such as Unaware for specialized strategies, but giving up Sharpness noticeably reduces its most natural physical attacks. Veluza therefore remains capable of sweeping an unprepared team but is a good example of a Pokémon whose theoretical setup payoff is much greater than its consistency in stronger metagames.
nuzlocke: Veluza is much safer in a Nuzlocke when treated as a direct attacker rather than built around Fillet Away. Sharpness-boosted Aqua Cutter and Psycho Cut provide strong physical STAB without recoil, and their high critical-hit ratios can occasionally break defensive boosts without requiring Veluza to sacrifice health first. Fillet Away's +2 Attack, Special Attack, and Speed is enormous, but losing half of maximum HP before the opponent attacks creates exactly the kind of low-margin situation that permadeath play normally tries to avoid; a critical hit, priority move, or surviving target can immediately end the run for Veluza. Recover can improve long-term reliability when obtained through Scarlet/Violet's Egg Move system, and Aqua Jet supplies valuable priority for cleaning up weakened opponents. Water/Psychic gives six useful resistances, but weaknesses to Bug, Ghost, Grass, Electric, and Dark are common enough that blind setup is particularly dangerous. Mold Breaker can be preferable for a known boss whose Ability would otherwise invalidate an attack, while Sharpness is the more consistently useful choice for normal battles. Veluza can be effective, but conservative move selection and avoiding unnecessary Fillet Away gambles materially increase its chance of surviving a full Nuzlocke.

pokemon.name: Veluza
pokemon.biologyAndBehavior: Veluza is a predatory fish Pokémon whose internal fins and spine-like structures extend beneath a layer of disposable outer flesh. Its hunting strategy involves deliberately shedding this excess flesh, which sharpens its mind, increases its psychic power, and makes its body more agile so that it can rapidly pursue and tear into prey. The species has exceptional regenerative ability and can regrow what it discards. The shed flesh is not wasted by humans: it is described as having a mild but delicious flavor.

playthrough: Dondozo is a standalone pure Water-type encountered in Casseroya Lake and arrives as an exceptionally durable physical tank with base 150 HP, 115 Defense, and a respectable 100 Attack. Unaware is usually its most valuable Ability because it ignores opposing stat changes when calculating damage, allowing Dondozo to stand in front of setup sweepers that would overwhelm ordinary defensive Pokémon; Oblivious prevents Taunt and Intimidate, while Water Veil prevents burns. Its enormous HP and physical Defense make it exceptionally forgiving against physical attackers, but base 65 Special Defense and base 35 Speed mean strong special Grass or Electric attacks can still remove it quickly. Liquidation is a reliable physical Water STAB, Body Press benefits from its high Defense, and Curse can simultaneously increase Attack and Defense at the cost of Speed Dondozo barely uses in the first place. Rest is its main form of full recovery and can be paired with Sleep Talk, but the forced sleep turns are much less convenient in a normal playthrough than immediate recovery moves would be. Wave Crash provides much higher Water damage but its recoil can consume Dondozo's huge HP pool rapidly, while the signature Order Up is a perfectly accurate Dragon attack whose extra stat-boosting effect matters specifically when Commander Tatsugiri is inside Dondozo during doubles. Impish is ideal for maximizing its defining physical wall role, while Careful can help patch the weaker Special Defense and Adamant can suit a more offensive Curse or doubles approach.
competitive: Dondozo has been one of Generation IX's most important defensive Pokémon in singles and one of its most distinctive team archetypes in doubles. Smogon currently classifies it as SV OU, where base 150 HP, base 115 Defense, pure Water typing, and Unaware let it answer a wide range of physical setup sweepers that would otherwise punish conventional walls. Singles sets commonly use combinations of Liquidation or Body Press, Rest, Sleep Talk, Curse, and defensive Terastallization; its greatest drawbacks are weak immediate special bulk, passivity against some special attackers, and dependence on Rest rather than conventional reliable recovery. Its doubles identity is completely different: when a Commander Tatsugiri enters its mouth, Dondozo receives +2 stages in Attack, Defense, Special Attack, Special Defense, and Speed, turning an already massive Pokémon into a self-contained offensive and defensive win condition. Order Up can then add a further Attack, Defense, or Speed boost depending on whether the swallowed Tatsugiri is Curly, Droopy, or Stretchy Form, while Tera and moves such as Wave Crash, Earthquake, Substitute, and Protect create many possible variants. The pairing remained competitively relevant for years rather than being only an early-SV gimmick; official 2026 EUIC preview coverage noted Dondozo taking second at the Birmingham Regional and Top 8 in Toronto and still emphasized the need for every serious team to have a Dondozo plan. Its longevity comes from the fact that Unaware Dondozo is already functional without Tatsugiri, while the Commander mode can force opponents to preserve very specific counterplay.
nuzlocke: Dondozo is one of Paldea's safest answers to physical threats because 150 HP and 115 Defense give it an enormous physical damage buffer even before defensive investment. Unaware is particularly valuable in permadeath play because it neutralizes much of the danger from enemy Swords Dance, Dragon Dance, Bulk Up, Defense boosts, and similar stat-based snowballing when damage is calculated, greatly reducing the chance that a setup turn suddenly becomes lethal. Water Veil is also useful because burn cannot cripple Dondozo's physical Attack, while Oblivious prevents Intimidate and Taunt, but neither provides the same broad emergency protection as Unaware. The major danger is special damage: base 65 Special Defense is mediocre and Dondozo is so slow that strong Electric or Grass special attacks will usually land first. Liquidation and Body Press are safer routine attacks than Wave Crash, whose recoil can remove large amounts of health precisely because Dondozo's maximum HP is so high, and Fissure's 30% accuracy is incompatible with predictable Nuzlocke planning. Rest can fully restore health and status but creates two turns of sleep, making Sleep Talk or a carefully controlled safe matchup important if it is used during battle. In doubles, Commander Tatsugiri can make Dondozo extraordinarily powerful, but even without that specialized pairing its natural bulk and Unaware make it an excellent survival-oriented team member.

pokemon.name: Dondozo
pokemon.biologyAndBehavior: Dondozo is an enormous catfish-like Pokémon and one of the largest ordinary Pokémon species known, with enough physical strength to create great waves simply by thrashing its body. Despite that strength and a very large appetite, it is poor at catching food on its own and forms an unusually close hunting partnership with Tatsugiri: Tatsugiri acts as the strategist and lure, while Dondozo follows its commands and attacks the prey. Dondozo is loyal to Tatsugiri and protects its much smaller partner inside its mouth, effectively serving as both muscle and shelter in the relationship. Documented prey include Basculin and Flamigo. A giant Dondozo living with a giant Tatsugiri in Casseroya Lake became part of the False Dragon Titan encounter after feeding on Spicy Herba Mystica.

playthrough: Tatsugiri is a standalone Dragon/Water special attacker found around Casseroya Lake, with base 120 Special Attack, 95 Special Defense, and 82 Speed giving it respectable immediate power despite its small size. Dragon/Water is defensively efficient, leaving only Dragon and Fairy weaknesses while resisting Steel and taking only one-quarter damage from Fire and Water before Ability effects. In an ordinary single-player battle, Commander normally does nothing because it requires an allied Dondozo in a Double Battle; the Hidden Ability Storm Drain is therefore much more generally useful, granting a Water immunity while raising Special Attack when a Water move is redirected into Tatsugiri. Nasty Plot can double its Special Attack, while Surf or Muddy Water and Dragon Pulse provide STAB; Draco Meteor offers much greater immediate Dragon damage at the cost of a two-stage Special Attack drop. The three ordinary forms have identical base stats and conventional movepools, but in doubles the form changes the extra stat Dondozo gains from successful uses of Order Up after Commander activates: Curly raises Attack, Droopy raises Defense, and Stretchy raises Speed. Mega Tatsugiri was added later in the Mega Dimension DLC for Pokémon Legends: Z-A and requires Tatsugirinite; it keeps Dragon/Water typing but rises from 475 to 575 BST, with 68/65/90/135/125/92 base stats, substantially improving its special offense, defenses, and Speed. That Mega is not part of Scarlet/Violet's normal playthrough and Z-A does not use the conventional Ability system in the same way as Scarlet/Violet, so Commander or any future standard-format Mega Ability should not be retroactively assumed to function there exactly as it does in turn-based main-series battles. Timid and Modest are the most natural Natures for ordinary offensive Tatsugiri.
competitive: Tatsugiri has two very different competitive identities: an independent lower-tier special attacker in singles and the enabling half of the famous Dondozo Commander core in doubles. Smogon currently classifies regular Tatsugiri as SV PU, where Storm Drain, base 120 Special Attack, Nasty Plot, Draco Meteor, Surf, and Rapid Spin let it function as an offensive spinner or inexpensive special breaker despite mediocre physical bulk and only base 82 Speed. Its singles role is limited by shallow coverage and 68/60 physical bulk, but Storm Drain gives a valuable Water immunity and the threat of a free Special Attack boost. In VGC, Commander is the defining mechanic: if Tatsugiri enters while an allied Dondozo is present, Tatsugiri disappears into Dondozo's mouth and becomes unable to act or be targeted while Dondozo receives +2 stages in Attack, Defense, Special Attack, Special Defense, and Speed. The form then determines Order Up's additional boost—Attack for Curly, Defense for Droopy, or Speed for Stretchy—and if Dondozo is knocked out, Tatsugiri returns to the field and can still contribute with attacks such as Draco Meteor or Muddy Water. The partnership proved durable across the Generation IX VGC era; official 2026 EUIC discussion still described Tatsugiri switch-in mind games as a central part of playing against successful Dondozo teams. Mega Tatsugiri is now confirmed canon through Legends: Z-A's Mega Dimension DLC, with a 575 BST and significantly improved bulk and Special Attack, but it is new enough that its confirmed form mechanics should be separated from the long-established SV Commander history rather than given an invented multi-year competitive résumé.
nuzlocke: Tatsugiri has a useful Nuzlocke typing and strong special damage, but its physical frailty means it should be positioned carefully rather than treated as a general-purpose defensive Water-type. Dragon/Water leaves only Fairy and Dragon weaknesses and gives excellent Fire and Water resistance, while Storm Drain is the safest Ability when available because it converts Water attacks into complete immunities and adds a Special Attack boost. Nasty Plot can create a strong sweep in known matchups, but spending a turn setting up with only base 68 HP and 60 Defense exposes Tatsugiri to critical hits and strong neutral physical attacks. Dragon Pulse and Surf are reliable, perfectly accurate routine STAB options; Draco Meteor's 90% accuracy and sharp Special Attack drop make it better as a deliberate finishing blow than as the default attack, while Muddy Water's 85% accuracy introduces even more variance. Memento causes the user to faint and therefore directly conflicts with conventional Nuzlocke rules, while Mirror Coat is dangerous because it depends on correctly surviving and reflecting a special attack. Commander can be extraordinarily strong in Double Battles when the run also has Dondozo, but it temporarily removes Tatsugiri from direct control and locks Dondozo into the field, so the combination should still be planned around opposing Grass, Electric, Haze, Clear Smog, or other anti-setup tools. The later Mega Evolution belongs to Legends: Z-A rather than Scarlet/Violet and should be evaluated under that game's distinct battle system rather than projected into a standard SV Nuzlocke.

pokemon.name: Tatsugiri
pokemon.biologyAndBehavior: Curly Form Tatsugiri is orange with darker markings and normally holds its body in an upward-curled posture atop its white, rice-like throat sac. Like the species generally, it is extremely intelligent and survives by deceiving stronger animals, including feigning weakness so that prey approaches before Dondozo attacks on its command. It shelters inside Dondozo's mouth for protection, and Legends: Z-A adds that Tatsugiri will fight fiercely among themselves over the opportunity to partner with a particular Dondozo. Its coloration and posture are part of a broader set of form differences believed to have evolved to match the preferences of different prey.

pokemon.name: Tatsugiri
pokemon.biologyAndBehavior: Droopy Form Tatsugiri is primarily magenta and lies in a drooping posture across its inflated white throat sac. Its color and pattern belong to the prey-adapted variation seen across the species, and this form is specifically described as using deception such as playing dead to compensate for its small size and physical weakness. Legends: Z-A further establishes that the throat sac is an emergency survival organ: if Tatsugiri is swallowed by a predator, it can inflate the sac in an attempt to escape. When partnered with Dondozo in battle, Droopy Form causes Order Up to increase Dondozo's Defense.

pokemon.name: Tatsugiri
pokemon.biologyAndBehavior: Stretchy Form Tatsugiri is solid yellow and holds its body straight and horizontally rather than curling or drooping. Bird Pokémon are specifically identified as important prey, and Tatsugiri relies on a partner because it recognizes its own physical weakness. It can inflate its throat sac to camouflage itself, and Legends: Z-A emphasizes its unusually rational survival behavior: it assesses whether a confrontation can be won and flees quickly when it determines that victory is unlikely. When partnered with Dondozo in battle, Stretchy Form causes Order Up to increase Dondozo's Speed.

pokemon.name: Tatsugiri
pokemon.biologyAndBehavior: Mega Tatsugiri consists of three enlarged Tatsugiri—one of each ordinary form—riding on a pink-and-blue dish formed from Mega Evolution energy, with the original Curly Form occupying the center and wearing a roe-like crown while the other two are copies it created. Mega Evolution further stimulates Tatsugiri's already exceptional brain, making the Curly-centered form even more cunning and allowing it to create and command those copies directly. The three bodies have lengthened dorsal structures and are separated by colored spikes that can extend during attacks. The dish and copies are manifestations of Mega Evolution rather than an ordinary Tatsugiri social group.

pokemon.name: Tatsugiri
pokemon.biologyAndBehavior: When a Droopy Form Tatsugiri Mega Evolves, the resulting Mega Tatsugiri again presents one member of each form on an energy-created dish, but the original Droopy individual occupies the crowned central position and the other two are copies. This variant is specifically described as solidifying Mega Evolution energy into an overflowing supply of roe-like projectiles. Those projectiles can be launched at opponents and explode on contact, turning the species' sushi mimicry into a direct offensive mechanism. The form shares Mega Tatsugiri's enhanced intelligence, enlarged bodies, movable spikes, and energy-formed dish.

pokemon.name: Tatsugiri
pokemon.biologyAndBehavior: Mega Evolving a Stretchy Form Tatsugiri places the original Stretchy individual in the crowned central position of the three-Tatsugiri formation, with Curly and Droopy copies beside it. The Stretchy-centered Pokédex description emphasizes the energy-created dish itself: by riding on it, Mega Tatsugiri gains unrestricted mobility and can even travel through the air. Like the other Mega variants, the three bodies become longer, their dorsal fins become rows of three, and extendable colored spikes separate the central individual from its copies. Mega Evolution therefore removes one of ordinary Tatsugiri's obvious physical limitations by giving the species a mobile platform capable of free aerial movement.

playthrough: Great Tusk is a standalone Ground/Fighting Paradox Pokémon and a Scarlet exclusive, with Violet players normally needing trade or Union Circle access to obtain one. Unlike most ancient Paradox Pokémon, it can be obtained before the final Area Zero chapter: after the Quaking Earth Titan is defeated in Scarlet, the Former Titan Great Tusk can be challenged and caught in the Asado Desert, while additional specimens appear later in Area Zero. Its 115 HP, 131 Attack, and 131 Defense make it immediately exceptional against physical opponents, and Ground/Fighting STAB gives it enormous offensive reach through moves such as Earthquake or Headlong Rush and Close Combat. Rapid Spin provides useful hazard removal while also raising Speed, Ice Spinner covers Flying-types and Dragons that resist or avoid its Ground attacks, and Knock Off or Stealth Rock can add utility once their relevant move access is available. Protosynthesis boosts Great Tusk's highest stat in harsh sunlight or when activated by Booster Energy, normally strengthening Attack or another deliberately optimized stat; because its Attack and Defense are both extremely high, Nature, IV, and EV differences can affect which stat receives the boost. Its major weakness is special durability: base 53 Special Defense is extremely poor, and Water, Grass, Ice, Flying, Psychic, and Fairy attacks can exploit that weakness despite its huge physical bulk. Headlong Rush and Close Combat are both perfectly accurate and extremely powerful but lower Great Tusk's defenses after use, so Earthquake and other less self-punishing attacks can be preferable when repeated fighting is expected. Adamant emphasizes its extraordinary physical damage, Jolly improves the middling base 87 Speed, and Impish can suit a more defensive physical role.
competitive: Great Tusk has been one of the defining Pokémon of Scarlet/Violet singles from the beginning of Generation IX and remains classified as OU in Smogon's current SV Pokédex. Its exceptional role compression is the core of that success: 115/131 physical bulk, base 131 Attack, Ground/Fighting STAB, Rapid Spin, Stealth Rock, Knock Off, and broad coverage allow one team slot to provide hazard removal, hazard setting, item disruption, physical checking, and real offensive pressure. Headlong Rush is often preferred for maximum Ground damage, while Ice Spinner pressures Flying- and Ground-immune checks and Rapid Spin's Speed increase can turn a utility action into late-game offensive momentum. Defensive sets use its immense physical bulk to check threats such as Kingambit and other physical attackers, while Booster Energy and Bulk Up variants exploit Protosynthesis to become dangerous sweepers rather than merely support Pokémon. Its poor base 53 Special Defense is the fundamental balancing flaw: strong special Water, Grass, Ice, Psychic, Fairy, or Flying attacks can force it out or KO it even when physical attackers struggle to make progress. Great Tusk was also immediately successful in early official VGC; for example, it appeared on the Masters Division champion teams at both the 2023 Perth and Vancouver Regionals, commonly using direct physical offense rather than its singles hazard-control identity. That distinction matters historically: Great Tusk's long-term singles reputation is as premier role compression, whereas doubles has generally valued its raw physical stats, Protosynthesis, spread or single-target Ground pressure, and offensive matchup control.
nuzlocke: Great Tusk can be an outstanding Scarlet Nuzlocke encounter because the static Former Titan can provide access before Area Zero if the ruleset permits static encounters, and the species arrives fully developed with no evolution requirement. Its 115 HP and 131 Defense make physical damage unusually predictable, while an Electric immunity and strong resistance to Rock plus resistances to Bug, Dark, and Poison create several useful switch opportunities. The danger is that its base 53 Special Defense provides very little protection from unexpected special coverage, and six ordinary weaknesses mean a Water, Grass, Ice, Flying, Psychic, or Fairy move can punish an otherwise safe-looking matchup. Earthquake is often safer than Headlong Rush because it preserves both defenses after attacking, and Close Combat should similarly be reserved for situations where its defensive drops will not expose Great Tusk on the following turn. Rapid Spin is unusually good Nuzlocke utility because it removes damaging hazards without sacrificing a teammate and simultaneously raises Speed, reducing future exposure if Great Tusk stays in. Bulk Up can make known physical matchups nearly one-sided, but setup does nothing to repair the Special Defense weakness and should not be attempted blindly against mixed attackers. If the player respects special coverage instead of treating its enormous Defense as universal bulk, Great Tusk is one of Paldea's strongest and most reliable physical Pokémon.

pokemon.name: Great Tusk
pokemon.biologyAndBehavior: Great Tusk is a massive proboscidean Paradox Pokémon with enormous inward-curving tusks, armored dark plates, serrated ears, spikes, and patches of reddish fur. It is explicitly savage and aggressive: the Scarlet Book records a Great Tusk attacking the Area Zero expedition with its body and tusks and fatally injuring one of the explorers, while later Occulture material describes the species as a mysterious Donphan-like life-form with gigantic tusks and tough scales. Its tusks usually prevent the compact rolling behavior associated with Donphan, although Pokémon Horizons has shown a Great Tusk curling up while using Rollout. Its true origin remains unresolved; AI Sada describes the ancient Paradox Pokémon as ancestors brought through her time machine, whereas the Professor encountered at the Crystal Pool describes such Pokémon as counterparts from another timeline, and Great Tusk was recorded by Heath's expedition roughly two centuries before Sada's machine was built.

playthrough: Scream Tail is a standalone Fairy/Psychic Paradox Pokémon found naturally only in Scarlet's Area Zero, placing normal access very late in the main story; Violet players need trade, event, or Union Circle access. Its 570 BST is distributed very differently from most offensive Paradox Pokémon: 115 HP, 99 Defense, 115 Special Defense, and 111 Speed make it both bulky and unusually fast, while its Attack and Special Attack are only 65 each. That stat line makes Scream Tail far better as a support Pokémon or gradual setup user than as an immediate attacker, with Wish, Protect, Encore, Thunder Wave, Stealth Rock, screens, and Calm Mind among the tools that can exploit the turns its bulk creates. Fairy/Psychic provides a Dragon immunity, a 4× resistance to Fighting, and a Psychic resistance while leaving only Ghost, Poison, and Steel weaknesses, so it can enter many predictable attacks safely. Protosynthesis can strengthen its highest stat in sun or through Booster Energy; because base Speed is already 111, Speed-focused builds can become extremely difficult for ordinary opponents to outrun. Its biggest playthrough drawback is low immediate damage: even STAB Psychic and Fairy moves can feel modest without Calm Mind, and extending fights gives opponents more opportunities to land critical hits or status. Timid is useful for maximizing its natural Speed, while Bold or Calm can emphasize its already excellent physical or special durability and suit a support-focused role.
competitive: Scream Tail currently sits in SV NU, where its combination of 115/99/115 bulk, base 111 Speed, Fairy/Psychic typing, and an unusually deep support movepool gives it several viable identities despite base 65 offenses. Utility sets use Wish and Protect for recovery, Encore to trap setup or passive moves, Thunder Wave for speed control, and sometimes Stealth Rock, allowing Scream Tail to support teammates while remaining faster than many offensive Pokémon it is checking. Calm Mind sets take a different approach: Scream Tail's natural bulk can make repeated boosting difficult to stop, and Booster Energy can supply a Speed increase, but its low starting Special Attack means it usually needs more setup than conventional sweepers before it becomes threatening. Later-generation move access such as Psychic Noise gives some current sets a way to block opposing recovery, while Dazzling Gleam prevents Dark-types from freely exploiting Psychic coverage. Its weaknesses are just as structural as its strengths: low offensive stats can make it passive, Steel-types resist its Fairy STAB and threaten it directly, and repeatedly using Wish or other support moves can surrender momentum to stronger wallbreakers. Scream Tail also saw meaningful early VGC experimentation rather than being only a singles curiosity; a Scream Tail appeared on the runner-up Masters team at the 2023 Perth Regional, where its combination of speed, bulk, support options, and Protosynthesis gave it a niche alongside more obviously offensive Paradox Pokémon. Its current NU status therefore reflects lower singles usage and modest immediate damage, not a lack of functional competitive tools.
nuzlocke: Scream Tail's unusually high Speed and mixed bulk make it one of the safer Paradox Pokémon for a Nuzlocke, although its Area Zero availability means that value arrives only during the final portion of Scarlet and the postgame unless the player obtains one through another legal method. Fairy/Psychic gives only three weaknesses and provides a Dragon immunity plus a 4× Fighting resistance, so known movesets can create extremely comfortable switch-ins. Wish is especially valuable under permadeath rules because Scream Tail's high HP can heal itself or pass substantial recovery to teammates, although the one-turn delay must be planned around rather than treated like immediate recovery. Encore can turn a predictable setup, recovery, or status move into a safe opportunity for the team, while Reflect and Light Screen can reduce incoming damage for several turns and improve survival margins beyond Scream Tail itself. Thunder Wave is useful but only 90% accurate in modern games, so it should not be treated as guaranteed emergency speed control when failure would cause a death. Calm Mind can produce safe sweeps against known special attackers, yet Scream Tail's low offensive stats often require multiple setup turns and therefore expose it to critical hits or disruptive status for longer than faster-killing sweepers. Its durability, speed, and non-damaging utility make it excellent for controlled battles, but a Nuzlocke player should avoid allowing its low damage output to turn simple encounters into unnecessarily long exchanges.

pokemon.name: Scream Tail
pokemon.biologyAndBehavior: Scream Tail is a round, pink Paradox Pokémon resembling Jigglypuff but possessing fangs, a long curled head tuft resembling a second tail, and the ability to levitate rather than walk. Occulture describes it as ferociously aggressive and prone to attacking anyone who approaches, a sharp behavioral contrast with the soothing-singing image of modern Jigglypuff; Pokémon Horizons likewise depicts Scream Tail as a poor singer whose performance becomes a loud scream. A sensational magazine theory claims it could be a Jigglypuff from one billion years ago, but this is presented as speculation rather than established biology. As with the other ancient Paradox Pokémon, its actual origin is deliberately uncertain: AI Sada calls it an ancestor from the ancient past, while the Crystal Pool Professor describes it as a Jigglypuff counterpart from another timeline.

playthrough: Brute Bonnet is a standalone Grass/Dark Paradox Pokémon available naturally in Scarlet's Area Zero near the end of the main story, while Violet normally requires trade or Union Circle access. Its stat distribution favors slow physical pressure and durability: 111 HP, 127 Attack, 99 Defense, and 99 Special Defense make it difficult to remove with neutral damage, but base 55 Speed means it will often take a hit before acting. Spore is the defining playthrough tool because its perfect base accuracy gives Brute Bonnet a highly reliable way to put susceptible targets to sleep, creating safe turns for attacking, switching, healing, or setting up; Grass-types, Overcoat users, and Safety Goggles still ignore powder moves. Seed Bomb and Crunch provide dependable physical STAB, Sucker Punch compensates for its low Speed with priority, and Close Combat can cover opposing Steel- and Dark-types at the cost of lowering both defenses. Synthesis gives it direct recovery, with the amount depending on weather, while Protosynthesis can further enhance its highest stat in harsh sunlight or through Booster Energy. Its type chart is the major drawback: Grass/Dark has weaknesses to Fire, Ice, Fighting, Flying, Poison, Fairy, and a devastating 4× weakness to Bug, so the high raw bulk does not make it safe against unknown coverage. Adamant is excellent for maximizing its physical pressure, while Impish or Careful can exploit its strong natural bulk when Spore and support are more important than damage.
competitive: Brute Bonnet currently resides in SV ZU, but that usage tier understates the specialized roles it has occupied in both singles and official doubles. In singles it combines base 127 Attack with Spore, Sucker Punch, Crunch, Seed Bomb, and coverage such as Close Combat, allowing it to disable an answer and then apply meaningful physical pressure rather than functioning as a purely passive mushroom. Smogon's PU analysis has treated it as a specialized offensive wallbreaker even while its current usage tier is ZU, illustrating the difference between usage placement and matchup-specific viability. The main obstacles are severe: base 55 Speed forces heavy dependence on Sucker Punch or absorbing a hit, the 4× Bug weakness can be exploited by U-turn, and six additional ordinary weaknesses make defensive positioning far less forgiving than its 111/99/99 bulk initially suggests. Its doubles niche is considerably clearer because Spore and Rage Powder combine disruption with redirection, while Sucker Punch keeps it from becoming totally passive and Pollen Puff can heal an ally; Smogon continued to document this bulky-support role as late as VGC 2025 Regulation I. Sun teams can activate Protosynthesis without consuming Booster Energy, and defensive Terastallization has historically been valuable for removing several of Grass/Dark's dangerous weaknesses. Brute Bonnet never replaced Amoonguss as the universal mushroom support Pokémon, but its stronger physical offense, Dark typing, Sucker Punch, and Protosynthesis created a distinct competitive niche rather than making it simply an ancient reskin.
nuzlocke: Brute Bonnet can be exceptionally useful in a late-game Scarlet Nuzlocke because 100%-accurate Spore gives the player direct control over many dangerous encounters without depending on a damage roll or an inaccurate sleep move. Its 111/99/99 bulk is genuinely strong and Synthesis provides renewable healing, while Sucker Punch offers priority that compensates for its low base 55 Speed when a weakened attacker must be removed before it moves. The danger is its unusually poor weakness profile: Grass/Dark is weak to Fire, Ice, Fighting, Flying, Poison, and Fairy and takes 4× damage from Bug, so an unexpected U-turn or other Bug coverage can overwhelm even its high HP. Spore also has clear exceptions—Grass-types, Overcoat, Safety Goggles, and other sleep-prevention effects can invalidate it—so relying on the move without checking the matchup can create a false sense of security. Close Combat is powerful but lowers both defenses and can make the next turn dangerous; Seed Bomb, Crunch, or another perfectly accurate attack is often the safer choice when it already secures the knockout. Synthesis becomes less reliable under unfavorable weather, and relying on Sucker Punch introduces prediction risk because it fails when the opponent does not choose an attacking move. When its many weaknesses are known and avoided, Brute Bonnet's combination of bulk, reliable sleep, recovery, and priority gives it a strong survival-oriented toolkit.

pokemon.name: Brute Bonnet
pokemon.biologyAndBehavior: Brute Bonnet is a large mushroom-like Paradox Pokémon combining the basic body plan of Amoonguss with dinosaur-like features, including a tail, four sturdy legs, spikes, and apparent moss beneath its main cap. The caps on its head and arms still resemble modern Poké Balls despite the creature's supposed antiquity, one of several deliberately puzzling details surrounding Paradox Pokémon. Occulture characterizes Brute Bonnet as gigantic, savage, powerful, and seemingly low in intelligence rather than describing the deceptive ambush behavior associated with modern Amoonguss. The game does not resolve whether it is literally Amoonguss's ancestor: AI Sada describes the ancient Paradox species as coming from the distant past, while the Professor encountered at the Crystal Pool instead calls them counterparts from another timeline, leaving Brute Bonnet's biological origin uncertain.

playthrough: Flutter Mane is a standalone Ghost/Fairy Paradox Pokémon found naturally in Scarlet's Area Zero, so it normally joins the team only during the final chapter of the main story; Violet players require trade, event, or Union Circle access. Its stat distribution is extraordinarily specialized: base 135 Special Attack, Special Defense, and Speed make it both an elite special attacker and very difficult for ordinary special moves to KO, but its 55 HP and 55 Defense leave it extremely vulnerable to physical damage. Ghost/Fairy is an exceptional offensive and defensive combination, providing immunities to Normal, Fighting, and Dragon and leaving only Ghost and Steel as ordinary weaknesses, while Moonblast and Shadow Ball give two strong, perfectly accurate STAB attacks with excellent combined coverage. Coverage and utility such as Mystical Fire, Power Gem, Thunderbolt, Psyshock, Calm Mind, Taunt, or Icy Wind can address specific matchups without requiring Flutter Mane to abandon its primary role as a fast special attacker. Protosynthesis becomes especially potent because both Special Attack and Speed are already enormous; depending on the actual stat spread, harsh sunlight or Booster Energy can enhance either damage or Speed beyond an already elite baseline. Terastallization can increase Fairy or Ghost damage or escape a dangerous Steel/Ghost matchup, but Flutter Mane is strong enough that it rarely needs Tera merely to function in ordinary story battles. Timid maximizes the Speed advantage and is the safest broadly useful Nature, while Modest produces even greater immediate damage when the existing base 135 Speed is already sufficient.
competitive: Flutter Mane was one of the most immediately dominant new Pokémon of Generation IX: the SV OU council unanimously quickbanned it on November 20, 2022, only two days after Scarlet and Violet released, and it remains classified as Uber in Smogon's current SV Pokédex. The problem was the convergence of base 135 Special Attack, base 135 Speed, Ghost/Fairy STAB, broad special coverage, Protosynthesis, Booster Energy, and Terastallization, which made conventional offensive checks difficult to keep ahead of it and defensive answers vulnerable to different coverage or Tera choices. In Ubers it remains a dangerous wallbreaker and revenge killer through sets such as Choice Specs Moonblast and Shadow Ball, but the much higher power level, physical priority, entry-hazard pressure, and specially bulky Pokémon prevent it from dominating that tier as completely as it overwhelmed early OU. Official VGC tells an even larger story because Flutter Mane remained legal there and became one of the signature Pokémon of the entire Scarlet/Violet competitive era, using Choice Specs, Booster Energy, Focus Sash, Fairy-boosting items, Icy Wind, Taunt, Thunder Wave, and many different Tera types depending on the format. It appeared on Alex Gómez Berna's 2023 North America International Championship-winning Masters team and continued adapting for years; official 2026 EUIC analysis discussed unusually bulky Thunder Wave Flutter Mane sets capable of surviving attacks that frailer early-generation builds would not attempt to take. The Pokémon Company's 2026 retrospective on the Terastallization era explicitly identified Flutter Mane alongside Incineroar as an MVP Pokémon, an unusually strong official acknowledgment of how central it became to VGC. Its competitive history therefore differs sharply by ruleset: too strong for standard SV OU almost immediately, but a legal and format-defining piece of multiple generations of Scarlet/Violet VGC strategy.
nuzlocke: Flutter Mane is an extraordinary late-game Nuzlocke attacker because base 135 Speed allows it to move first against most opponents and base 135 Special Attack frequently ends battles before retaliation is possible. Ghost/Fairy contributes major safety through complete immunities to Normal, Fighting, and Dragon, and Moonblast plus Shadow Ball are both perfectly accurate STAB attacks, reducing the miss variance that often makes high-powered sweepers risky. Its base 135 Special Defense is also excellent, but the combination of only base 55 HP and 55 Defense means physical attacks—especially physical priority or super-effective Ghost and Steel moves—can KO it far more easily than its overall 570 BST suggests. Calm Mind is useful against known special attackers because it raises both Special Attack and Special Defense, but it does nothing for Flutter Mane's physical weakness and should not be used as though it makes the Pokémon universally bulky. Protosynthesis can create even safer sweeps by boosting Speed or Special Attack under sun or with Booster Energy, although Booster Energy is a consumable resource during ordinary game play and should not be assumed to be available for every fight. Moves such as Mystical Fire can lower an opponent's Special Attack and Taunt can shut down dangerous status or setup, providing survival value beyond raw offense. If the player keeps it away from strong physical attackers rather than using its high Special Defense as evidence of general durability, Flutter Mane is one of the safest and most powerful late-game offensive Pokémon available in Scarlet.

pokemon.name: Flutter Mane
pokemon.biologyAndBehavior: Flutter Mane is a limbless, ghost-like Paradox Pokémon resembling an enlarged Misdreavus, with red gems around its neck, horn-like red spikes on its head, and long hair that resembles feathered arms. It is reported to float through the night sky while its long hair writhes around it, and eyewitness accounts describe it as markedly fierce and aggressive. Occulture sensationally proposes that it may be the ghost of a pterosaur from a long-lost era, but the game presents that explanation as rumor rather than established fact. Its relationship to Misdreavus is likewise unresolved: AI Sada calls it an ancient ancestor, while the Crystal Pool Professor describes it as a Misdreavus counterpart from another timeline, and the Scarlet Book records a matching creature long before Sada's time machine was constructed.

playthrough: Slither Wing is a standalone Bug/Fighting Paradox Pokémon found naturally in Scarlet's Area Zero near the end of the story, while Violet normally requires trade, event, or Union Circle access. Its base 135 Attack and 105 Special Defense make it a powerful physical attacker that can also absorb special hits better than its appearance suggests, though base 81 Speed means it is not naturally fast enough to sweep every opponent without support. First Impression is one of its most important tools: the 90-base-power Bug attack has +2 priority and works only on the user's first turn after entering battle, making it excellent for immediate damage or revenge killing without relying on Slither Wing's middling Speed. Close Combat is an extremely strong Fighting STAB but lowers both defenses, U-turn allows Slither Wing to attack while repositioning, and Morning Sun supplies direct weather-dependent recovery; Bulk Up and Flame Charge can instead build toward a sweep. Bug/Fighting grants useful resistances to Bug, Dark, Fighting, Grass, and Ground, but it is weak to Fairy, Fire, and Psychic and has a severe 4× weakness to Flying. Protosynthesis can strengthen its highest stat through harsh sunlight or Booster Energy, naturally favoring its enormous Attack unless the stat spread is deliberately manipulated. Adamant maximizes First Impression and general physical damage, Jolly improves its borderline Speed, and Impish can support a defensive pivot role that uses Will-O-Wisp and Morning Sun.
competitive: Slither Wing currently sits in SV UU and has developed a much broader competitive identity than a simple physical Volcarona counterpart. Base 135 Attack, STAB First Impression, Close Combat, and U-turn make it an effective offensive pivot and revenge killer, since First Impression's +2 priority lets it threaten fast offensive Pokémon immediately when it enters the field. Booster Energy hyper-offense sets can use Bulk Up and Flame Charge to accumulate power and Speed, while sun support activates Protosynthesis without consuming the item slot and strengthens the broader archetype around it. Slither Wing has also demonstrated a specific OU niche: Assault Vest variants use base 105 Special Defense and useful resistances to pivot into special attackers before threatening them with First Impression or maintaining momentum through U-turn. Defensive sets can instead use Heavy-Duty Boots, Morning Sun, Will-O-Wisp, and U-turn to exploit resistances to attacks from Pokémon such as Great Tusk, Kingambit, Rillaboom, and other physical or special threats it matches well into. The obvious checks keep it from being a universal top-tier choice: base 81 Speed is awkward without priority or boosting, its physical Defense is merely adequate, and the 4× Flying weakness makes many Flying attacks catastrophically dangerous. Its stable UU placement reflects a Pokémon with real offensive and defensive niches whose typing and priority can be excellent in the right matchup but whose weaknesses prevent it from compressing roles as universally as Great Tusk.
nuzlocke: Slither Wing's best Nuzlocke traits are immediate physical power, strong special bulk, priority, pivoting, and access to recovery, all of which reduce the number of turns it must remain exposed to an opponent. First Impression is especially valuable because its +2 priority and perfect accuracy can remove a dangerous target immediately after Slither Wing enters, while U-turn allows it to deal damage and escape an unfavorable matchup in one action. Morning Sun provides repeatable recovery, although the amount restored varies with weather, and its interaction with harsh sunlight is particularly convenient on a Pokémon whose Protosynthesis also benefits from sun. Close Combat should be used more cautiously than in ordinary competitive play because the Defense and Special Defense drops can turn a safe initial knockout into a dangerous following turn; Drain Punch or other weaker options can be preferable when they accomplish the same goal more safely. The 4× Flying weakness is the largest survival hazard and can overwhelm even Slither Wing's respectable HP and Special Defense, so unknown opponents capable of carrying Acrobatics, Brave Bird, Air Slash, or other Flying coverage should be treated very conservatively. Bulk Up can make known physical matchups safer while increasing damage, but critical hits and special coverage still bypass the sense of security created by Defense boosts. With disciplined switching, First Impression, U-turn, and Morning Sun make Slither Wing unusually good at controlling its exposure rather than simply trading damage.

pokemon.name: Slither Wing
pokemon.biologyAndBehavior: Slither Wing is a huge, shaggy moth-like Paradox Pokémon with four walking legs, a long abdomen, compound eyes, horn-like facial structures, and six brightly colored leaf-shaped wings. Those wings do not appear strong enough for flight, so it normally travels as a quadruped, although it can rear onto two legs during battle. Only a small number of sightings are reported in Occulture, which speculates that the creature could be a prehistoric Volcarona revived from fossils even though no Volcarona fossils from the proposed era have ever been found. Scarlet/Violet provides a competing explanation rather than confirming that story: AI Sada describes Slither Wing as an ancestor of Volcarona, while the Crystal Pool Professor calls it a Volcarona counterpart from another timeline, leaving its true origin unresolved.

playthrough: Sandy Shocks is a standalone Electric/Ground Paradox Pokémon found naturally only in Pokémon Scarlet's Area Zero, so it normally becomes available during the final portion of the story; Violet players need trade, event, or Union Circle access. Its base 121 Special Attack and 101 Speed make it a strong immediate special attacker, while Electric/Ground STAB is particularly useful because Thunderbolt and Earth Power provide two powerful, perfectly accurate attacks with very different defensive answers. Volt Switch lets Sandy Shocks attack while repositioning, and Stealth Rock or Spikes can add team utility when the player wants more than direct damage; Power Gem and Flash Cannon offer additional special coverage. Protosynthesis raises its highest stat in harsh sunlight or when Booster Energy activates, with Speed receiving a 50% increase instead of the 30% increase applied to other stats, so actual stat distribution determines whether Sandy Shocks becomes faster or stronger. Electric/Ground grants an Electric immunity and resistances to Flying, Poison, Rock, and Steel, but weaknesses to Water, Grass, Ice, and Ground are all common enough to punish careless switching. Its 85/97/85 bulk is respectable rather than exceptional and it lacks easy conventional recovery, so its safest story role is generally fast special offense and pivoting rather than repeated defensive switching. Timid can push its Speed high enough to make Speed-focused Protosynthesis sets especially fast, while Modest maximizes its already strong Special Attack.
competitive: Sandy Shocks currently sits in SV UU and has established itself as a useful fast special attacker, entry-hazard setter, and pivot rather than a one-dimensional sun sweeper. Its Electric/Ground STAB combination is difficult to switch into cleanly, with Thunderbolt pressuring Flying- and Water-types while Earth Power punishes many Grounded Electric resists and Steel-types, and base 101 Speed places it above a large portion of slower wallbreakers. Stealth Rock and Spikes give it hazard-setting utility, while Volt Switch can preserve momentum against opponents it forces out; this combination lets Sandy Shocks make progress even when it cannot immediately break a defensive answer. Booster Energy or sun can activate Protosynthesis, and Speed-boosting variants can become effective cleaners or fast support Pokémon while Special Attack-boosting variants emphasize immediate damage. Its limitations keep it below OU: four common weaknesses, no reliable recovery, only moderate bulk, and competition from faster or stronger Electric- and Ground-types make it difficult to fit on every team. Sandy Shocks nevertheless had documented official doubles use early in Generation IX; for example, it appeared on the 2023 Charlotte Regional Senior Division championship team alongside Iron Bundle, showing that its Speed, typing, and support options could translate beyond singles. Its current UU placement therefore represents a real competitive niche based on offensive typing and role compression rather than merely novelty as a Paradox Magneton.
nuzlocke: Sandy Shocks is a strong late-game Scarlet Nuzlocke attacker because Thunderbolt and Earth Power are both perfectly accurate, powerful special STAB moves and base 101 Speed frequently lets it attack before the opponent. Its Electric immunity creates useful switch opportunities, while resistances to Flying, Poison, Rock, and Steel can make known physical or special matchups comparatively safe. Volt Switch is especially valuable under permadeath rules because it deals damage while moving Sandy Shocks out of danger, allowing the player to preserve favorable positioning instead of leaving it exposed. Stealth Rock and Spikes can generate safe team-wide value against boss battles with repeated switches, but spending turns setting hazards is unnecessary when an opponent can threaten one of Sandy Shocks's Water, Grass, Ice, or Ground weaknesses. Its bulk is adequate but not strong enough to absorb repeated super-effective hits, and the absence of dependable instant recovery means damage accumulation matters across long routes or sequential battles. Protosynthesis can improve either offense or Speed and may create safer knockouts, but Booster Energy is a consumable resource in ordinary gameplay rather than something that should be assumed for every encounter. Timid is usually the safer Nuzlocke Nature because moving first reduces exposure, while Modest is worthwhile when the additional damage changes important knockout ranges.

pokemon.name: Sandy Shocks
pokemon.biologyAndBehavior: Sandy Shocks is composed of three Magneton-like metallic units covered partly in iron filings, with the upper unit bearing markings reminiscent of war paint and the lower magnets elongated into leg-like structures. Unlike modern Magneton, it does not normally float; it walks by bending those elongated magnets, while a group of screws coated in iron filings floats behind it like a tail. Reports describe Sandy Shocks as aggressive, with some observers claiming to have been attacked in Paldea's arid regions. Its origin is intentionally unresolved: AI Sada calls it an ancient ancestor of Magneton, whereas the Professor encountered at the Crystal Pool describes it as a Magneton counterpart from another timeline, and Heath recorded the creature roughly 200 years before Sada's time machine was built.

playthrough: Iron Treads is a standalone Ground/Steel Paradox Pokémon and a Violet exclusive, but unlike most future Paradox species it can be caught before the final Area Zero chapter: after defeating the Quaking Earth Titan, the Former Titan Iron Treads can later be challenged in the Asado Desert. Its base 120 Defense, 112 Attack, and unusually high 106 Speed create an excellent combination of physical durability and offensive tempo, while Ground/Steel supplies Electric and Poison immunities plus numerous resistances. Earthquake and Iron Head are dependable, perfectly accurate physical STAB attacks, and Rapid Spin removes entry hazards while increasing Speed; Knock Off also becomes available naturally at level 42 and strips held items while dealing useful Dark coverage. Quark Drive boosts its highest stat under Electric Terrain or after Booster Energy activates, and carefully built competitive-style sets can deliberately make Speed the boosted stat despite Iron Treads's naturally higher Attack and Defense. Its defensive weakness is special damage: base 70 Special Defense is much less impressive than its physical side, and Fighting, Fire, Ground, and Water attacks are all super effective. The Indigo Disk move pool adds options such as Supercell Slam and High Horsepower, but ordinary story sets rarely need riskier coverage when Earthquake, Iron Head, Rapid Spin, and utility already cover most situations. Jolly is particularly valuable because it reinforces Iron Treads's unusual speed for a Steel-type, while Adamant improves damage and Careful can help compensate for weaker special bulk.
competitive: Iron Treads currently occupies SV OU, where its value comes from exceptional role compression rather than overwhelming raw damage. Ground/Steel typing, base 106 Speed, 120 Defense, Stealth Rock, Rapid Spin, Knock Off, and strong Ground STAB allow it to set hazards, remove opposing hazards, disrupt items, and check important threats within a single team slot. Modern OU sets can use Booster Energy to trigger a Speed-boosting Quark Drive, letting Iron Treads function as a fast lead or cleaner, while bulkier sets invest heavily in Special Defense to compensate for the weakest part of its defensive profile. Physical Earthquake sets pressure Electric-types such as Raging Bolt, while current analyses also document special variants using Earth Power or Steel Beam for specific targets, demonstrating that its competitive identity is more flexible than its base 72 Special Attack would suggest. Air Balloon or defensive Terastallization can temporarily remove the Ground weakness, and Tera Ghost has utility for blocking Rapid Spin or avoiding Fighting attacks, but using Tera defensively carries the normal opportunity cost. Iron Treads is not a dominant wallbreaker: base 112 Attack is merely good by OU standards, it lacks a strong conventional Attack-boosting move, and strong special Water, Fire, or Fighting attackers can force it out. Its persistent OU value instead comes from being one of the few Pokémon capable of combining fast hazard control, Stealth Rock, Knock Off, useful immunities, and respectable offense without becoming passive.
nuzlocke: Iron Treads is one of Violet's better physical Nuzlocke encounters because the Former Titan can be caught before Area Zero if static encounters are permitted, avoiding the extreme late-game availability of most future Paradox Pokémon. Base 120 Defense and Ground/Steel's many resistances make physical damage relatively predictable, while complete Electric and Poison immunities can create extremely safe switches against known moves. Rapid Spin is valuable because it removes entry hazards without sacrificing a teammate and raises Speed at the same time, while Earthquake, Iron Head, and Knock Off are all perfectly accurate and avoid unnecessary miss variance. Its main danger is the discrepancy between its defenses: base 70 Special Defense means a strong special Fire, Water, Fighting, or Ground attack can inflict much more damage than its heavy armor suggests. High Horsepower is slightly weaker and only 95% accurate compared with Earthquake, while Supercell Slam is particularly dangerous in a Nuzlocke because a miss or immunity can cost half of Iron Treads's maximum HP; neither is usually worth replacing a safer move unless a specific matchup demands it. Quark Drive can improve Speed or another key stat, but players should not depend on Booster Energy as permanent safety insurance during an ordinary run. Used as a fast physical tank and utility Pokémon rather than as a special wall, Iron Treads offers an excellent combination of survivability and controlled damage.

pokemon.name: Iron Treads
pokemon.biologyAndBehavior: Iron Treads is a metallic, Donphan-like quadruped dominated by a segmented tread that runs from its back over its head, allowing the body to curl into a wheel and rotate at high speed. It is described as cruel and dangerous; the Violet Book records one fatally injuring a member of the Area Zero expedition, and the trails left behind after it moves have been compared to scorched earth. Pokécology material explains that its tire-like armor enables the rotating movement, and sleeping Iron Treads curl into wheel form, rock back and forth, and power down so the red energy on their tread goes dark. Its true origin remains uncertain: AI Turo calls it a future descendant of Donphan, whereas the Crystal Pool Professor describes it as a Donphan counterpart from another timeline; Heath encountered it around two centuries before Turo's time machine existed.

playthrough: Iron Bundle is a standalone Ice/Water Paradox Pokémon found naturally only in Violet's Area Zero, making it a late-game encounter; Scarlet players normally need trade, an event, or Union Circle access. Its defining strengths are base 136 Speed and 124 Special Attack, which let it outspeed nearly every ordinary story opponent and immediately threaten them with special damage. Freeze-Dry is especially valuable because it is perfectly accurate and hits Water-types super effectively despite being an Ice move, while Ice Beam offers stronger reliable Ice damage and Hydro Pump provides enormous Water power at the cost of only 80% accuracy. Flip Turn gives Iron Bundle a perfectly accurate way to attack and retreat, although its base 80 Attack means the move is more about positioning than damage. Quark Drive commonly makes its already extreme Speed even higher with Booster Energy or Electric Terrain when Speed is its highest actual stat, while offensive builds can also manipulate the stat distribution toward Special Attack. Iron Bundle's base 114 Defense is surprisingly high, but 56 HP and 60 Special Defense leave it fragile overall against special attacks, and Electric, Fighting, Grass, and Rock weaknesses punish reckless switching. Timid is the standard way to exploit its extraordinary Speed, while Modest is reasonable in ordinary play when additional damage matters more than outrunning an already slower opponent pool.
competitive: Iron Bundle was immediately recognized as too powerful for standard Scarlet/Violet OU and was quickbanned on November 25, 2022, only one week after the games released; it remains classified as Uber. Its core offensive problem for OU was the combination of base 136 Speed, 124 Special Attack, Hydro Pump, and Freeze-Dry: Water plus Freeze-Dry has essentially unresisted type coverage, forcing many would-be Water checks to fear the Ice move instead. Choice Specs can turn that coverage into devastating wallbreaking, Booster Energy can push Speed beyond even many Choice Scarf or boosted threats, and Flip Turn lets Iron Bundle escape bad matchups rather than surrender momentum. In Ubers the environment is powerful enough to keep it under greater control, since its 56 HP and 60 Special Defense make safe entry difficult and paralysis or strong priority can ruin its Speed-based game plan, but it still functions as an elite revenge killer and speed-control attacker. Iron Bundle also became an important early VGC Pokémon: Booster Energy and Icy Wind allowed it to provide extremely fast speed control, while Freeze-Dry, Hydro Pump, Encore, and Protect gave it offensive and disruptive flexibility. That impact was immediately visible in official competition, including a place on Taran Birdee's 2023 Perth Regional Masters championship team. Its competitive history therefore combines an almost immediate singles ban with a substantial legal doubles career built around speed control and difficult-to-resist special coverage.
nuzlocke: Iron Bundle is a devastating late-game Nuzlocke attacker because base 136 Speed minimizes the number of turns opponents get to act and Freeze-Dry plus Ice Beam supply perfectly accurate offensive options from base 124 Special Attack. Freeze-Dry is particularly safe against Water-types because it converts what would normally resist Ice into a super-effective target without relying on prediction or an inaccurate coverage move. Hydro Pump is much riskier despite its 110 base power because 80% accuracy creates a one-in-five miss chance before other modifiers, so a lower-powered accurate Water option is preferable whenever it still guarantees the knockout. Flip Turn is excellent positioning utility because it can move Iron Bundle out before the opponent acts, but the player's calculations must account for Iron Bundle's relatively weak physical Attack. Its base 114 Defense can survive some physical hits, yet 56 HP and 60 Special Defense mean the Pokémon should never be treated as generally bulky; strong special attacks and Electric, Fighting, Grass, or Rock coverage remain dangerous. Booster Energy Speed can make already favorable matchups nearly foolproof, but a consumable item should not substitute for checking priority attacks or opposing Choice Scarf users. Timid maximizes the core survival strategy of moving first, while Modest can be justified when raw damage produces cleaner one-hit knockouts.

pokemon.name: Iron Bundle
pokemon.biologyAndBehavior: Iron Bundle is a robotic bird resembling Delibird, with a metallic ring around its neck concealing an extendable wire that allows its head to stretch far from the body and a cable physically connecting its bundle-like apparatus. It moves across snow by using its feet like skis and is reported to fire enormous blasts of ice from the spherical apparatus to propel itself through snowy terrain. When Iron Bundle sleeps, it powers down: the blue energy on its belly and bundle turns black. Only a tiny number of sightings were historically reported, and its origin is unresolved—AI Turo describes it as a future descendant of Delibird, while the Crystal Pool Professor calls it a counterpart from another timeline; Heath nevertheless recorded it about 200 years before Turo's time machine was built.

playthrough: Iron Hands is a standalone Fighting/Electric Paradox Pokémon found naturally only in Violet's Area Zero, so it is normally a late-story acquisition; Scarlet players require trade, event, or Union Circle access. Its extraordinary 154 HP, 140 Attack, and 108 Defense make it one of Paldea's most physically imposing non-legendary Pokémon, while base 50 Speed strongly favors absorbing a hit and striking back rather than attempting to move first. Drain Punch is particularly effective in ordinary play because it is perfectly accurate, receives STAB, and restores half the damage dealt, allowing Iron Hands's enormous HP pool to be replenished while attacking; Thunder Punch provides a similarly safe Electric STAB option. Wild Charge offers more immediate Electric power but inflicts recoil, while the Indigo Disk TM Supercell Slam reaches 100 base power but is only 95% accurate and can cost half of Iron Hands's maximum HP when it fails, making both moves meaningfully riskier than Thunder Punch. Fake Out provides first-turn priority and flinch utility, Ice Punch or Heavy Slam can cover common checks, and Swords Dance or Belly Drum can push its already huge Attack much higher when a matchup safely permits setup. Quark Drive strengthens its highest stat under Electric Terrain or through Booster Energy, usually Attack on conventional builds, but its base 68 Special Defense remains much weaker than its enormous physical bulk. Adamant maximizes its defining Attack, Careful can reinforce special durability, and Brave is useful when deliberately exploiting its low Speed in Trick Room.
competitive: Iron Hands is currently UUBL in SV singles: it is legal in OU but does not have enough usage to be OU by usage and is considered too strong for UU.
